<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:cocycle} 
                                                                                                 
An object of $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ determines a self-adjoint, Clifford linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on a real vector bundle $V\to M$ (not necessarily finite-rank). The families index construction for self-adjoint superconnections determines a cocycle map 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:cocycleK}
1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)\xrightarrow{{\rm Index}} \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)
\end{eqnarray}
     
                                             
                                             
                                     
                                  
                                                        
                                                   
                                       
                  
                                                                                                                                    
     
valued in the differential ${\rm KO}$-theory of $M$. If the renormalization group flow sends an object $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ to the zero theory, then its underlying class in ${\rm KO}^n(M)$ is zero.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:index}
The Bismut superconnection of a family of Riemannian spin manifolds $X\to M$ determines an object $\alpha(X)\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^{-n}(M)$ whose image under~\eqref{eq:cocycleK} is the families differential analytic index of $X\to M$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:mainA}
There is a functor 
$$
{\rm Rep}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\to {\sf Vect}^{{\mathbb{A}}}(M)
$$
from (not necessarily finite-rank) representations of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ to the groupoid of (not necessarily finite-rank) super vector bundles with superconnection on~$M$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:dataofeft}
There is an equivalence of categories
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:dataofeft}
{\rm sPar}\colon {\sf Vect}^{{\mathbb{A}}}_{\rm ind}(M) \xrightarrow{\sim} 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^0(M)
\end{eqnarray}
from the category of real, self-adjoint superconnections admitting smooth index bundles to the category~$1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^0(M)$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- rmk-1: body_md -->
\label{rmk:SParinfinite}
Dumitrescu's super parallel transport~\cite{florin} extends~\eqref{eq:dataofeft} to a functor
$$
{\sf Vect}^{\mathbb{A}}_{{\rm fin}}(M)\to 1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^0(M),
$$ 
from superconnection on finite-rank super vector bundles; compare Corollary~\ref{prop:florin1}. An infinite-rank generalization of super parallel transport would provide a complete dictionary between $1|1$-Euclidean field theories and superconnections.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
However, in our present analytical setting (following~\cite{ST11})) super parallel transport for infinite rank bundles need not be defined owing to the failure of existence and uniqueness results for differential equations in topological vector spaces, e.g., see \cite[Example~5.6.1]{Hamilton} for counterexamples in Fr\'echet spaces. From the physics point of view, one expects field theories to be determined by infinitesimal data. 
                                                                                  
                                                                                                                
We note that some of the prior definitions of $1|1$-Euclidean field theory leverage existence and uniqueness results in Hilbert spaces~\cite[\S6]{HST}. In a different direction, there are existence and uniqueness results for tame Fr\'echet spaces and tame maps. Adopting a more Wilsonian approach, one could define $1|1$-Euclidean field theories as an ${\rm Ind}$-completion of finite-rank objects with compatibilities via the energy filtration; this also forces existence and uniqueness. When attempting to weigh these options, the main concern is that the correct analytical context for the $d=2$ case in conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture} is not yet clear. As such, we leave these choices of analysis flexible to avoid over-constraining the possible definitions in this $d=2$ generalization.
<!-- end rmk-1 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{defn:ogFT} For $n\in {\mathbb{Z}}$ the \emph{degree~$n$ twist} is a $\otimes$-invertible functor 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:maintwist}
 \mathscr{T}^n\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}({\rm pt})\to {\sf {Alg}}
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\sf {Alg}}$ is a Morita category of (topological) algebras, bimodules, and bimodule maps. Pulling back along the canonical functor $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}({\rm pt})$ we obtain a twist for the $1|1$-Euclidean bordism category over $M$ that we will also denote by $\mathscr{T}^n$. 
                                                                                                                               
A \emph{degree~$n$ field theory over $M$} is a natural transformation
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$};
\node (B) at (5,0) {${\sf {Alg}}.$};
\node (C) at (2.5,0) {$E \Downarrow$};
\draw[->,bend left=15] (A) to node [above] {$\mathbbold{1}$} (B);
\draw[->,bend right=15] (A) to node [below] {$\mathscr{T}^n$} (B);
\path (0,0) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:twistedEFT}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- rmk-2: body_md -->
Some details of the above definition have not appeared in the literature; we refer to \S\ref{sec:degreendefns} for further discussion that culminates in Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}.
<!-- end rmk-2 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{defn:STfieldtheories} Define a category $1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)$ whose objects are real, reflection positive degree~$n$ field theories~\eqref{eq:twistedEFT}. Morphisms in $1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)$ are isomorphisms between internal natural transformations $E\simeq E'$ that are compatible with the real and reflection positive structures.
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- rmk-3: body_md -->
\label{rmk:KTate}
Reflection positivity is perhaps unnecessary in the $d=1$ version of conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture}: unoriented, real field theories (with a different positivity condition) recover KO-theory~\cite{HST}, see Remark~\ref{rmk:RPFT}. However, unoriented and real structures do not generalize to the $2|1$-dimensional Euclidean bordism category, and the Miller character ${\rm TMF}\to {\rm KO}(\!(q)\!)$ necessitates a map from $2|1$-Euclidean field theories to real K-theory if conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture} is to hold. Reflection positivity is one way to obtain real structures on Hilbert spaces of states in dimension~$2|1$; see~\cite[3.2.2]{GPPV} and~\cite{DBEtorsion}.
<!-- end rmk-3 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop1}\label{prop:geodata}
The restriction of a degree~$n$ Euclidean field theory~\eqref{eq:twistedEFT} along the functor~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines:
\begin{enumerate}
\item vector bundles $V_+,V_-\to M$ with fiberwise ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{+n}$- and ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}$-actions and Clifford linear superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_+$ and ${\mathbb{A}}_-$, respectively (Proposition~\ref{prop:superconn});
\item a pairing between section-valued differential forms (Proposition~\ref{eq:proppairing})
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:mainhermitian}
&&\langle-,-\rangle\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{n}\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} \Big(\Omega^\bullet(M;V_-)\otimes \Omega^\bullet(M;V_+)\Big)\to \Omega^\bullet(M)
\end{eqnarray}
for which the superconnections satisfy $\langle {\mathbb{A}}_-x,y\rangle=(-1)^{|x|}\langle x,{\mathbb{A}}_+y\rangle$; 
\item differential forms $Z,Z_\ell\in \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}))$ satisfying 
$$
dZ=0, \ \ \partial_\ell Z=dZ_\ell, \qquad {\rm deg}(Z)=n \mod 2,\ \ {\rm deg}(Z_\ell)=n-1\mod 2
$$
where $\ell$ is the standard coordinate on ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:trace}).
\end{enumerate}
The renormalization group flow on degree~$n$ field theories induces the Getzler rescaling of superconnections (Proposition~\ref{prop:Getzler}): renormalization flow by $\mu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ restricts to
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\mathbb{A}}_\pm\mapsto \mu ({\mathbb{A}}_\pm)_0+({\mathbb{A}}_\pm)_1+\mu^{-1}({\mathbb{A}}_\pm)_2+\mu^{-2}({\mathbb{A}}_\pm)_3 + \dots\label{eq:RGsconn}
\end{eqnarray}
Reflection and real structures restrict along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} as follows. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item A reflection structure determines isomorphisms $V_\pm \simeq \overline{V}_\mp$ of bundles of Clifford modules relative to the $*$-superalgebra structure ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n} \to \overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\mp n}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:superstarCl}. Using this data, the pairing~\eqref{eq:mainhermitian} determines graded hermitian pairings on~$V_+$ and~$V_-$ for which the superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_+$ and ${\mathbb{A}}_-$ are graded self-adjoint. The positivity condition requires the hermitian pairing to be positive (Proposition~\ref{prop:selfadjoint}).
\item A real structure determines isomorphisms $V_\pm\simeq \overline{V}_\pm$ of bundles of modules relative to the standard real structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$. The superconnections are compatible with this real structure on~$V_\pm$. For a reflection positive theory with real structure, the hermitian inner product is also real (Proposition~\ref{prop:realA}). 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
\label{defn:effective1}\label{defn:effective}
The groupoid $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ has objects degree~$n$ representations of~${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ (Definition~\ref{defn:degreensP}) that are reflection positive (Definition~\ref{defn:rssP}), trace class (Definition~\ref{defn:tracestru}), real (Definition~\ref{defn:rrsP}), and admit cutoffs (Definition~\ref{def:hypothesis}). Morphisms are isomorphisms between degree~$n$ representations of~${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ that are compatible with the reflection structure, real structure, and trace.
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:STcocycle}
Theorem~\ref{thm:cocycle} constructs a cocycle map for a subcategory of Stolz and Teichner's degree~$n$ theories,
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
&&\{E\in 1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)\mid E \ {\rm admits\ energy\ cutoffs}\}\xrightarrow{{\rm cocycle}} \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The definition of $2|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ is set up so that an object $E\in 1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)$ determines the \emph{data} of an object in $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ by restriction to specific families of super Euclidean bordisms; it remains to check that these data satisfy the required properties. The positivity property for an object in $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ follows from reflection positivity for $1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)$. Field theories satisfying the cutoff property provide a subcategory of field theories, and we have a span
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:STcomparison}
&&1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)\hookleftarrow \{E\in 1|1 \hbox{-{\sf EFT}}^n(M)\mid E \ {\rm admits\ energy\ cutoffs}\}\xrightarrow{{\rm restrict}} 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M). 
\end{eqnarray}
Postcomposing the map on the right with~\eqref{eq:cocycleK} provides the claimed map to $\widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- rmk-4: body_md -->
\label{rmk:generalcocycle}
One can formulate the span~\eqref{eq:STcomparison} for any definition of degree~$n$, $1|1$-Euclidean field theories defined using a bordism category that contains the families of small bordisms (see Definition~\ref{defn:smallbordisms}) where the degree twist satisfies Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}. Hence, such field theories admit a subcategory with a cocycle map valued in $\widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)$ by composing with~\eqref{eq:cocycleK}. For finite-rank examples, the cutoff condition is automatically satisfied, see Corollary~\ref{prop:florin1} which follows from~\cite[\S9.1]{BGV}. Hence, the cutoff condition in~\eqref{eq:STcomparison} is only interesting for infinite-rank examples.
<!-- end rmk-4 -->
<!-- rmk-5: body_md -->
\label{rmk:elliptic}
Cutoffs make sense for a broad class of field theories. Indeed, in Witten's study of the $\mathcal{N}=(0,1)$ supersymmetric sigma model~\cite[\S1]{Witten_Dirac}, he suggested that cutoffs be used to analyze the field theories in the $d=2$ version of the conjectures~\eqref{eq:conjecture}. 
                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                             
For $1|1$-dimensional field theories, the property of having smooth energy cutoffs is analogous to the property of a differential operator being elliptic; in particular, cutoffs require eigenfunctions of the degree zero part of ${\mathbb{A}}^2$ to determine smooth sections over~$M$.
<!-- end rmk-5 -->
<!-- rmk-6: body_md -->
\label{rmk:smallfieldtheory}
Assuming a generators and relations description of the category $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ (following \cite[6.7]{HST} and \cite[3.2]{ST11}), the data of an object of $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ is the data of a degree~$n$ field theory defined on a subcategory of \emph{small bordisms in $M$}
$$
1|1\hbox{-{\sf ebord}}(M)\hookrightarrow 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)
$$
generated by the $S$-families of bordisms in Definition~\ref{defn:smallbordisms}.
<!-- end rmk-6 -->
<!-- rmk-7: body_md -->
\label{rmk:concordance}
By results of Hopkins--Hovey~\cite{HopkinsHovey}, Theorems~\ref{thm:cocycle}  and~\ref{thm:index} yield a surjection 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:KOsurjection}
1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)\twoheadrightarrow {\rm KO}^n(M),
\end{eqnarray} 
verifying a version of the $d=1$ case of~\eqref{eq:conjecture}.
A stronger form of the conjectures~\eqref{eq:conjecture} asserts that the map~\eqref{eq:KOsurjection} induces an isomorphism on concordance classes, so that the corresponding cohomology theories are a complete invariant of field theories~\cite[\S1.5]{ST11}. It is easy to see that~\eqref{eq:KOsurjection} factors through concordance classes, but we do not expect an isomorphism in our framework used below for reasons we explain presently. 
                                                                                                                                                   
In view of the factorization~\eqref{eq:FTtosConn} of the cocycle map, the stronger form of conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture} in particular requires a category of superconnections whose concordance classes are KO-theory. But in existing definitions the isomorphism class of the underlying vector bundle is a concordance invariant. In particular, the rank of a vector bundle is a concordance invariant, but is not an invariant of the underlying ${\rm KO}$-class. We see two possible ways to avoid this problem. The first option is to define field theories on (infinite rank) Hilbert bundles, using that such bundles are always trivializable~\cite{Kuiper}; this resonates with previous definitions from \cite{ST04} and \cite{HST}, and likely makes contact with Lott and Gorokhovsky's model for differential K-theory~\cite{LottGorokhovsky}. The second option follows the suggestion in~\cite[Remark~3.16]{ST11}, and requires a framework for superconnections defined on (not necessarily locally free) sheaves of topological vector spaces, e.g., see~\cite{PeterU} for finite-rank results in this direction. It is not clear if either of these approaches generalize to the desired statement in dimension~$2|1$.
<!-- end rmk-7 -->
<!-- rmk-8: body_md -->
Often one takes the Hilbert completion of the Fr\'echet space $\mathcal{H}=C^\infty(X;{\mathbb{C}})$, resulting in a Hilbert space of states and an unbounded Hamiltonian $H=\Delta$. For the definition of field theory from~\cite{ST11} the domain of the operator $\Delta$ (as a Fr\'echet space) turns out to be more fundamental. By contrast, the Hilbert completion is the basic object of study for definitions of field theories in~\cite{ST04} and \cite{HST}. 
                                                                                                                                                                              
It is unclear which point of view generalizes more readily to the $d=2$ conjecture in~\eqref{eq:conjecture}. In this paper we will largely follow~\cite{ST11}, though we will ignore these functional analytic distinctions for the remainder of this section.
<!-- end rmk-8 -->
<!-- rmk-9: body_md -->
\label{rmk:collars} We comment briefly on an important technical detail ignored above. Various quantities in a 1-dimensional Euclidean field theory ought to depend smoothly on geometric parameters, e.g., the semigroup $t\mapsto E({\sf I}_t^+)$ and the partition function $Z=E({\sf S}_t)$ should depend smoothly on~$t$. In Stolz and Teichner's formalism~\cite{HST,ST11} this is addressed by defining field theories as fibered functors, assigning smoothly varying quantities to smoothly varying families of bordisms;
                                                                                                                                                            
see~\S\ref{sec:ebord} below.
<!-- end rmk-9 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
Define the super Lie group ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ with multiplication 
\begin{eqnarray}
(t,\theta)\cdot (s,\eta)=(t+s+\theta\eta,\theta+\eta)\qquad (t,\theta),(s,\eta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S), \label{eq:superEuc}
\end{eqnarray}
where the above formula is understood in terms of the functor of points of~${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- rmk-10: body_md -->
\label{rmk:SUSYmorse}
A closely related (and perhaps better known) example of supersymmetric quantum mechanics takes as its space of states~$\mathcal{H}=\Omega^\bullet(X)$, differential forms on an oriented Riemannian manifold~\cite[\S2]{susymorse}. The Hamiltonian is then defined to be the Hodge Laplacian $H=dd^*+d^*d$, which has a pair of commuting odd square roots, 
\begin{eqnarray}
Q_1=d+d^*, \quad Q_2=i(d-d^*), \quad [Q_1,Q_2]=0, \quad Q_1^2=Q_2^2=H.\label{eq:Nis2}
\end{eqnarray}
This is the data of $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry, rather than the $\mathcal{N}=1$ example above. With our intended connections to index theory, $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry is more fundamental. Of course, forgetting one of the $Q_i$ in~\eqref{eq:Nis2} extracts an $\mathcal{N}=1$ theory.
<!-- end rmk-10 -->
<!-- rmk-11: body_md -->
Restricting~\eqref{eq:N1super} along the homomorphism ${\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$ of semigroups forgets the supersymmetry, extracting an ordinary quantum mechanical theory. Similarly, any $1|1$-dimensional Euclidean field theory determines a 1-dimensional Euclidean field theory; see~\cite[Equation~4.14]{ST11}.
<!-- end rmk-11 -->
<!-- rmk-12: body_md -->
Supersymmetric quantum mechanics can be understood entirely from the vantage of super Lie algebra representations~\eqref{eq:Lie11} or super semigroup representations~\eqref{eq:N1super}. Our primary motivation for pursuing a description in terms of the $1|1$-Euclidean bordism category is that there is an evident $2|1$-Euclidean generalization, illuminating a candidate definition for $2|1$-Euclidean field theory in the conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture}.
<!-- end rmk-12 -->
<!-- rmk-13: body_md -->
One could equally equip $\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}$ with the restricted Hamiltonian $H|_{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}}$ when defining the cutoff theory. 
For our purposes, it turns out to be more convenient for the cutoff theory to be RG-invariant.
<!-- end rmk-13 -->
<!-- ex-1: body_md -->
For the theory with $Q=\slashed{D}$ the Dirac operator on an even dimensional spin manifold, the Witten index agrees with the analytic index ${\rm Ind}(\slashed{D})=[\mathcal{H}_0]\in {\rm K}^0({\rm pt})$ of the Dirac operator. In the example discussed in Remark~\ref{rmk:SUSYmorse}, the Witten index is the Euler characteristic of~$X$.
<!-- end ex-1 -->
<!-- rmk-14: body_md -->
We note that the McKean--Singer formula~\eqref{eq:partition function2} equates the Witten index and the partition function as elements of~${\mathbb{Z}}$. In families, this identification is modified: the partition function is a differential form which agrees with the Chern character of the Witten index.
<!-- end rmk-14 -->
<!-- rmk-15: body_md -->
For an inner product space $W$, the Clifford algebra ${\rm Cl}(W)$ can be understood as the quantization of a free (fermionic) particle moving in the odd vector space $\Pi W$, e.g., see~\cite[page~19]{Freed5}. Free fermions in higher dimensions illuminate a path towards a general framework for degree~$n$ field theories. In particular, this suggests a $2|1$-dimensional generalization for the second conjecture in~\eqref{eq:conjecture}.
<!-- end rmk-15 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A \emph{positively oriented Euclidean path} in~$M$ is a triple $(\phi,t_{\rm in},t_{\rm out})$ for a smooth map $\phi\colon {\mathbb{A}}^1\to M$ and points~$t_{\rm in},t_{\rm out}\in {\mathbb{A}}^1$ with $t_{\rm out}-t_{\rm in}\in {\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}$. Similarly, a \emph{negatively oriented Euclidean path} in $M$ is a triple $(\phi,t_{\rm in},t_{\rm out})$ with $t_{\rm out}-t_{\rm in}\in {\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}$. A \emph{Euclidean path} is a positively or negatively oriented Euclidean path. The point~$\phi(t_{\rm in}) \in M$ is the \emph{incoming} boundary and~$\phi(t_{\rm out})\in M$ is the \emph{outgoing} boundary of a Euclidean path. 
                                                                                                       
An \emph{isometry} $(\phi,t_{\rm in},t_{\rm out})\stackrel{\sim}{\to} (\phi',t_{\rm in}',t_{\rm out}')$ between a pair of Euclidean paths is the data of $s \in {\mathbb{R}}$ such that $\phi'=\phi\circ T_s^{-1}$, $T_s(t_{\rm in})=t_{\rm in}'$, and $T_s(t_{\rm out})=t_{\rm out}'$.
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
\label{defn:Path} Define the (Lie) \emph{category of constant paths in $M$}, denoted ${\sf Path}_0(M)$, as having objects and morphisms the smooth manifolds
$$
{\rm Ob}({\sf Path}_0(M))=M\coprod M,\qquad {\rm Mor}({\sf Path}_0(M)) ={\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}\times M\coprod {\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}\times M.
$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
The source and target maps in ${\sf Path}_0(M)$ are given by the projections.
                                                                                                                                                           
 The unit map is determined by inclusion at $0\in {\mathbb{R}}$, and composition is determined by addition in ${\mathbb{R}}$.
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
\label{ex:modelgeo} Form the semidirect product ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ where ${\mathbb{Z}}/2=\{\pm1\}$ acts on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ by $(t,\theta)\mapsto (t,\pm \theta)$. The 
\emph{$1|1$-Euclidean geometry} is specified by the triple
$$
(G,{\mathbb{M}},{\mathbb{M}}^c)=({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2,{\mathbb{A}}^{1|1},{\mathbb{A}}^{0|1})
$$ 
for the evident action of ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ on ${\mathbb{A}}^{1|1}$ and the inclusion ${\mathbb{A}}^{0|1}\subset {\mathbb{A}}^{1|1}$ described above.
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- ex-2: body_md -->
\label{ex:Eucpair}
Our main example of an $S$-family of $1|1$-Euclidean pairs depends on $(t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S)$ and is given by 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:Eucpairmain}
Y^c=S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{t,\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}=Y
\end{eqnarray}
where
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:itthetadef}
i_{t,\theta}\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\subset S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{T_{t,\theta}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}
\end{eqnarray}
using the standard inclusion and the super translation map $T_{t,\theta}$ defined as the composition
\begin{eqnarray}
&&S \times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{{{\rm id}}_S\times (t,\theta)\times {{\rm id}}_{{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{{{\rm id}}_S\times{\rm act}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},\label{eq;translation}
\end{eqnarray}
where the second arrow is the action of ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ on itself. For any $(t,\theta)$ and $(s,\eta)$ the associated $1|1$-Euclidean pairs are isomorphic via the isometry
$$
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{T_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)^{-1}}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}.
$$
In particular, all pairs~\eqref{eq:Eucpairmain} are isomorphic to the standard one $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\subset S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end ex-2 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
\label{defn:orientationbord}\emph{Orientation reversal} is the automorphism of the $1|1$-Euclidean geometry determined by the homomorphism
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                         
{\sf or} \colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},&&\qquad (t,\theta)\mapsto (-t,-i\theta),\qquad (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).\label{eq:supertimereverse}
\end{eqnarray}
We observe that when restricted to ${\mathbb{R}}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$~\eqref{eq:supertimereverse} is the standard orientation reversing map~\eqref{Eq:easyorr} on ${\mathbb{R}}$.
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- rmk-16: body_md -->
The map~\eqref{eq:supertimereverse} is called the \emph{pin generator} in~\cite[Example 6.16]{HST}.
<!-- end rmk-16 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{defn:rg}For $\mu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$, the \emph{renormalization group action} is the automorphism of the $1|1$-Euclidean geometry determined by the homomorphism 
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                         
{\sf rg}_\mu \colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},&&\qquad (t,\theta)\mapsto (\mu^2t,\mu\theta),\qquad (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).\label{eq:superRG}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- defn-10: body_md -->
\label{defn:spinflip}The \emph{spin flip} is the automorphism of the $1|1$-Euclidean geometry determined by the action of $-1\in \{\pm 1\}\simeq {\mathbb{Z}}/2<{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf fl}\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},\qquad (t,\theta)\mapsto (t,-\theta),\qquad (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).\label{eq:spinflipfor11}
\end{eqnarray}
Since ${\mathbb{Z}}/2<{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ is in the center, the spin flip commutes with the action of the isometry group.
<!-- end defn-10 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{rmk:real2}
The super Lie group ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ has a real structure
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:real11}
{\sf r}\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{\sim}  \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}^{1|1},\qquad \overline{{\sf r}} \circ {\sf r}={{\rm id}}_{{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}}.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Following Example~\ref{ex:real}, first choose an identification ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\simeq \Pi (\underline{{\mathbb{R}}}_ {\mathbb{C}})$ where $\underline{{\mathbb{R}}}$ is the trivial real line bundle on~${\mathbb{R}}$ and $\underline{{\mathbb{R}}}_ {\mathbb{C}}$ is its complexification. This endows the supermanifold underlying ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ with a real structure. To promote this to a real structure on the super Lie group, let $\theta\in C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})^{\rm odd}\simeq \Gamma({\mathbb{R}},\Lambda^1 (\underline{{\mathbb{R}}}_{\mathbb{C}}))$ denote the function associated with a (real) trivialization of $\underline{{\mathbb{R}}}$. With this choice, the group multiplication~\eqref{eq:superEuc} is real.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- defn-11: body_md -->
\label{defn:realbordisms}Define a real structure on the $1|1$-dimensional super Euclidean model geometry from the real structure on the super Lie group ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ from Lemma~\ref{rmk:real2}, using that ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$ preserves this real structure on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end defn-11 -->
<!-- ex-3: body_md -->
\label{ex:functorsuperpair}\label{ex:realstructureonSP}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:GMaddstructure1}, the maps \eqref{eq:supertimereverse}, \eqref{eq:superRG} and \eqref{eq:spinflipfor11} determine endofunctors of the stack of $1|1$-Euclidean manifolds,
$$
{\sf Or},{\sf RG}_\mu,{\sf Fl}\colon ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2,{\mathbb{A}}^{1|1})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld}\to ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2,{\mathbb{A}}^{1|1})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld},
$$
that send an $S$-family of $1|1$-Euclidean manifolds to another $S$-family. Applied to the super Euclidean pair~\eqref{eq:Eucpairmain}, we find
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Or}(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{t,\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})&=&(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{-t,-i\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})\nonumber\\
{\sf RG}_\mu(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{t,\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})&=&(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{\mu^2t,\mu\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})\nonumber\\
{\sf Fl}(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{t,\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})&=&(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{t,-\theta}}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
Similarly, the map~\eqref{eq:real11} determines a map of stacks 
$$
{\sf R}\colon ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2,{\mathbb{A}}^{1|1})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld}\to ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2,{\mathbb{A}}^{1|1})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld},\quad (Y^c,Y)\mapsto (\overline{Y}{}^c,\overline{Y})
$$
covering complex conjugation of supermanifolds, that sends an $S$-family of $1|1$-Euclidean manifolds to an $\overline{S}$-family. There are natural isomorphisms of functors
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:Orrelation}
{\sf Or}^2\simeq {\sf Fl},\quad {\sf RG}_\mu\circ {\sf RG}_{\mu'}\simeq {\sf RG}_{\mu\mu'}, \quad {\sf R} \circ {\sf Or}\simeq \overline{{\sf Fl}}\circ \overline{{\sf Or}} \circ {\sf R}, \quad \overline{{\sf R}}\circ {\sf R}\simeq {{\rm id}}
\end{eqnarray}
coming from the equalities of maps
$$
{\sf or}^2={\sf fl}, \quad {\sf rg}_\mu\circ {\sf rg}_{\mu'}={\sf rg}_{\mu\mu'}, \quad \overline{{\sf or}}\circ {\sf r}=\overline{{\sf fl}}\circ {\sf r}\circ {\sf or}, \quad \overline{{\sf r}} \circ {\sf r}={{\rm id}}_{{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}}. 
$$
<!-- end ex-3 -->
<!-- defn-12: body_md -->
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $S$ a supermanifold. An $S$-family of \emph{positively oriented super Euclidean paths} in~$M$ is a triple $(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))$ determining a diagram~\eqref{diag:atriple} with the property 
\begin{eqnarray}
                  
\nonumber
 (t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out})\cdot (t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in})^{-1} \in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}(S)\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).
\end{eqnarray}
                                                        
Similarly, an $S$-family of \emph{negatively oriented super Euclidean paths} in~$M$ is a triple where 
\begin{eqnarray}
                  
\nonumber
 (t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out})\cdot (t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in})^{-1} \in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}(S)\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).
\end{eqnarray}
An $S$-family of \emph{super Euclidean paths} in~$M$ is a triple $(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))$ that over each component of $S$ is a family of positively or negatively oriented superpaths. The \emph{incoming} and \emph{outgoing} boundaries of $(\phi,(t,\theta),(s,\eta))$ are the compositions 
$$
\phi_{\rm out} \colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out})}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{\phi} M,\quad \phi_{\rm in} \colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xhookrightarrow{i_{(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in})}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{\phi} M.
$$
An \emph{isometry} $(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))\stackrel{\sim}{\to}(\phi',(t_{\rm out}',\theta_{\rm out}'),(t_{\rm in}',\theta_{\rm in}'))$ between a pair of $S$-families of superpaths is the data of $(s,\eta) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S)$ such that 
$$
\phi'=\phi\circ T_{s,\eta}, \quad  T_{s,\eta}\circ \phi_{\rm in}=\phi_{\rm in}', \quad T_{s,\eta}\circ \phi_{\rm out}=\phi_{\rm out}'
$$
where $T_{s,\eta}$ is the super translation by $(s,\eta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S)$ defined in~\eqref{eq;translation}.
<!-- end defn-12 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:bigsEpath}
The groupoid of super Euclidean paths over $S$ is equivalent to the discrete groupoid given by the value of the sheaf
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:bigsEpath}
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\coprod {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)
\end{eqnarray}
on the supermanifold $S$, and hence the stack of super Euclidean paths in $M$ is equivalent to the sheaf~\eqref{eq:bigsEpath}.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Given an $S$-family of positively (respectively, negatively) oriented super Euclidean paths $(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))$, there is a unique isomorphism to a superpath with $(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in})=(0,0)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S)$. With this identification fixed, the remaining data is
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M,\qquad (t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out})=(t,\theta) \in ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\coprod {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0})(S). \label{eq:protocat}
\end{eqnarray}
The result follows.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- defn-13: body_md -->
An $S$-family of \emph{nearly constant super Euclidean paths in $M$} is the data of a super Euclidean path $(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))$ for which $\phi$ is determined by a map $\phi_0$, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{q} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}/{\mathbb{R}}\simeq S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xrightarrow{\phi_0} M,\label{eq:constantsuper}
\end{eqnarray}
where the first arrow is the quotient of $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ by the ${\mathbb{R}}$-action on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end defn-13 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:st} The groupoid of $S$-families of nearly constant super Euclidean path in $M$ is equivalent to the discrete groupoid given by the value of the sheaf
                                                                                                                                                 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M),\label{eq:fdrepresentable}
\end{eqnarray}
on the supermanifold $S$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The follows the same argument as the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:bigsEpath}, but the map $\phi$ in~\eqref{eq:protocat} is required to be of the form~\eqref{eq:constantsuper} and hence determined by $\phi_0\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to M$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:concat} Suppose that $\gamma=(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))$ and $\gamma'=(\phi',(t_{\rm out}',\theta_{\rm out}'),(t_{\rm in}',\theta_{\rm in}'))$ are $S$-families of positively (respectively, negatively) oriented nearly constant superpaths in $M$ and that $\phi_{\rm out}=\phi_{\rm in}'\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to M$. Then there is a well-defined concatenation $\gamma*\gamma'$ as a positively (respectively, negatively) oriented nearly constant superpath in $M$ that is unique up to unique isomorphism.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
It suffices to work in the universal case~\eqref{eq:fdrepresentable}, for which the concatenation of positively oriented superpaths is given by
\begin{eqnarray}
&&({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\times_{{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)} ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\nonumber\\
&&\simeq {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M) \stackrel{m\times {{\rm id}}}{\longrightarrow} {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\label{eq:compose}
\end{eqnarray}
where $m$ is the restriction of multiplication on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$. The concatenation map in the negatively oriented case is completely analogous.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- defn-14: body_md -->
\label{defn:sP} The super Lie category of \emph{nearly constant superpaths in $M$}, denoted ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$, has objects and morphisms,
$$
{\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))={\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M),$$
$$
 {\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M)) ={\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}^{1|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M),
$$
where source, target, and unit data are given by the incoming and outgoing boundaries of a superpath and the identity superpath (using Lemma~\ref{lem:st}) while composition is the concatenation of superpaths from Lemma~\ref{lem:concat}.
<!-- end defn-14 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:action}
                                                                           
There is an essentially surjective and faithful (but not full) functor
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf sPath}_0(M)\hookrightarrow \left({\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\right)/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},\label{eq:itsafunctor}
\end{eqnarray}
to the quotient super Lie groupoid for the ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$-action factoring through the homomorphism ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$ (see~\eqref{eq:evaluationaction}), with the functor~\eqref{eq:itsafunctor} determined by the standard inclusions ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}, {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By definition, the source map on an $S$-point of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is
$$
(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))\mapsto \phi_{\rm in},\qquad \phi_{\rm in} \colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xhookrightarrow{i_0} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{\phi} M,
$$
with $\phi$ as in~\eqref{eq:constantsuper}. Since $q\circ i_0={{\rm id}}_{S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}}$, we find $\phi_{\rm in}=\phi_0$ in the notation of~\eqref{eq:constantsuper}. The source map is therefore the projection ${\sf s}=p\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\to {\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))$. The target map on an $S$-point of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:positive}
                                                                                              
(\phi,(t_{\rm out},\theta_{\rm out}),(t_{\rm in},\theta_{\rm in}))\mapsto \phi_{\rm out},\qquad \phi_{\rm out} \colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xhookrightarrow{T_{t,\theta}\circ i_0} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{\phi} M.
                                                             
\end{eqnarray}
                        
                                                                                              
                                                                                           
            
                                                 
     
                                                                                                               
Again using that  $q\circ i_0={{\rm id}}_{S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}}$, the target map is the restriction of the (left) action 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\rm act} \colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\label{eq:evaluationaction}
\end{eqnarray}
coming from the precomposition with the ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$-action on ${\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$, 
$$
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},\qquad (t,\theta)\cdot \eta=(\theta+\eta), \quad (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S), \ \eta\in {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}(S).
$$
The lemma is proved.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- rmk-17: body_md -->
Using~\eqref{eq:oddtangentiso}, functions on the quotient groupoid ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$ give a supergeometric interpretation of the de~Rham complex of~$M$, e.g., see~\cite[\S3]{HKST}. Lemma~\ref{lem:action} shows that the category of superpaths is closely related to this groupoid.
<!-- end rmk-17 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:stmap}
Using~\eqref{eq:oddtangentiso} and~\eqref{eq:oddtangentiso1}, the source and target maps ${\sf s},{\sf t}\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\rightrightarrows {\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))$ are determined by the super algebra maps
$$
\Omega^\bullet(M)\oplus \Omega^\bullet(M)\to \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}^{1|1}))\oplus \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}^{1|1}))
$$
$$
{\sf s}^*(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha,\beta),\qquad {\sf t}^*(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha-\theta d\alpha,\beta-\theta d\beta),\quad \alpha,\beta\in \Omega^\bullet(M),
$$
where we use the canonical inclusions 
$$
\Omega^\bullet(M)\hookrightarrow \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}^{1|1})),\qquad \Omega^\bullet(M)\hookrightarrow \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}^{1|1}))
$$ 
along the constant functions on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$ or ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}$
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Standard results (e.g.,~\cite[Lemma~3.8]{HKST}) compute the ${\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$-action on ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ in terms of a map on differential forms:
                                                      
                                                                                      
                    
                                                                                                                         
                                                                     
     
                                                                 
\begin{eqnarray}
\Omega^\bullet(M)\simeq C^\infty({\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))&\to& C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}))\nonumber\\
\alpha&\mapsto& \alpha-\theta  d\alpha,\quad \alpha\in \Omega^\bullet(M), \ C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1})\simeq C^\infty({\mathbb{R}})[\theta]\label{eq:actdeRham}
\end{eqnarray}
where $d$ is the de~Rham differential on $\Omega^\bullet(M)$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:action}, the source and target maps in ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ are therefore determined by restrictions of~\eqref{eq:actdeRham}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- rmk-18: body_md -->
The formula~\eqref{eq:actdeRham} differs from~\cite[Lemma~3.8]{HKST} by a sign; their formula is for the right action of ${\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$ on $\Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}$, whereas~\eqref{eq:actdeRham} is for the left action.
<!-- end rmk-18 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:structureonsP}
The maps \eqref{eq:supertimereverse}, \eqref{eq:superRG}, \eqref{eq:spinflipfor11} and~\eqref{eq:real11} determine smooth functors 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Or}\colon {\sf sPath}_0(M)\to {\sf sPath}_0(M),&& (t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (-t,-i\theta,\phi\circ {\sf or}^{-1}) \label{eq:formOr}\\ 
{\sf RG}\colon {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf sPath}_0(M)\to {\sf sPath}_0(M), && (\mu,t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (\mu^2 t,\mu\theta, \phi\circ {\sf rg}_\mu^{-1}) \label{eq:formRG}\\ 
{\sf Fl}\colon {\sf sPath}_0(M)\to {\sf sPath}_0(M),&& (t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (t,-\theta,\phi\circ {\sf fl}^{-1})\label{eq:formFl} \\ 
{\sf R} \colon {\sf sPath}_0(M)\to \overline{{\sf sPath}_0(M)}, && (t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (\overline{t},\overline{\theta},\overline{\phi}\circ {\sf r}) \label{eq:formRR}
\end{eqnarray}
given by the indicated maps on $S$-points of morphisms. Furthermore, there are equalities of smooth functors
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Eq:Orrelation}
{\sf Or}\circ {\sf Or}={\sf Fl},\qquad {\sf R} \circ {\sf Or}= \overline{{\sf Fl}}\circ \overline{{\sf Or}} \circ {\sf R}
\end{eqnarray}
and ${\sf RG}$ gives the structure of a strict ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$-action on ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ in the sense that the diagram of super Lie categories strictly commutes
\begin{eqnarray}
                  
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (B) at (6,0) {${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (D) at (6,-1.5) {${\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${{\rm id}}_{{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}}\times {\sf RG}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$m\times {{\rm id}}_{{\sf sPath}_0(M)}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf RG}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf RG}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:RGaction}
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ is regarded as a discrete super Lie category and $m\colon {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\to {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ is multiplication.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The formulas~\eqref{eq:formOr}-\eqref{eq:formFl} follow from Example~\ref{ex:functorsuperpair}. The equalities~\eqref{Eq:Orrelation} and commutativity~\eqref{eq:RGaction} follow from~\eqref{eq:Orrelation}. The real structure~\eqref{eq:formRR} is inherited from the real structure on $1|1$-Euclidean supermanifolds in Example~\ref{ex:realstructureonSP}, together with the canonical real structure on $M$, giving the $\bar{S}$-point of ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$
$$
\overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{{{\rm id}}_{\overline{S}}\times {\sf r}} \overline{S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}}\xrightarrow{\overline{\phi}} \overline{M}\simeq M
$$
determined by the image of $\phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to M$ under the conjugation functor on supermanifolds.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
The functors~\eqref{eq:formOr}-\eqref{eq:formFl} are determined by the maps on morphisms induced by the super algebra maps
$$
\Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}))\oplus \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}))\to \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}))\oplus \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}))
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Or}^*(\alpha(t,\theta),\beta(t,\theta))&=&(i^{|\beta|}\beta(-t,-i\theta),i^{|\alpha|}\alpha(-t,-i\theta)), \quad i=\sqrt{-1}\\
{\sf RG}_\mu^*(\alpha(t,\theta),\beta(t,\theta))&=&(\mu^{|\alpha|}\alpha(\mu^2t,\mu\theta),\mu^{|\beta|}\beta(\mu^2t,\mu\theta)\label{eq:RGonsP}\\
{\sf Fl}^*(\alpha(t,\theta),\beta(t,\theta))&=&((-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha(t,-\theta),(-1)^{|\beta|}\beta(t,-\theta))
\end{eqnarray}
for $\alpha,\beta\in \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}))$, where $|\alpha|,|\beta|\in {\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the ${\mathbb{Z}}$-grading of $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
This follows from~\eqref{eq:formOr}-\eqref{eq:formFl} and standard results (e.g.,~\cite[Lemma~3.8]{HKST}) that compute the ${\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{C}}^\times$-action on ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$. The above statements follow by specializing to the subgroups ${\mathbb{Z}}/4$, ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ and ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$ of ${\mathbb{C}}^\times$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- defn-15: body_md -->
\label{defn:supercircle}
Given an $S$-point $(\ell,\lambda)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}(S)$, define the family of $1|1$-dimensional \emph{super Euclidean circles} as the quotient
\begin{eqnarray}
S^{1|1}_{\ell,\lambda}:=(S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})/{\mathbb{Z}}\label{eq:supercircle}
\end{eqnarray}
for the left ${\mathbb{Z}}$-action on $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ given by
            
     
                                                                                                                                            
     
                                                                                                                                                                               
   
                                                                                                                                                
   
                                                      
\begin{eqnarray}
n\cdot (t,\theta)= (t+n\ell+n\lambda\theta,n\lambda+\theta),\quad n\in {\mathbb{Z}}(S), (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S).\label{eq:Zact}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-15 -->
<!-- rmk-19: body_md -->
The $S$-family of subgroups $S\times {\mathbb{Z}}\hookrightarrow S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ generated by $(\ell,\lambda)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}(S)$ is normal if and only if $\lambda=0$. Hence, the standard super circle $S^{1|1}={\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}/{\mathbb{Z}}$ inherits a group structure from ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, but a generic $S$-family of super Euclidean circles $S^{1|1}_{\ell,\lambda}$ does not.
<!-- end rmk-19 -->
<!-- defn-16: body_md -->
\label{defn:sEucloop} Define the \emph{super Euclidean loop space} as the generalized supermanifold (see Example~\ref{ex:mappingsheaf})
$$
\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M):={\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}(S^{1|1},M).
$$
<!-- end defn-16 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:spanofinclude}
There is a span of inclusions
$$
{\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\hookleftarrow {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\mathbb{R}}_{<0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{L}_0^{1|1}(M)
$$
that views a constant superpath with the same source and target and nonzero super length as a constant super loop.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- defn-17: body_md -->
\label{defn:11EB}
Let $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ denote the geometric bordism category associated with the super Euclidean geometry from Example~\ref{ex:modelgeo}. We call $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ the \emph{$1|1$-Euclidean bordism category over $M$}.
<!-- end defn-17 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:extrastrEB}
The internal category $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ admits internal endofunctors:
\begin{enumerate}
\item orientation reversal, ${\sf Or}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$,
\item the renormalization group action, ${\sf RG}_\mu\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$, and
\item a real structure, ${\sf R}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$,
\end{enumerate}
                                                              
where ${\sf Or}$, and ${\sf RG}_\mu$ are maps of categories internal to symmetric monoidal stacks with involution, whereas the functor ${\sf R}$ is an internal functor that covers complex conjugation on supermanifolds.
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
From Definition~\ref{defn:orientationbord} and Example~\ref{ex:orientationGM}, we obtain an orientation reversal functor
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\sf Or}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M).\label{eq:timereversal11EB}
                                            
\end{eqnarray}
Using Definition~\ref{defn:rg} and Example~\ref{ex:RGgeneral}, we obtain an internal functor
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\sf RG}_\mu\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M).\label{eq:RG11EB}
                                            
\end{eqnarray}
Finally, Definition~\ref{defn:realbordisms} determines an internal functor (see Example~\ref{ex:realGM}) 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\sf R}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M) \label{eq:realstru11EB}
\end{eqnarray}
whose values are given by
$$
(S\leftarrow Y\to M)\stackrel{{\sf R}_0}{\mapsto} (\overline{S}\leftarrow \overline{Y}\to \overline{M}\simeq M) \qquad (S\leftarrow \Sigma\to M)\stackrel{{\sf R}_1}{\mapsto} (\overline{S} \leftarrow \overline{\Sigma}\to \overline{M}\simeq M)
$$ 
where $\overline{Y}\to \overline{S}$ and $\overline{\Sigma}\to \overline{S}$ have the canonical structure of an $\overline{S}$-family of super Euclidean manifolds. We emphasize that the family parameter changes under the functor ${\sf R}$ to the conjugate supermanifold.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- defn-18: body_md -->
\label{defn:11EBspt}
Define maps of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:sptM}
{\rm spt}^+_M,{\rm spt}^-_M\colon {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))
\end{eqnarray}
as follows. Given an $S$-point $\phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ of the source, define objects $({\rm spt}^+,\phi),({\rm spt}^-,\phi)$ in the groupoid ${\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))(S)$ by
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:collardataI}
\begin{array}{c}
Y^c=S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \subset S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}=Y\stackrel{\phi}{\to} M,\label{eq:stdinclude} \\
Y\setminus Y^c \simeq S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{<0} =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} Y^+\coprod Y^- & ({\rm spt}^+,\phi) \\ Y^-\coprod Y^+ & ({\rm spt}^-,\phi)\end{array}\right.
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
where $Y^c \hookrightarrow Y$ (the inclusion of the \emph{core}) is determined by the standard inclusion $0\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\hookrightarrow {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$. As indicated in the second line, the $+$ or $-$ decoration on ${\rm spt}^\pm_M$ reflects the choice of the partition of the collar. By pulling back families, the above is natural in~$S$ and hence leads to the claimed maps~\eqref{eq:sptM}.
<!-- end defn-18 -->
<!-- rmk-20: body_md -->
\label{rmk:germs1}
A pair of $S$-points of ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ determine isomorphic objects under ${\rm spt}^\pm_M$ if the the maps $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ agree on a half-open neighborhood of the core $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\hookrightarrow 
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$; see Definition~\ref{defn:GBord}. Hence, the map of stacks~\eqref{eq:sptM} factors through the quotient of ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ that parameterizes half-open germs of superpaths in~$M$.
<!-- end rmk-20 -->
<!-- defn-19: body_md -->
\label{defn:11EBspath}
Define maps of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:IM}
\begin{array}{c} {\sf I}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\sf I}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
as follows. Given $\Phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ and $(t,\theta)\colon S\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, consider
\begin{eqnarray}
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xrightarrow{i_0 \coprod i_{t,\theta}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}=\Sigma \xrightarrow{\Phi} M,\label{eq:morphism11}
\end{eqnarray}
     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
     
using the notation from~\eqref{eq:itthetadef}.
To promote~\eqref{eq:morphism11} to an object in the groupoid ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))(S)$, we require a choice of source and target data. Take
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:morphisms11EB}
&&
(Y_{{\rm in}}^c, Y_{{\rm out}}^c)=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \Big(({\rm spt}^+,\Phi), ({\rm spt}^+,\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1})\Big) &\implies (I_{t,\theta}^+,\Phi), & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}(S)\\ 
\Big(({\rm spt}^-,\Phi), ({\rm spt}^-,\phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1})\Big) &\implies (I_{t,\theta}^-,\Phi) & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}(S) \end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
i.e., the ordering in the coproduct in~\eqref{eq:morphism11} lists the source followed by the target $1|1$-Euclidean pair. The resulting options and the restriction on $(t,\theta)$ in~\eqref{eq:morphisms11EB} follow from requiring the existence of collars for the source and target. Any pair of choices of collar provide isomorphic functors~\eqref{eq:IM}; see Remark~\ref{rmk:collarexists}.
<!-- end defn-19 -->
<!-- rmk-21: body_md -->
In parallel to Remark~\ref{rmk:germs1}, $S$-points of ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ or ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ determine isomorphic objects in ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ under ${\sf I}^\pm_M$ if the associated maps $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ agree on a neighborhood of the core of the bordism, and so the family pulls back from the associated quotient.
<!-- end rmk-21 -->
<!-- defn-20: body_md -->
\label{defn:11EBspath2}
Define maps of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:LM}
\begin{array}{c} {\sf L}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\sf L}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)),\\
{\sf R}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\sf R}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{< 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
as follows. Again for $\Phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ and $(t,\theta)\colon S\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ consider~\eqref{eq:morphism11}, but choose source and target data
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:spath11EB}
&&(Y_{{\rm in}}^c, Y_{{\rm out}}^c)=\left\{\begin{array}{lll} \Big(\big(({\rm spt}^+,\Phi),({\rm spt}^-,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})\big),\emptyset\Big) &\implies (L_{t,\theta}^+,\Phi) & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}(S) \\
\Big(\big(({\rm spt}^-,\Phi),({\rm spt}^+,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})\big),\emptyset\Big) & \implies(L_{t,\theta}^-,\Phi) & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}(S)  \\ 
\Big(\emptyset,\big(({\rm spt}^-,\Phi),({\rm spt}^+,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})\big)\Big)& \implies(R_{t,\theta}^+,\Phi) & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}(S) \\
\Big(\emptyset,\big(({\rm spt}^+,\Phi),({\rm spt}^-,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})\big)\Big) & \implies(R_{t,\theta}^-,\Phi) & (t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{<0}(S)
\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
where the restriction on $(t,\theta)$ is necessary for the existence of collars for the source and target. Any pair of choices provide isomorphic functors~\eqref{eq:LM}; see Remark~\ref{rmk:collarexists}.
<!-- end defn-20 -->
<!-- rmk-22: body_md -->
\label{rmk:collarexists}
The requirements on~$(t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}(S)$ in~\eqref{eq:morphisms11EB} and~\eqref{eq:spath11EB} come from demanding the existence of the collars $W_{{\rm in}/{\rm out}}^\pm$ with properties demanded by Definition~\ref{defn:GBord}; any pair of choices of $W_{{\rm in}/{\rm out}}^\pm$ lead to isomorphic objects in ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ by intersecting the choices of collar. 
                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
We emphasize that the families $(R_{t,\theta}^\pm,\Phi)$ in~\eqref{eq:morphisms11EB} do not have a limit in $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ as $(t,\theta)\to 0$; compare \cite[Theorem 6.23]{HST}.
<!-- end rmk-22 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
The restriction of the spin flip on ${\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ or ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ along ${\rm spt}^\pm_M$, ${\sf I}^\pm_M$, ${\sf L}^\pm_M$ or ${\sf R}^\pm_M$ is determined by the maps
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)&\to&{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\quad \phi\mapsto \phi\circ {\sf fl}^{-1}\nonumber\\
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)&\to&{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\quad (t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (t,-\theta,\phi\circ {\sf fl}^{-1})\nonumber\\
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)&\to&{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\quad (t,\theta,\phi)\mapsto (t,-\theta,\phi\circ {\sf fl}^{-1})\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
This follows from Definition~\ref{defn:spinflip} of the spin flip.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:stI}
Let ${\sf u}$ be the unit functor in $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$. There is a 2-commutative diagrams of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (C) at (7,0) {${\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (D) at (7,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (E) at (3.25,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\rm spt}^+_M$} (C);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (A) to node [left] {$i_0\times{{\rm id}}_{{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)}$} (B);
\draw[->] (C) to node [right] {${\sf u}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [above] {${\sf I}^+_M$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:unitcyl}
\end{eqnarray}
where the left vertical arrow is inclusion along $0\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$. Let ${\sf c}$ be the composition functor. There is a 2-commutative diagrams of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (8,0) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))^{[2]}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (D) at (8,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}(2|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (E) at (4,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\sf I}^+_M \circ p_2 \times  {\sf I}^+_M \circ p_1$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf m}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf I}^+_M$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf c}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:comp2iso}
\end{eqnarray}
where the top horizontal arrow is determined by the family ${\sf I}^+_M$ and the maps
\begin{eqnarray}
&&p_i\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) \to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\nonumber\\ 
&&p_1\big((s,\eta),(t,\theta),\Phi\big)=(t,\theta,\Phi),\qquad p_2\big((s,\eta),(t,\theta),\Phi\big)=(s,\eta,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})\label{eq:composablesuperpath}
\end{eqnarray}
and ${\sf m}$ is inherited from multiplication in ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:sfm}
{\sf m}\big((s,\eta),(t,\theta),\Phi\big)=(s+t+\eta\theta,\eta+\theta,\Phi).
\end{eqnarray}
There are analogous diagrams to~\eqref{eq:unitcyl} and~\eqref{eq:comp2iso} for the family of bordisms classified by~${\sf I}^-_M$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
The commutativity of the diagram~\eqref{eq:unitcyl} is almost immediate; the only subtlety comes from the choice of collars in the construction of the family ${\sf I}^+_M$. Indeed, rather than a strictly commutative diagram this choice leads to 2-commutativity data gotten from the isomorphism between objects of ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ from shrinking the collar in~\eqref{eq:collardataI}. 

Turning to the diagram~\eqref{eq:comp2iso}, the definition of the $S$-family $(I_{t,\theta}^+,\Phi)$ of bordisms implies that the pair~\eqref{eq:composablesuperpath} is indeed in the fibered product. The construction of 2-commutativity data comes from unpacking the definition of the functor ${\sf c}$, i.e., composition of bordisms. Consider the diagram 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:triplepath}
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xhookrightarrow{i_0 \coprod i_{t,\theta}\coprod i_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1} \xrightarrow{\Phi} M.
\end{eqnarray}
By forgetting any of the three inclusions of $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$, one obtains three possible $S$-points of the source of ${\sf I}^+_M$ via the input datum~\eqref{eq:morphism11}: forgetting $i_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)}$ gives the $S$-family of bordisms $(I^+_{t,\theta},\Phi)$, forgetting $i_{t,\theta}$ gives the $S$-family of bordisms $(I^+_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)},\Phi)$, and forgetting $i_0$ gives a family that is isomorphic to $(I^+_{s,\eta},\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta})$ (where the isomorphism is specified by $T_{t,\theta}$). These three $S$-families of bordisms gotten from~\eqref{eq:triplepath} coincide with the two projections out of the fibered product and the value of the functor~${\sf c}$. The only subtle aspect in commutativity of the diagram~\eqref{eq:comp2iso} is the choice of collars in the definitions of these families of bordisms, i.e., the choices in the construction of the functor ${\sf I}^+_M$. However, since any pair of choices lead to isomorphic bordisms (by intersecting the collars), we obtain canonical 2-commutativity data in~\eqref{eq:comp2iso}.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

The arguments involving ${\rm spt}^-_M$ and ${\sf I}^-_M$ are identical.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- rmk-23: body_md -->
In terms of $S$-families of bordisms, the top horizontal map in~\eqref{eq:comp2iso} is 
$$
\big((s,\eta),(t,\theta),\Phi\big)\mapsto \big((I^+_{s,\eta},\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}),(I^+_{t,\theta},\Phi)\big). 
$$
<!-- end rmk-23 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
Let ${\sf I}^\pm_0$ denote the composition ${\sf u}\circ {\rm spt}^\pm_M$, 
$$
{\sf I}^\pm_0\colon {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)).
$$
For an $S$-point $\Phi$ of the source above, let $(I_0^\pm,\Phi)$ denote the associated $S$-family of (identity) $1|1$-Euclidean bordisms.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjunctionbordisms}
There is a 2-commutative diagrams of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (9,0) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))^{[2]}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (D) at (9,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (E) at (3.25,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\sf L}^+_M\circ p_2 \times ({\sf I}^+_M\circ p_1 \coprod {\sf I}^-_M\circ p_3)$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf L}^+_M$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf c}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:adjunctioncyl}
\end{eqnarray}
where the top vertical arrow is determined by the families ${\sf L}^+_M$, ${\sf I}^+_M$ and ${\sf I}^-_M$ and the maps
\begin{eqnarray}
&&p_i\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M), \quad i=1,2\nonumber\\
&&p_1((t,\theta),(s,\eta),(r,\rho),\Phi)= (t,\theta,\Phi), \quad p_2((t,\theta),(s,\eta),(r,\rho),\Phi)= (s,\eta,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}) \label{eq:targetofadj}\\
                                                                                                                                                              
&&p_3\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\nonumber\\
&&p_3((t,\theta),(s,\eta),(r,\rho),\Phi)= (r,\rho,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}\circ T^{-1}_{s,\eta})
                                                                                                                                                            
\end{eqnarray}
and the left vertical arrow is determined by the multiplication in ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$,
$$
((t,\theta),(s,\eta),(r,\rho),\Phi)\mapsto ((r,\rho)^{-1}\cdot (s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta),\Phi). 
$$
There is a similar 2-commutative diagram for ${\sf L}^-_M$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
From the definitions of source and target data, the top map in~\eqref{eq:adjunctioncyl} does indeed yield an object in the fibered product. The 2-commutativity data comes from unpacking the definition of the functor ${\sf c}$. Similar to before, consider the diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
\resizebox{.9\textwidth}{!}{$
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xhookrightarrow{i_0 \coprod i_{t,\theta}\coprod i_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)}\coprod i_{(r,\rho)^{-1}\cdot (s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1} \xrightarrow{\Phi} M.$}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
In this case, forgetting any pair of factors in the coproduct gives the input data to an $S$-family of bordisms. For example, forgetting the middle two factors corresponds to the $S$-family of bordisms $(L^+_{(r,\rho)^{-1}\cdot (s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)},\Phi)$, which is the claimed composition.  The bordisms in~\eqref{eq:targetofadj} can similarly be extracted by forgetting the appropriate pair of inclusions and applying an appropriate isometry determined by a translation of $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- rmk-24: body_md -->
In terms of $S$-families of bordisms, the top horizontal map in~\eqref{eq:adjunctioncyl} is
$$
((t,\theta),(s,\eta),(r,\rho),\Phi)\mapsto \Big((L^+_{s,\eta},\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}),\big((I^+_{t,\theta},\Phi)\coprod (I^-_{r,\rho},\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}\circ T^{-1}_{s,\eta})\big)\Big).
$$
<!-- end rmk-24 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:duality}
There is a 2-commutative diagrams of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (10,0) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))^{[2]}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (D) at (10,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (E) at (3.25,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$({\sf L}_M^+\circ p_1\coprod {\sf I}_0^+\circ q_2)\times ({\sf I}_0^+\circ q_1\coprod {\sf R}^+_M\circ p_2)$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf m}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf I}^+_M$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf c}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:thickdiagram}
\end{eqnarray}
where the top vertical arrow is determined by the families ${\sf L}^+_M$, ${\sf R}^+_M$, ${\sf I}^\pm_0$, and the maps 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&p_i\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\nonumber\\
&&p_1((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=(t,\theta,\Phi),\quad p_2((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=(s,\eta,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}), \label{eq:targetofdual1}\\
&&q_i\colon \colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\to  {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\nonumber\\
&&\quad q_1((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=\Phi, \quad q_2((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1}\circ T_{s,\eta}^{-1}\nonumber
                                                                                                                                                                                          
\end{eqnarray}
and ${\sf m}$ is~\eqref{eq:sfm}. There is a similar 2-commutative diagram factoring ${\sf I}^-_M$ as a composition.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- rmk-25: body_md -->
In terms of $S$-families of bordisms, the top horizontal arrow in~\eqref{eq:thickdiagram} is 
$$
((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)\mapsto \Big((L^+_{t,\theta},\Phi)\coprod (I^+_0,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta} \circ T^{-1}_{s,\eta})\Big) , \Big((I_0^+,\Phi)\coprod (R_{s,\eta}^+,\Phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta}) \Big) . 
$$
<!-- end rmk-25 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:symmetry}
Let ${\sf L}^\pm_M\circ\sigma$ denote the functor ${\sf L}^\pm_M$ post-composed with the isomorphism in ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$ that exchanges the order of components of the target, i.e.,
$$
{\sf t}({\sf L}^\pm_{t,\theta}\circ\sigma,\Phi)=({\rm spt}^\mp,\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1})\coprod ({\rm spt}^\pm,\Phi).
$$
There is a 2-commutative triangle
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (7,-.75) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$};
\node (E) at (3.25,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\sf L}^+_M\circ \sigma$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf L}^-_M$} (B);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:symmetrybordism}
\end{eqnarray}
for the left vertical arrow
\begin{eqnarray}
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)&\to& {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\nonumber\\
(t,\theta,\phi)&\mapsto& (-t,-\theta,\phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1}). \label{eq:2morphsigma}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Starting with the data that determines $(L_{t,\theta}^+,\Phi)$, 
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\coprod S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1} \xhookrightarrow{i_0 \coprod i_{t,\theta}} S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1} \xrightarrow{\Phi} M.
\end{eqnarray}
exchanging the factors of the coproduct and acting on $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ by $T^{-1}_{t,\theta}=T_{(-t,-\theta)}$ provides the data determining $(L_{-t,-\theta}^-,\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1})$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:tracerelations}
There is 2-commutative diagrams of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M))^{\mathbb{Z}}$};
\node (B) at (8,0) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))^{[2]}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {$\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$};
\node (D) at (8,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$};
\node (E) at (3.25,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\sf L}^-_M\circ p_1\times {\sf R}^+_M\circ p_2$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to (C);
\draw[->] (C) to (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf c}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \label{eq:tracerelations}
\end{eqnarray}
where the ${\mathbb{Z}}$-fixed subspace has $S$-points $(t,\theta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}(S)$, $(s,\eta)\in {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}(S)$ and $\Phi\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to M$ satisfying
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:periodic1}
\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1}=\Phi\circ T_{s,\eta}^{-1}\iff \Phi=\Phi\circ (T_{(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)^{-1}})^{n},\quad n\in {\mathbb{Z}}
\end{eqnarray}
the top vertical arrow is determined by the families ${\sf L}^-_M$ and ${\sf R}^+_M$ and the maps
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:targetofdual}
&&p_1((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=(t,\theta,\Phi), \qquad p_2((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)=(s,\eta,\Phi)
\end{eqnarray}
and the left vertical arrow is determined by
$$
((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)\mapsto ((s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)^{-1},\Phi)\in \big({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)\big)(S)\supset \mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)(S)
$$
which determines an $S$-point of $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$ by the condition~\eqref{eq:periodic1}. There is a diagram analogous to~\eqref{eq:tracerelations} involving ${\sf L}^-_M$ and ${\sf R}^+_M$.
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
The compatibility $\Phi\circ T_{t,\theta}^{-1}=\Phi\circ T_{s,\eta}^{-1}$ in~\eqref{eq:periodic1} guarantees that the target of $(R^-_{s,\eta},\Phi)$ agrees with the source of~$(L^+_{t,\theta},\Phi)$. Hence, the bordisms are indeed composable and their composition is necessarily a bordism from the empty set to itself. Unpacking the definition of the functor ${\sf c}$ and examining the periodicity condition~\eqref{eq:periodic1}, one finds that this composition is indeed the claimed super Euclidean loop in~$M$ with circumference $(\ell,\lambda)=(s,\eta)\cdot (t,\theta)^{-1}$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- rmk-26: body_md -->
In terms of $S$-families of bordisms, the top horizontal arrow in~\eqref{eq:tracerelations} is 
$$
((t,\theta),(s,\eta),\Phi)\mapsto \Big((L^-_{t,\theta},\Phi),(R^+_{s,\eta},\Phi) \Big).
$$
<!-- end rmk-26 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:restrictRR}
The real structure on $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ sends $S$-families of bordisms to $\overline{S}$-families of bordisms specified by
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf R}({\rm spt}^\pm,\phi)&\simeq&({\rm spt}^\pm,\overline{\phi}\circ {\sf r})\nonumber\\
{\sf R}(I^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(I^\pm_{\overline{t},\overline{\theta}},\overline{\Phi}\circ {\sf r}) \nonumber\\
{\sf R}(L^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(L^\pm_{\overline{t},\overline{\theta}},\overline{\Phi}\circ {\sf r}) \nonumber\\
{\sf R}(R^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(R^\pm_{\overline{t},\overline{\theta}},\overline{\Phi}\circ {\sf r} ) \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where (in an abuse of notation) ${\sf r}\colon \overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to \overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{1|1}$ and ${\sf r}\colon \overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to \overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{0|1}$ are the maps determined by the real structure~\eqref{eq:real11} on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, $(\overline{t},\overline{\theta})\colon \overline{S}\to \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{1|1}$ is value of the conjugation functor on the map $(t,\theta)\colon S\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, and $\overline{\Phi}\colon \overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{1|1}\to M$, $\overline{\phi}\colon \overline{S}\times\overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{0|1}\to M$ are the maps conjugate to $\Phi$ and $\phi$ that use the canonical real structure $\overline{M}\simeq M$ on the ordinary manifold $M$.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The real structure on $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ evaluated on any of the above families is determined by the diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (AA) at (5,1.5) {$\overline{M}$};
\node (AAA) at (5.7,1.5) {$\simeq M$};
\node (A) at (0,0) {$\overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{0|1}$};
\node (B) at (5,0) {$\overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{1|1}$};
\node (C) at (10,0) {$\overline{S}\times \overline{{\mathbb{R}}}{}^{0|1}$};
\node (D) at (0,-1.5) {$\overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\node (E) at (5,-1.5) {$\overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$};
\node (F) at (10,-1.5) {$\overline{S}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (A) to node [above] {$i_{\overline{t},\overline{\theta}}$} (B);
\draw[->] (D) to node [left] {${\sf r}$} (A);
\draw[->] (E) to node [left] {${\sf r}$} (B);
\draw[->] (F) to node [left] {${\sf r}$} (C);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (D) to (E);
\draw[->,left hook-latex] (F) to (E);
\draw[->] (B) to node [left] {$\overline{\Phi}$} (AA);
