\draw[->] (C) to node [above] {$i_{\overline{0}}$} (B);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where the middle row is the value of the conjugation functor on a bordism over $M$, and the isomorphisms with the lower row use the real structure on the $1|1$-Euclidean geometry. Together with the fact that the real structure preserves the subspaces ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0},{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, one can choose isomorphisms as indicated in the proposition. These isomorphisms are unique up to the choice of collar data for the source and target.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:orientation11restrict}
The orientation reversal automorphism of $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ takes values
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Or}({\rm spt}^\pm,\phi)&\simeq&({\rm spt}^\mp,\phi\circ {\sf or}^{-1})\nonumber\\
{\sf Or}(I^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(I^\mp_{-t,-i\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf or}^{-1}) \nonumber\\
{\sf Or}(L^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(L^\mp_{-t,-i\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf or}^{-1}) \nonumber\\
{\sf Or}(R^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(R^\mp_{-t,-i\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf or}^{-1}) \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where (in an abuse of notation) ${\sf or}\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ is determined by the map~\eqref{eq:supertimereverse}.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The orientation reversal automorphism of $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ evaluated on any of the above families is determined by the diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (AA) at (5,1.5) {$M$};
\node (A) at (0,0) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\node (B) at (5,0) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$};
\node (C) at (10,0) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\node (D) at (0,-1.5) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\node (E) at (5,-1.5) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$};
\node (F) at (10,-1.5) {$S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$};
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (A) to node [above] {$i_{t,\theta}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf or}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [left] {${\sf or}$} (E);
\draw[->] (C) to node [left] {${\sf or}$} (F);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (D) to node [above] {$i_{-t,-i\theta}$} (E);
\draw[->,left hook-latex] (F) to node [above] {$i_0$} (E);
\draw[->] (B) to node [left] {$\Phi$} (AA);
\draw[->] (C) to node [above] {$i_0$} (B);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where the inclusions in the lower row are the unique ones making the diagram commute. Together with the fact that orientation reversal exchanges the subspaces ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0},{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$, one can choose isomorphisms as in the statement. These isomorphisms are unique up to the choice of collar data for the source and target.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:RG11restrict}
For $\mu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$, the renormalization group automorphism of $1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ takes values
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf RG}_\mu({\rm spt}^\pm,\phi)&\simeq&({\rm spt}^\pm,\phi\circ {\sf rg}_\mu^{-1})\nonumber\\
{\sf RG}_\mu(I^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(I^\pm_{\mu^2t,\mu\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf rg}_\mu^{-1}) \nonumber\\
{\sf RG}_\mu(L^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(L^\pm_{\mu^2 t,\mu\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf rg}_\mu^{-1}) \nonumber\\
{\sf RG}_\mu(R^\pm_{t,\theta},\Phi)&\simeq&(R^\pm_{\mu^2t,\mu\theta},\Phi\circ {\sf rg}_\mu^{-1}) \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where (in an abuse of notation) ${\sf rg}_\mu\colon S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ is determined by the map~\eqref{eq:superRG}.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
The argument is analogous to the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:orientation11restrict}, using this time that ${\sf rg}_\mu$ preserves the subspaces ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0},{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- defn-21: body_md -->
\label{defn:smallbordisms}
Consider the families of bordisms associated to the maps of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:LM0}
\begin{array}{c} 
{\rm spt}^\pm_M\colon {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\
{\sf i}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\sf i}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\
{\rm l}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\rm l}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\
{\sf r}^+_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\\ 
{\sf r}^-_M\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
by restriction of~\eqref{eq:sptM},~\eqref{eq:IM} and~\eqref{eq:LM} to the (finite-dimensional) subspace 
$$
{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\subset {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\qquad \phi_0\mapsto (S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\xrightarrow{p}S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\xrightarrow{\phi_0} M).
$$
We refer to the families~\eqref{eq:LM0} as \emph{small bordisms} in $M$.
<!-- end defn-21 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:FTrestrict1}
The maps of stacks~\eqref{eq:superpathtoEB} are part of the data of an internal functor~\eqref{eq:maininclude} from the super Lie category of nearly constant superpaths in~$M$ (viewed as a category internal to stacks) to the $1|1$-Euclidean bordism category over $M$. Under this functor, the restriction of the structures ${\sf Or}, {\sf RG}_\mu$ and ${\sf R}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:extrastrEB} are compatible with the structures on ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:structureonsP}.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
The data of an internal functor is reviewed in Definition~\ref{defn:internalfunctor}. In addition to the maps of stacks~\eqref{eq:superpathtoEB}, we require compatibility data for composition and units. This is given by Proposition~\ref{prop:stI}. Since the 2-isomorphism data in this proposition is canonical (coming from intersecting collars of bordisms), the coherence property demanded by these 2-isomorphisms is automatic. This completes the construction of the internal functor~\eqref{eq:maininclude}.

The compatibility of this functor with the additional structures follows from Propositions~\ref{prop:restrictRR}, \ref{prop:orientation11restrict} and~\ref{prop:RG11restrict}: the isomorphisms in these propositions restricted to the appropriate families in~\eqref{eq:LM0} supply 2-commutativity data, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{eq:RGOrRR}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (B) at (3,0) {$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (D) at (3,-1.5) {$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf RG}_\mu,{\sf Or}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to  (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf RG}_\mu,{\sf Or}$} (D);
\node (E) at (1.5,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\quad 
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf sPath}_0(M)$};
\node (B) at (3,0) {$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {$\overline{{\sf sPath}_0(M)}$};
\node (D) at (3,-1.5) {$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf R}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to  (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf R}$} (D);
\node (E) at (1.5,-.75) {$\ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{eqnarray}
witnessing the claimed compatibility.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- rmk-27: body_md -->
Composition and disjoint union of small bordisms generates a subcategory $1|1\hbox{-{\sf ebord}}(M)\subset 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ of small bordisms in $M$. Morally, the categories $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ in Theorems~\ref{thm:cocycle} and~\ref{thm:index} considers degree~$n$ field theories defined on these subcategories. However, it is difficult to formulate a precise notion of generators for a (sub)category in the framework from~\cite{ST11}, and so instead we formulate our results in terms of the further subcategory ${\sf sPath}_0(M)\subset 1|1\hbox{-{\sf ebord}}(M)$.
<!-- end rmk-27 -->
<!-- rmk-28: body_md -->
\label{rmk:genrelate} 
                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                  
                                                                                          
                                         
                                                                                                                            
 
The values of the degree~$n$ twist for a $d$-dimensional Euclidean field theories without supersymmetry are listed in~\cite[\S5.3]{ST11}. 
                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                              
                                                                                                     
One possible way to extend this construction to (supersymmetric) $1|1$-Euclidean bordisms involves a generators and relations presentation for the bordism category. Such presentations have been described in~\cite[6.7]{HST}, \cite[3.2]{ST11}, and the proof of~\cite[Proposition 4.16]{ST11}. However, complete statements and proofs have yet to appear. 
In terms of these expected generators and relations, $1|1$-Euclidean field theories of degree~$n$ are equivalent to a quantum mechanical theory with the $n$th Clifford algebra ${\rm Cl}_n$ acting by symmetries in the sense of~\S\ref{eq:CliffordlinearFT}, see~\cite[\S3.2]{ST04} and~\cite[Main Theorem]{HST}. The construction of the degree~$n$ twist outlined below is compatible with these prior expectations.
<!-- end rmk-28 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:dataoftwistedFT} Given an internal functor $\mathscr{T}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$, a $\mathscr{T}$-twisted field theory~$E$ determines data
\begin{enumerate}
\item bundles of left modules
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
\begin{array}{c}
\nonumber _{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)}E({\rm spt}^+_M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),\quad \nonumber _{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)}E({\rm spt}^-_M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)
                
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
where $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$ are super algebra bundles over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$;
\item maps of bimodule bundles over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf I}^+_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)} {\rm proj}_+^*E({\rm spt}^+_M)\to {\rm act}_+^*E({\rm spt}^+_M),\nonumber\\
&& E({\sf L}^+_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes {\rm act}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)} {\rm proj}_+^*E({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes {\rm act}_+^*E( {\rm spt}^-_M)\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}} ,\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
maps of bimodule bundles over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf R}^+_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf R}^+_M)\to {\rm proj}_+^*E({\rm spt}^-_M) \otimes {\rm act}_+^*E({\rm spt}^+_M), \nonumber
 \end{eqnarray}
 maps of bimodule bundles over  ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$,
 \begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf I}^-_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^-_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^-_M)} {\rm proj}_-^*E({\rm spt}^-_M)\to {\sf t}^*E({\rm spt}^-_M),\nonumber\\
&& E({\sf L}^-_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf L}^-_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)\otimes {\rm act}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)} {\rm proj}_-^*E({\rm spt}^-_M)\otimes {\rm act}_-^*E( {\rm spt}^+_M)\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}} ,\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
and maps of bimodule bundles over  ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{< 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$,
\begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf R}^-_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf R}^-_M)\to {\rm proj}_-^*E({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes {\rm act}_-^*E({\rm spt}^-_M), \nonumber
 \end{eqnarray}
for the projection and action maps ${\rm proj}_\pm$ and ${\rm act}_\pm$ defined immediately after~\eqref{eq:actproj};
\item a section of the dual of the equivariant vector bundle $\mathscr{T}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M))$ over the stack~$\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$
$$
E(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M))\colon \mathscr{T}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)) \to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}\nonumber
$$
that is invariant under the action of super Euclidean isometries on $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
By Definition~\ref{defn:internalfunctor} of an internal functor, the twist determines maps of stacks
$$
{\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\to {\rm Ob}({\sf {Alg}}),\qquad {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})
$$
which can be evaluated on the objects of the source stacks defined in~\S\ref{sec:superpathbordism}. Hence, the twist determines bundles:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of super algebras;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of ${\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)$-${\rm act}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)$-bimodules;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^-_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of ${\rm proj}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-${\rm act}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-bimodules;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of right ${\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes{\rm act}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-modules;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^-_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of right ${\rm proj}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)\otimes{\rm act}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)$-modules;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^+_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of left ${\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)\otimes{\rm act}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)$-modules;
\item $\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^-_M)\to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{< 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ of left ${\rm proj}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes{\rm act}_-^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-modules; 
\item and $\mathscr{T}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M))\to\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$, a vector bundle.
\end{itemize}
The additional data $\mu$ in~\eqref{eq:internalfunctordiag} of an internal functor provides maps of bimodule bundles associated with compositions of bordisms; we spell out the data inherited from Propositions~\ref{prop:stI}, \ref{prop:adjunctionbordisms},~\ref{prop:duality},~\ref{prop:symmetry}, and~\ref{prop:tracerelations}. We obtain a map of $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)$-bimodules,
                                                                 
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
&&p_2^* \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\otimes_{p_2^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)} p_1^* \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\to  {\sf m}^*\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M),\nonumber\\ 
&&{\rm over}\quad  {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where $p_1,p_2$ are the maps in~\eqref{eq:composablesuperpath}. There is a similar isomorphism of $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$ bimodules over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$. We also obtain a map of right $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes \mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-module bundles
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:twistadjunction}
&&p_2^* \mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M)\otimes_{p_2^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes p_3^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)} (p_1^* \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\otimes p_3^*\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^-_M))\to {\sf m}^*\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M),\nonumber \\ 
&&{\rm over} \quad {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where $p_1,p_2,p_3$ are the maps in~\eqref{eq:targetofadj}. There is a similar isomorphism involving $\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^-_M)$. There is a map of vector bundles
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Eq:twisttrace}
&&p_1^*\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M)\otimes_{p_1^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes p_2^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)} p_2^*\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^-_M)\to {\sf c}^*\mathscr{T}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)),\quad {\rm over } \quad \mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)
\end{eqnarray}
for $p_1,p_2$ the maps in~\eqref{eq:targetofdual}. There is an isomorphism of right ${\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^+_M)\otimes {\rm act}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^-_M)$-module bundles
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:twistsymemtry}
{\rm inv}^*\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^-_M)\simeq \mathscr{T}({\sf L}^+_M)\quad {\rm over} \quad {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) 
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\rm inv}$ is the map~\eqref{eq:2morphsigma}. The isomorphisms above associated to composition are subject to further coherence conditions, as dictated by the definition of an internal functor. 


A twisted field theory is defined as an internal natural transformation (see Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}), and hence is the data of a map of symmetric monoidal stacks with involution $\eta\colon {\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$ and compatibility data~\eqref{diag:nu}. The map of stacks~$\eta$ hence determines morphisms over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
\begin{array}{c}
\nonumber E({\rm spt}^\pm_M) \in {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}}), \quad {\rm with} \quad {\sf t}(E({\rm spt}^\pm_M))= \mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M), \ {\sf s}(E({\rm spt}^\pm_M))= \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}.
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
By the definition of ${\sf {Alg}}$, this provides the bundles of left modules in~(1): the right action by $\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$ is no additional data.  The data $\rho$ of a twisted field theory yields the data in (2) and (3) by the argument from~\cite[page 52]{ST11}. For example, $\rho$ evaluated on the family ${\sf I}^\pm_M$ is a map of bimodules
$$
E({\sf I}^+_M)\colon \mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_+^*\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^+_M)} {\rm proj}^*E({\rm spt}^+_M)\to {\rm act}_+^*E({\rm spt}^+_M)
                                                                                                                                                              
$$
which is the first map of bimodules listed above.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:maincompositionstatement}
The data in Proposition~\ref{prop:dataoftwistedFT} satisfy compatibility properties with respect to composition of bordisms. 
In particular, we have an equality of bimodule maps 
                                                                 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:comppathbimodule}
p_1^* E({\sf I}^+_M)\circ p_2^* E({\sf I}^+_M)= {\sf m}^*E({\sf I}^+_M),\quad {\rm over}\quad  {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) 
\end{eqnarray}
where $p_1,p_2$ are the maps~\eqref{eq:composablesuperpath}. There is further an equality of bimodule maps
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:bimoduleadjunction}
&&
\resizebox{.9\textwidth}{!}{$p_2^* E({\sf L}^+_M)\circ (p_1^* E({\sf I}^+_M)\otimes p_3^*E({\sf I}^-_M))= {\sf m}^*E({\sf L}^+_M), \ {\rm over} \ {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge0}\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) $}
\end{eqnarray}
where $p_1,p_2,p_3$ are the maps in~\eqref{eq:targetofadj}. We have the equality of dual sections of $\mathscr{T}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M))$ 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Eq:bimoduletrace}
p_1^*E({\sf L}^+_M)\circ p_2^*E({\sf R}^-_M)={\sf m}^*E(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)),\quad {\rm over } \quad \mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)
\end{eqnarray}
for $p_1,p_2$ the projections to the factors in~\eqref{eq:targetofdual}. Proposition~\ref{prop:symmetry} yields the equality of maps
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:bimodulesymemtry}
{\rm inv}^*E({\sf L}^-_M)=E({\sf L}^+_M)\quad {\rm over} \quad {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M) 
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\rm inv}$ is the map~\eqref{eq:2morphsigma}. Analogous statements hold after exchanging the $+$ and $-$ decorations for the families of bordisms.
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
The claim follows from Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory} of an internal natural transformation, where the data in Proposition~\ref{prop:dataoftwistedFT} must satisfy compatibility properties for composition in the internal category~$1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)$ and invariance properties for isomorphisms in the stack ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$. We emphasize that the relations demanded above are now \emph{conditions} that certain maps of vector bundles be equal rather than additional data.

In more detail,~\eqref{eq:comppathbimodule} follows from compatibility with composition for the families ${\sf I}^+_M$ as computed in Proposition~\ref{prop:stI}. The equality~\eqref{eq:bimoduleadjunction} follows from compatibility for composition of the families ${\sf L}^+_M$ and ${\sf I}^+_M\coprod {\sf I}^-_M$ computed in Proposition~\ref{prop:adjunctionbordisms}. The equality~\eqref{Eq:bimoduletrace} follows from compatibility with the composition of ${\sf L}^+_M$ and ${\sf R}^-_M$ computed in Proposition~\ref{prop:tracerelations}. Finally,~\eqref{eq:bimodulesymemtry} follows from the isomorphism of families of bordisms computed in Proposition~\ref{prop:symmetry}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:RPtwist}
A reflection structure for a twist $\mathscr{T}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$ determines an invertible $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$-${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M))}$-bimodule $\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$
and isomorphisms of bimodules (where the bimodule on the right is the identity bimodule)
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:involutiondata}
\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm\otimes {\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{R}}_\mathscr{T}^\mp\simeq \mathscr{T}({\sf S}^\pm_M)
\end{eqnarray}
and isomorphisms of bimodules
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^\pm_M)\otimes_{{\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)} {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm \xrightarrow{\sim} {\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm \otimes_{{\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}} {\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^\mp_M)},\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^\pm_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}({\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm\otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\mp) \xrightarrow{\sim} {\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^-_M)},\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$  or ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$, and 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^+_M)\xrightarrow{\sim}({\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\mp \otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm)\otimes_{{\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*(\overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)})}  {\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^-_M)},
\end{eqnarray}
over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ or ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{<0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ satisfying an involutive property, where above we have used the notation for values of the twist listed in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:dataoftwistedFT}.
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Equivariance data demands an internal natural isomorphism, which (from Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}) is a map of stacks 
$$
\phi\colon {\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}({\rm pt}))\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})^\times
$$
valued in invertible bimodules, together with coherence data $\rho$ satisfying properties. Applying $\phi$ to the family ${\rm spt}^\pm_M$, we obtain the claimed bundle of invertible bimodules. Applying $\rho$ to the families ${\sf I}^\pm_M$, ${\sf L}^\pm_M$ and ${\sf R}^\pm_M$ from~\S\ref{sec:superpathbordism}, a reflection structure specifies data of isomorphisms of bimodules involving the values of the twist listed in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:dataoftwistedFT}. The other ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-equivariance datum is an isomorphism $\beta$ between internal natural isomorphisms, see~\eqref{eq:equivariantfunctor2}; this determines the isomorphism of bimodules~\eqref{eq:involutiondata}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:RPFT}
Fix a reflection structure for a twist $\mathscr{T}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$. Then a reflection structure for a $\mathscr{T}$-twisted field theory is an isomorphism of bundles of left $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$-modules over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$
 
 
                                                                                
     
                                                                                                                                                   
     
\begin{eqnarray}
E({\rm spt}^\pm_M) \stackrel{\sim}{\to} \mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm \otimes_{{\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}}  {\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\mp_M))}.\label{eq:RPdataonspt}
                                                                                     
\end{eqnarray}
These isomorphisms are required to satisfy compatibility conditions for the families ${\sf L}^\pm(M)$, ${\sf R}^\pm(M)$, and~${\sf I}^\pm(M)$, namely commutative squares, 
\begin{eqnarray}
\resizebox{.95\textwidth}{!}{$
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^\pm_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)} {\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$};
\node (B) at (8,0) {${\rm act}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\Big(\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf I}^\mp_M)} \otimes_{\overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}} \overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}\Big)$};
\node (D) at (8,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^* \overline{E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$E({\sf I}^\pm_M)$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\simeq$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{E({\sf I}^\mp_M)}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\simeq$} (D);

\end{tikzpicture}$}\label{eq:selfadjointdiagram}\\
\resizebox{.95\textwidth}{!}{$
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^\pm_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)} {\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\otimes{\rm act}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)$};
\node (B) at (9,0) {$\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*(\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf L}^\mp_M)} \otimes_{\overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}} \overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}$};
\node (D) at (9,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^* \underline{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}}}$};

\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\simeq$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{E({\sf L}^\mp_M)}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\simeq$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}$}\label{eq:RPdataonL0m}
\end{eqnarray}
over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$, and commutative squares over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{<0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$
\begin{eqnarray}\resizebox{.95\textwidth}{!}{$
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$};
\node (B) at (9,0) {$\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^\pm_M)\otimes_{{\rm proj}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)\otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)} {\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)\otimes{\rm act}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^* \underline{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}}}$};
\node (D) at (9,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*(\overline{\mathscr{T}({\sf R}^\mp_M)} \otimes_{\overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}} \overline{{\rm proj}}_\mp^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\mp^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\mp_M)}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$E({\sf R}^\pm_M)$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\simeq$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{E({\sf R}^\mp_M)}$} (D);

where the vertical arrows use data from Lemma~\ref{lem:RPtwist} and~\eqref{eq:RPdataonspt}, though we have suppressed the tensor products with the bimodules $\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm$ that mediate between $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm)$-modules and ${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\mp)}$-modules to avoid (further) cluttering the notation.
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Reflection positivity data for a twisted field theory is defined as an isomorphism between internal natural transformations, see Definition~\ref{defn:equivariancedata2}. From Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}, this is an isomorphism between the maps of stacks ${\rm Ob}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$ that are part of the data of the internal natural transformation. Evaluating this isomorphism between maps of stacks on the families ${\rm spt}^\pm_M$ yields the data~\eqref{eq:RPdataonspt}. 

For the data~\eqref{eq:RPdataonspt} to determine an isomorphism between internal natural transformations, there are compatibility requirements for each object of ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$. Evaluating on the families ${\sf I}^\pm_M$, ${\sf L}^\pm_M$ and ${\sf R}^\pm_M$ recovers the claimed commutative squares.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:Realtwist}
A real structure for a twist $\mathscr{T}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$ determines an invertible $\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)$-${\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M))}$-bimodule $\mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ with involutive data analogous to~\eqref{eq:involutiondata} and isomorphisms of bimodules analogous to those in Lemma~\ref{lem:RPtwist}.

\begin{eqnarray}
E({\rm spt}^\pm_M) \stackrel{\sim}{\to} \mathscr{R}_\mathscr{T}^\pm \otimes_{{\sf r}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}({\rm spt}^\pm_M)}}  {\sf r}^*\overline{E({\rm spt}^\pm_M))}\label{eq:RPdataonspt2}

<!-- hyp-1: body_md -->
\label{hyp1}
When $d=1$, an invertible twist $\mathscr{T}$ is equivalent to the invertible twist~\eqref{eq:degreetwistsketch} constructed from the value~\eqref{eq:valueoftwist} of $\mathscr{T}$ on ${\rm spt}^+$.
<!-- end hyp-1 -->
<!-- hyp-2: body_md -->
\label{hyp:twist}
The degree twist $\mathscr{T}=\mathscr{T}^{\otimes 1}$ is determined under~\eqref{eq:valueoftwist} by the Clifford algebra,~${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_1$. A reflection structure for the degree twist is fixed by the standard $*$-structure~\eqref{eq:starCl} on~${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_1$. A real structure for the twist is fixed by the standard real structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_1$.
<!-- end hyp-2 -->
<!-- rmk-29: body_md -->
The 2-dimensional spin topological field theory associated to a Clifford algebra has been studied in detail by Gunningham~\cite{Sam}.
<!-- end rmk-29 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:degreenvalues}
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, a degree~$n$ twisted field theory $E$ determines
\begin{itemize}
\item bundles of left ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-modules
$$
{\mathcal{V}}_\pm :=E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M);
$$
\item maps of bundles of ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-modules over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf I}^\pm_M)\colon {\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\to {\rm act}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M),\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
compatible with composition~\eqref{eq:comppathbimodule};
\item maps of vector bundles over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:Clnliearpairing}
&& E({\sf L}^\pm_M)\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n} \otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n} \otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\mp n}} \Big({\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M)\otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*E( {\rm spt}^\mp_M)\Big)\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}} ,
\end{eqnarray}
satisfying the adjunction relation~\eqref{eq:bimoduleadjunction} and the symmetry relation~\eqref{eq:bimodulesymemtry}; 

\item maps of left ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\mp n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-modules over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{> 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{< 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M)$
\begin{eqnarray}
&&E({\sf R}^\pm_M)\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\mp n} \to {\rm proj}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\mp_M) \otimes {\rm act}_\pm^*E({\rm spt}^\pm_M);\nonumber
 \end{eqnarray}
\item a section of the dual of the trivial line bundle with fiber ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n/[{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n]$ over the stack $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$
$$
E(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M))\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n/[{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n] \to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}\nonumber
$$
that is invariant under the action of super Euclidean isometries on $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)$ and agrees with the value gotten from~\eqref{Eq:bimoduletrace}. 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end cor-3 -->

<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:hermitian}
The pairing~\eqref{eq:Lzeropairing3} is hermitian in the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded sense
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle x,y\rangle =(-1)^{|x||y|}\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}.\label{eq:sesquilinear}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The argument uses similar ideas to the first part of \cite[Corollary 6.25]{HST}, though the signs here are different as we are working in the oriented setting (versus the unoriented framework of \cite{HST}). 
Equation~\eqref{eq:sesquilinear} follows from commutativity of the diagram 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:hermitianargument}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (AA) at (0,1.5) {$\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}\otimes_{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}\otimes{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}} ({\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{{\rm proj}}_\pm^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\pm\otimes {\rm act}_\mp^*{\mathcal{V}}_\pm)$};
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\mp n}\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\mp n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}}({\rm proj}_\mp^*{\mathcal{V}}_{\mp}\otimes {\rm act}_\mp^*{\mathcal{V}}_\pm)$};
\node (B) at (8,0) {$\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\Big(\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}\otimes_{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}\otimes \overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\mp n}} (\overline{{\rm proj}}_\pm^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\pm\otimes \overline{{\rm act}}_\pm^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\mp)\big)$};
\node (D) at (8,-1.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}}$};
\node (DD) at (4,-3.5) {${\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\big(\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\mp n}\otimes_{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\mp n}\otimes \overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}} (\overline{{\rm act}}_\pm^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\mp\otimes \overline{{\rm proj}}_\pm^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\pm)$};
\draw[->] (AA) to (A);
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$E({\sf L}^\mp_M)$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$\overline{E({\sf L}^\pm_M)}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\simeq$} (D);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$\sigma$} (DD);
\draw[->] (DD) to node [right=10pt] {$\overline{{\rm inv}}^*\overline{E({\sf L}^\mp_M)}$} (D);
\draw[->, bend left=10] (AA) to node [above=8pt] {restricts to $\langle-,-\rangle$} (B);
\path (0,0) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{eqnarray}
where the $*$-structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$ is used implicitly throughout. As indicated, the upper right arrow restricts to the pairing $\langle-,-\rangle$ by definition. 
Commutativity of the lower triangle follows from~\eqref{eq:bimodulesymemtry}.  Commutativity of the inner square is the condition ~\eqref{eq:RPdataonL0m2} on reflection positivity data.
                                                                                                  
The composition of arrows starting from the top left and using the lower triangle is the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:sesquilinear}, and hence the restriction of this diagram along~\eqref{eq:restrictalongthis} implies the claimed formula.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- rmk-30: body_md -->
We comment in more detail about the differing signs in the above argument and \cite[Corollary 6.25]{HST}.
First, in the unoriented framework of \cite{HST} there is a ${\mathbb{C}}$-linear isomorphism ${\mathcal{V}}_\pm\simeq {\sf or}^*{\mathcal{V}}_\mp$. This results in a ${\mathbb{C}}$-bilinear pairing through a definition analogous to~\eqref{eq:Cliffadjoint}. Second, ${\sf or}^2=(-1)^{\sf F}$ whereas $\overline{({\sf r}\circ {\sf or})}\circ ({\sf r}\circ {\sf or})={{\rm id}}$. This extra factor of $(-1)^{\sf F}$ results in a pairing that is naively symmetric in \cite[Corollary 6.25]{HST}, as compared with the graded symmetry of~\eqref{eq:sesquilinear}.
<!-- end rmk-30 -->
<!-- defn-22: body_md -->
\label{defn:RPFT} A $1|1$-Euclidean field theory of degree~$n$ with reflection positivity data is \emph{reflection positive} if the pairing~\eqref{eq:Lzeropairing3} is a (graded) positive-definite hermitian pairing on the super vector bundle~$V_+$ over $M$.
<!-- end defn-22 -->
<!-- rmk-31: body_md -->
For a reflection positive field theory,~\eqref{eq:Cliffadjoint} implies that the ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$-action on $V_+$ is automatically a $*$-representation relative to the hermitian inner product.
<!-- end rmk-31 -->
<!-- rmk-32: body_md -->
\label{rmk:RPFT}
We contrast Definition~\ref{defn:RPFT} with the definition of positivity in~\cite{HST}, where the $1|1$-Euclidean bordism category includes the orientation reversing map as an isometry. By functoriality, this orientation-reversing isometry must be sent to a ${\mathbb{C}}$-linear map. In particular, the positivity condition in~\cite[Definition 6.26 and 6.49]{HST} is not equivalent to reflection positivity above, where orientation-reversal corresponds to a ${\mathbb{C}}$-antilinear map. However, after one imposes real structures on field theories, positivity in the sense of~\cite{HST} implies the real reflection-positive structure in the sense above.
<!-- end rmk-32 -->
<!-- defn-23: body_md -->
\label{defn:repofSL}
A \emph{representation} of a super Lie category ${\sf C}$ is the data of a vector bundle ${\mathcal{V}}\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and a map of vector bundles $\rho\colon {\sf s}^*{\mathcal{V}}\to {\sf t}^*{\mathcal{V}}$ over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$. This data is required to satisfy the condition ${\sf u}^*\rho={{\rm id}}_{\mathcal{V}}$ on ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and $p_1^*\rho\circ p_2^*\rho={\sf c}^*\rho$ on ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})$. An \emph{isomorphism} $({\mathcal{V}},\rho)\simeq ({\mathcal{V}}',\rho')$ between representations is an isomorphism of vector bundles ${\mathcal{V}}\to {\mathcal{V}}'$ over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ for which $\rho$ and $\rho'$ satisfy a compatibility property over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$.
<!-- end defn-23 -->
<!-- ex-4: body_md -->
A supermanifold $S$ determines a super Lie category ${\sf C}$ with ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})={\rm Mor}({\sf C})=S$, i.e., a discrete super Lie category. In this case, a representation of ${\sf C}$ is the same data as a vector bundle over $S$.
<!-- end ex-4 -->
<!-- ex-5: body_md -->
\label{ex:supersemigroup}
Let ${\sf C}$ be the super Lie category with a single object and ${\rm Mor}({\sf C)}={\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$, where composition is inherited from the super semigroup structure on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$. Then a representation of ${\sf C}$ as a super Lie category is equivalent to a super semigroup representation~\eqref{eq:N1super}.
<!-- end ex-5 -->
<!-- defn-24: body_md -->
\label{defn:SLtwist}
A \emph{twist} $\mathscr{T}$ for a super Lie category ${\sf C}$ is the data of:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathscr{T}_0\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ a bundle of algebras;
\item $\mathscr{T}_1 \to {\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ a bundle of invertible ${\sf t}^*\mathscr{T}_0$-${\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0$-bimodules;
\item an isomorphism of bimodule bundles $\epsilon\colon {\sf u}^*\mathscr{T}_1\stackrel{\sim}{\to} \mathscr{T}_0$ over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ where $\mathscr{T}_0$ is regarded as a bimodule over itself; 
\item a map of bimodule bundles $\mu\colon p_1^*\mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{p_2^*{\sf t}^*\mathscr{T}_0} p_2^*\mathscr{T}_1\stackrel{\sim}{\to} {\sf c}^*B\mathscr{T}_1$ over the fibered product of pairs of composable morphisms, ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})$.
                  
                                                                               
                                                                                                                                        
                         
   
                                                 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
   
\end{enumerate}
The maps of $\mathscr{T}_0$-bimodules are required to satisfy further coherence conditions for composition with the identity and associativity of composition (see Lemma~\ref{lem:fancyrep}). An \emph{isomorphism} $\mathscr{T}\simeq \mathscr{T}'$ between twists is an invertible $\mathscr{T}_0$-$\mathscr{T}_0'$ bimodule $\mathscr{B}$ over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and an isomorphism $\mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{{\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0} {\sf s}^*\mathscr{B}\simeq {\sf t}^*\mathscr{B}\otimes_{{\sf t}^*\mathscr{T}_0'}\mathscr{T}_1'$ of bimodules over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ satisfying a property over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})$.
<!-- end defn-24 -->
<!-- rmk-33: body_md -->
When ${\sf C}$ is a Lie groupoid and the fibers of $\mathscr{T}_0\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ are central simple algebras, the above definition reduces to Freed's notion of an invertible algebra bundle over~${\sf C}$ \cite[Definition 1.59]{Freedalg}. In particular, gerbes provide examples of twists for the (\v{C}ech) groupoid associated to an open cover~\cite[Example 1.74]{Freedalg}. Invertible algebra bundles over quotient Lie groupoids determine twists for (equivariant) K-theory~\cite[Definition 1.78]{Freedalg}, see also Karoubi~\cite{KaroubiFrench} and Donovan--Karoubi \cite{DonovanKaroubi}. All the examples of twistings below will have algebra bundles whose fibers are central simple.
<!-- end rmk-33 -->
<!-- rmk-34: body_md -->
Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist} is set up so that Lemma~\ref{lem:fancyrep} holds using \cite[Definition 5.1]{ST11} for the internal Morita category ${\sf {Alg}}$. As a consequence, Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist} does not play well with equivalences of super Lie categories, see Remark~\ref{rmk:badcat}. There are various well-known ways to fix this issue. 
                                                                                                                    
For example, define a new version of twisting consisting of an equivalence of super Lie categories ${\sf C}'\xrightarrow{\sim} {\sf C}$ and a twist for ${\sf C}'$ in the above sense; this is essentially the definition of twistings for the K-theory of topological groupoids in~\cite{FHTI}. In all the examples below, twistings fit into the more naive framework of Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist}.
<!-- end rmk-34 -->
<!-- defn-25: body_md -->
\label{def:twrep}
Given a twist for a super Lie category ${\sf C}$, a \emph{twisted representation is}
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\eta\colon {\mathcal{V}}\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ a bundle of left $\mathscr{T}_0$-modules;
\item $\rho\colon \mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{{\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0} {\sf s}^*{\mathcal{V}}\to {\sf t}^*{\mathcal{V}}$ a map of bundles of left ${\sf t}^*\mathscr{T}_0$-modules over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$
                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                    
                  
                                                                               
                                                                                                                                        
                         
   
                                                 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
   
\end{enumerate}
with the condition that the module maps (2) are compatible with composition in ${\sf C}$. Given an isomorphism between twists, and isomorphism between twisted representations $({\mathcal{V}},\rho)\simeq ({\mathcal{V}}',\rho')$ is an isomorphism of left modules $\mathscr{B}\otimes_{\mathscr{T}_0} {\mathcal{V}}\simeq {\mathcal{V}}'$ over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ with a compatibility condition over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$.
<!-- end defn-25 -->
<!-- defn-26: body_md -->
\label{defn:algebratwist}
For any super Lie category ${\sf C}$ and super algebra~$A$, define the twist $\mathscr{T}_A$ given by the trivial bundle of algebras over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ with fiber $A$, and trivial bundle of bimodules over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ with fiber $A$ regarded as a bimodule over itself. The isomorphism $\epsilon$ is the identity, and $\mu$ is determined by the isomorphism $A\otimes_A A\simeq A$. We observe that Morita equivalent algebras give rise to isomorphic twists. For $A={\mathbb{C}}$, the twist $\mathscr{T}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is the \emph{trivial twist}, which we will also denote by $\mathbbold{1}\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf {Alg}}$.
<!-- end defn-26 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
A twisted representation for the trivial twist determines a representation of ${\sf C}$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:repofSL}.
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:fancyrep}
A twist for a super Lie category ${\sf C}$ is the same as an internal functor $\mathscr{T}\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf {Alg}}$, and a $\mathscr{T}$-twisted representation is equivalent to an internal natural transformation 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\sf {Alg}},$};
\node (C) at (2.1,0) {$E \Downarrow$};
\draw[->,bend left=12] (A) to node [above] {$\mathbbold{1}$} (B);
\draw[->,bend right=12] (A) to node [below] {$\mathscr{T}$} (B);
\path (0,0) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\sf {Alg}}$ is the internal Morita category (see Definition~\ref{defn:Morita}). Isomorphisms between twists in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist} are equivalent to internal natural isomorphisms between $\mathscr{T},\mathscr{T}'\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf {Alg}}$. Isomorphisms between twisted representations in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:twrep} are the same as isomorphisms between internal natural transformations $E\simeq E'$.
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
The claim follows from unpacking the definitions. Super Lie categories can be regarded as categories internal to stacks; see \S\ref{sec:STBord} below. Using that ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ are representable stacks, the data of the internal functor~$\mathscr{T}$ (see Definition~\ref{defn:internalfunctor}) is the same as a twist in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist}. The data of an internal natural transformation~$E$ (see Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}) is equivalent to a twisted representation $({\mathcal{V}},\rho)$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:twrep}. The statements for isomorphisms between twists and isomorphisms between twisted representations follow similarly.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- ex-6: body_md -->
Let ${\sf C}$ be the super Lie category from Example~\ref{ex:supersemigroup}. Consider the twist from Definition~\ref{defn:algebratwist} relative to the algebra ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$. 
                                                                                                                                                    
Then a twisted representation of ${\sf C}$ is a Clifford linear super semigroup representation ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\to {\rm End}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\mathcal{V}})$ for a ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$-module~${\mathcal{V}}$.
<!-- end ex-6 -->
<!-- defn-27: body_md -->
For a super Lie category ${\sf C}$, the \emph{conjugate} super Lie category, denoted $\overline{\sf C}$, is defined by applying the conjugation functor on supermanifolds to the objects, morphisms, and structure maps of ${\sf C}$. Similarly, for a smooth functor $F\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ between super Lie categories, let $\overline{F}\colon \overline{\sf C}\to \overline{\sf D}$ be the \emph{conjugate} smooth functor between conjugate categories, and for a smooth natural transformation $\eta\colon F\Rightarrow G$, let $\overline{\eta}\colon \overline{F}\Rightarrow \overline{G}$ denote the \emph{conjugate} smooth natural transformation between the conjugate smooth functors.
<!-- end defn-27 -->
<!-- defn-28: body_md -->
\label{defn:RealLie} A \emph{Real} structure on a super Lie category ${\sf C}$ is a smooth functor ${\mathscr R}\colon {\sf C}\to \overline{\sf C}$ and a smooth natural isomorphism $\eta\colon {{\rm id}}_{\sf C}\Rightarrow \overline{{\mathscr R}}\circ {\mathscr R}$. A super Lie category with a real structure is a \emph{Real super Lie category}, denoted $({\sf C},{\mathscr R},\eta)$.
<!-- end defn-28 -->
<!-- defn-29: body_md -->
\label{defn:Realrep}
For ${\sf C}$ be a super Lie category with Real structure ${\mathscr R}$, a \emph{Real structure} for a twist $\mathscr{T}$ is an internal natural isomorphism~$\phi_\mathscr{T}$
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1) {$\overline{\sf C}$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\sf {Alg}}$};
\node (D) at (4,-1) {${\sf {Alg}},$};
\node (E) at (2,-.5) {$\phi_\mathscr{T} \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$\mathscr{T}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\mathscr R}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$\overline{\mathscr{T}}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$(\overline{\phantom{A}})$} (D);
\path (0,-.5) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
and an isomorphism $\beta_\mathscr{T}$ of internal natural transformations $\phi_\mathscr{T}^2\circ \eta_{\sf C}\simeq \eta_{{\sf {Alg}}}={{\rm id}}$, see~\eqref{eq:equivariantfunctor2}. The data $(\mathscr{T},\phi_\mathscr{T},\beta_\mathscr{T})$ is a \emph{Real twist}. A \emph{Real structure} for a $\mathscr{T}$-twisted representation $E$ is a Real structure for $\mathscr{T}$ and an isomorphism between internal natural transformations $\phi_\mathscr{T} \circ E\simeq E\circ \phi_\mathbbold{1}$ compatible with $\beta_\mathscr{T}$ using the canonical real structure for the internal functor~$\mathbbold{1}$.
<!-- end defn-29 -->
<!-- lem-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:RealData} For a Real super Lie category $({\sf C},{\mathscr R})$ and twist $\mathscr{T}$, a Real structure on $\mathscr{T}$ determines data
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
a bundle $N \to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ of invertible $\mathscr{T}_0$-${{\mathscr R}_0}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}$  bimodules with an isomorphism
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:dataofbeta}
N\otimes_{\mathscr{T}_0} {\overline{{\mathscr R}}_0}^*\overline{N}\simeq \mathscr{T}_0
\end{eqnarray}
of bimodule bundles over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$;
\item[(ii)] an isomorphism of ${\sf t}^*\mathscr{T}_0$-${\sf s}^*{\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}$ bimodule bundles over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$
$$
\mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{{\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0} {\sf s}^*N\xrightarrow{\sim} {\sf t}^*N\otimes_{{\sf t}^*{\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\mathscr R}_1^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_1}
$$
\end{enumerate}
satisfying a compatibility condition on ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})$. 

Given a Real twist, a Real twisted representation determines additional data 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(iii)] an isomorphism of left $\mathscr{T}_0$-modules $N\otimes_{{\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}\xrightarrow{\sim} {\mathcal{V}}$ over ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$
\end{enumerate}
satisfying the property that the diagram of ${\sf t}^*{\mathscr R}_0\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}$-${\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0$ bimodule bundles over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ commutes
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (-4,0) {$\mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{{\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0} {\sf s}^*(N\otimes_{{\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}})$};
\node (B) at (-4,-1.5) {${\sf t}^*N\otimes_{{\sf t}^*{\mathscr R}_0^* \overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\mathscr R}_1^*(\overline{\mathscr{T}_1} \otimes_{{\sf s}^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\sf s}^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}})$};
\node (C) at (2,0) {$\mathscr{T}_1\otimes_{{\sf s}^*\mathscr{T}_0} {\sf s}^*{\mathcal{V}}$};
\node (D) at (2,-1.5) {${\sf t}^*{\mathcal{V}}$};
\node (E) at (-1,-3) {${\sf t}^*(N\otimes_{{\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}} {\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}})$};
\draw[->] (C) to node [right] {$\rho$} (D);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\rm {\rm (ii)}}\otimes {{\rm id}}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${{\rm id}}\otimes {\rm (iii)}$} (C);
\draw[->] (B) to node [left=5pt] {${{\rm id}}\otimes {\mathscr R}_1^*\overline{\rho}$} (E);
\draw[->] (E) to node [right=5pt] {${\sf t}^*{\rm (iii)}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{diag:reflectionpositivitycondition}
\end{eqnarray}
with maps defined by the data above as indicated.
<!-- end lem-18 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}, the first piece of data of the internal natural transformation $\phi_\mathscr{T}$ is a map of stacks
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:bimoduleN}
N\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}}), \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
which by the Yoneda lemma is equivalent to a bundle of bimodules over the supermanifold ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$. The source of this bimodule is the algebra bundle ${\mathscr R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}}_0$, and the target is $\mathscr{T}_0$. As the internal natural transformation is invertible, this bundle of bimodules is also required to be invertible. The isomorphism~\eqref{eq:dataofbeta} is the datum $\beta_\mathscr{T}$. This provides the data in part (i) of the lemma. Part (ii) supplies the datum denoted $\rho$ in~\eqref{diag:nu} for an internal natural transformation. The condition on the data (i) and (ii) similarly follows from the definition of an internal natural transformation over ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})$. 

The data of an isomorphism between internal natural transformations is an isomorphism between their corresponding maps of stacks ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$; see Definition~\ref{rmk:twistedcategory}. In this case, this is precisely the datum~(iii). The diagram~\eqref{diag:reflectionpositivitycondition} is the coherence condition so that this isomorphism of maps of stacks determines an isomorphism between internal natural transformations.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- ex-7: body_md -->
\label{Ex:Atiyah}
For an ordinary manifold $X$ regarded as a super Lie category, an involution $\alpha\colon X\to X$ determines a Real structure on~$X$ by setting ${\mathscr R}$ to be the composition
$$
X\xrightarrow{\alpha} X\simeq \overline{X}
$$ 
for the canonical real structure on $X$ coming from complex conjugation of smooth functions. Taking the trivial twist with its canonical Real structure, a Real representation of $(X,\alpha)$ is then the same data as a Real vector bundle in the sense of Atiyah~\cite{AtiyahReal}.
<!-- end ex-7 -->
<!-- defn-30: body_md -->
\label{defn:Cliffordtwist} The \emph{degree~$n$ twist} for the super Lie category ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is the coproduct of trivial algebra bundles on objects,
$$
\underline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_n\coprod \underline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{-n}\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)={\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))
$$
and the coproduct of trivial bimodule bundles over morphisms
$$
\underline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_n\coprod \underline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{-n} \to {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)={\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M)).
$$
The remaining data for this twist is specified by the identity isomorphism $\epsilon={{\rm id}}\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}\to {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$ and the canonical isomorphisms of Clifford bimodules, $
\mu\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}}{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}\stackrel{\sim}{\to} {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$ (for $\epsilon$ and $\mu$ in the notation of Definition~\ref{defn:SLtwist}). The required properties in this case are trivially satisfied.
<!-- end defn-30 -->
<!-- defn-31: body_md -->
\label{defn:degreensP}
A \emph{degree $n$ representation} of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is a twisted representation for the degree~$n$ twist.
<!-- end defn-31 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:EFT1}
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the restriction of a degree~$n$ field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines a degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$.
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
The value of the restriction on objects and morphisms of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is immediate from Corollary~\ref{cor:degreenvalues}, after further restricting the data there to the subspace
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:constantpathsubspace}
{\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\subset {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1},M),
\end{eqnarray}
which includes along the $S$-families of maps that factor through the quotient
$$
S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\to (S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1})/{\mathbb{R}}\simeq S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to M. 
$$
The compatibility with source, target, and units is clear; compatibility with composition comes from restricting~\eqref{eq:comppathbimodule} along~\eqref{eq:constantpathsubspace}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:superconn}
A degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ 
                     
   
                                                                           
    
determines ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-linear superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$ on super vector bundles $V_\pm \to M$.
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Following Definition~\ref{def:twrep}, let ${\mathcal{V}}={\mathcal{V}}_+\coprod {\mathcal{V}}_-$ denote the value of the representation on objects, where ${\mathcal{V}}_\pm\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ is a bundle of ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-modules and ${\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))={\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$. Using Lemma~\ref{lem:sVect}, we make the identification
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:vbidentification}
\Gamma({\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M);{\mathcal{V}}_\pm)\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm),\qquad V_\pm={\mathcal{V}}_\pm|_M
\end{eqnarray}
for vector bundles $V_\pm\to M$ gotten by restriction along the canonical inclusion $M\hookrightarrow {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$. 

The map of left $A$-modules in Definition~\ref{def:twrep} translates in this case to maps $\rho_\pm$ of ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-module bundles 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\rho_+\colon {\rm proj}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_+\to {\rm act}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_+\ {\rm over} \ {\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}^{1|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M) \nonumber\\
&&\rho_-\colon {\rm proj}_-^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\to {\rm act}_-^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\ {\rm over} \ {\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}^{1|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
for the projection and action maps gotten by restriction of~\eqref{eq:actproj}. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                            
Using~\eqref{eq:vbidentification} and applying Lemma~\ref{lem:action}, $\rho_\pm$ are maps of $\Omega^\bullet(M)$-modules for the action on the source and target gotten by pulling back along the projection or the restriction of~\eqref{eq:actdeRham}. This gives the description 
\begin{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                  
\rho_\pm(t,\theta,\alpha v)=(\alpha-\theta d\alpha)\rho_\pm (t,\theta,v),&& \alpha\in \Omega^\bullet(M), \ v\in \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)\label{eq:Leibniz} 
\end{eqnarray}
for the standard coordinates $t$ and $\theta$ on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Compatibility with composition promotes $\rho_+$ and $\rho_-$ to super semigroup representations, since multiplication in ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}$ corresponds to composition in~${\sf sPath}_0(M)$. 

                                                              

Taylor expanding~\eqref{eq:Leibniz}  in the odd variable $-\theta\in C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0})$, define
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:AB}
\rho_\pm(t,\theta,-)=A_\pm(t)- \theta B_\pm(t)
\end{eqnarray}
     
                                                                                                                                   
     
where $A_\pm(t)\colon \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)\to \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)$ is an even map and $B_\pm (t)\colon \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)\to \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)$ is odd, and both commute with the Clifford actions. Define
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\mathbb{A}}_\pm:=B_\pm(0)\colon \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm)\to \Omega^\bullet(M;V_\pm).\label{eq:superconnconstrr}
\end{eqnarray}
Since $B_\pm (t)$ is odd, so is ${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$. Furthermore, because $B_\pm(t)$ is ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-linear, so is ${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$. Finally, combining~\eqref{eq:Leibniz} and~\eqref{eq:AB} yields the pair of equations
$$
A_\pm(t)(\alpha v)=\alpha A_\pm(t)(v),\qquad B_\pm(t)(\alpha v)=d\alpha A_\pm(t)(v)+(-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha B_\pm(t)(v).
$$
Using that $A_\pm(0)={{\rm id}}_{V_\pm}$, the value of the second equation at $t=0$ is the Leibniz rule for the superconnections~${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- defn-32: body_md -->
Define the \emph{(Getzler) rescaling} of a Clifford linear superconnection by the ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$-action~\eqref{eq:RGsconn}.
<!-- end defn-32 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:Getzler}
The renormalization group flow on a degree~$n$ field theory restricts along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} to determine the rescaling of the superconnections extracted in Proposition~\ref{prop:superconn}.
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Using~\eqref{eq:RGOrRR}, we can compute using the action of the renormalization group on ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$. This action was computed in~\eqref{eq:RGonsP}. In particular, we have an isomorphism
$$
{\mathcal{V}}_\pm\xrightarrow{\sim}{\sf RG}_\mu^*{\mathcal{V}}_\pm,\qquad s\mapsto \mu^{{\rm deg}/2}s,\qquad s\in \Gamma({\mathcal{V}}_\pm)
$$
viewing the source and target as $\Omega^\bullet(M)$-modules as in~\eqref{eq:vbidentification}, where the target module structure is twisted by pulling back along the RG-action. Hence, under the above identification a representation $\rho_\pm(t,\theta)$ of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is sent under ${\sf RG}_\mu$ to $\mu^{-{\rm deg}/2}\rho(\mu^2t,\mu\theta)\mu^{{\rm deg}/2}$. From the  definition~\eqref{eq:superconnconstrr} of the superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_+$ and ${\mathbb{A}}_-$ in terms of the representations $\rho_\pm(t,\theta)$ this yields the formula~\eqref{eq:RGsconn}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
The pullback of $\rho_-$ along ${\rm inv}$ gives a map of vector bundles 
$$
{\rm inv}^*\rho_-\colon {\rm act}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\to {\rm proj}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_-
$$
over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ commuting with the ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}$-action.
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
We observe that the triangles commute,
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\node (C) at (2,-2) {${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\rm inv}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left=5pt] {${\rm act}_+$} (C);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right=5pt] {${\rm proj}_-$} (C);
\path (0,-.5) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\quad
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\node (C) at (2,-2) {${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\rm inv}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left=5pt] {${\rm proj}_+$} (C);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right=5pt] {${\rm act}_-$} (C);
\path (0,-.5) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
using that 
$$
{\rm act}_\pm(t,\theta,\phi)=\phi\circ T^{-1}_{t,\theta},\qquad {\rm proj}_\pm(t,\theta,\phi)=\phi.
$$
Hence, we have
$$
{\rm act}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\simeq {\rm inv}^*{\rm proj}_-^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\xrightarrow{{\rm inv}^*\rho_-} {\rm inv}^*{\rm act}_-^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\simeq {\rm proj}_+{\mathcal{V}}_-
$$
so ${\rm inv}^*\rho_-$ uniquely determines a map with the claimed source and target.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- defn-33: body_md -->
\label{defn:pairing}
A \emph{pairing} on a degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is a vector bundle map over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:sPpairing}
L\colon {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} ({\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+)\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}
\end{eqnarray}
with the property that the diagram of vector bundles over ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ commutes 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\rm act}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\rm proj}_+^*{\mathcal{V}}_+)$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\rm proj}_+^*({\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+))$};
\node (B) at (7,0) {${\rm act}^*_+({\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+))$};
\node (D) at (7,-1.5) {$\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}.$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${{\rm id}}\otimes \rho_+$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\rm inv}^*\rho_-\otimes {{\rm id}}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\rm proj}_+^*L$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\rm act}_+^*L$} (D);
\path (0,-.5) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:adjunction}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-33 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:EFT2} Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the restriction of a degree~$n$ field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} equips the resulting degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ with a pairing.
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
The datum~\eqref{eq:sPpairing} follows from restricting $E({\sf L}^-_M)$ in Corollary~\ref{cor:degreenvalues} along~\eqref{eq:constantpathsubspace}. The property~\eqref{eq:adjunction} follows from~\eqref{eq:bimoduleadjunction} in Proposition~\ref{prop:maincompositionstatement}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\label{eq:proppairing}
Given a pairing on a degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$, the Clifford linear superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_+,{\mathbb{A}}_-$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:superconn} satisfy the adjunction formula,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:initialadjunction}
L({\mathbb{A}}_-v,w)+(-1)^{|v|}L( v,{\mathbb{A}}_+w)=dL( v,w). 
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Using the descriptions of ${\rm proj}^*_+{\mathcal{V}}_\pm$ and ${\rm act}^*_+{\mathcal{V}}_\pm$ in terms of modules over $\Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}))$ and $\Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}))$ (see Lemma~\ref{lem:stmap}) and the notation from Proposition~\ref{prop:superconn} we compute
\begin{eqnarray}
({\rm proj}_+^*L)(({\rm inv}^*\rho_-)(t,\theta,v),w)&=&L(\rho_-(-t,-\theta,v),w)=L( (A_-(-t)+\theta B_-(-t))v,w)\nonumber\\
&=&({\rm act}^*_+L)( v,\rho_+(t,\theta,w))\nonumber\\
&=&L( v,\rho_+(t,\theta,w)\rangle+\theta d\langle v,\rho_+(t,\theta,w))\nonumber\\
&=&L( v,(A_+(t)-\theta B_+(t))w\rangle+\theta d\langle v,(A_+(t)-\theta B_+(t))w), \nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
where the equalities above are between elements of $\Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}))$. 
Collecting the terms involving $\theta$, setting $t=0$, and using the definition of the superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_+$ and ${\mathbb{A}}_-$, the result follows.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- defn-34: body_md -->
\label{defn:reflectionstructure}
A \emph{reflection structure} for the degree~$n$ twist is a Real structure for the twist relative to $({\sf sPath}_0(M),{\sf R}\circ {\sf Or})$.
<!-- end defn-34 -->
<!-- lem-21: body_md -->
A $*$-superalgebra structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$ determines a reflection structure for the degree~$n$ twist.
<!-- end lem-21 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
By Definition~\ref{defn:Realrep} and Lemma~\ref{lem:RealData}, a Real structure is an invertible $\mathscr{T}_0-{\sf Or}_0^*{\sf R}_0^*\overline{\mathscr{T}_0}$-bimodule
over ${\rm Ob}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\simeq {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\coprod {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ with additional involutive data. For the degree~$n$ twist it suffices to consider the case $M={\rm pt}$. Such an invertible bimodule can be constructed from isomorphisms of algebras 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:whatisstar}
{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}\simeq \overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\mp n}=\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}^{\sf{op}}
\end{eqnarray}
satisfying an involutive property. Indeed, the above allows us to view ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ as a $\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_{\pm n}^{\sf{op}}$-${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ bimodule. An involutive algebra isomorphism~\eqref{eq:whatisstar} is precisely the data of a $*$-superalgebra structure, proving the lemma.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- defn-35: body_md -->
Define a $*$-superalgebra structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ given by the ${\mathbb{C}}$-antilinear extension of the map on generators,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:superstarCl}
f_j^*=-if_j,\qquad e_j^*=ie_j.
\end{eqnarray}
using the notation of generators for the Clifford algebra from~\eqref{eq:Clifford}.
<!-- end defn-35 -->
<!-- defn-36: body_md -->
\label{defn:rssP}
Suppose we are given a degree~$n$ representation $E$ of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ with a pairing~$L$. For the reflection structure for the degree~$n$ twist fixed by~\eqref{eq:superstarCl}, define a \emph{reflection structure} on $(E,L)$ as a Real twisted representation (see Definition~\ref{defn:Realrep}) with the additional property that the the pairing,
$$
\langle-,-\rangle\colon {\sf Or}_0^*{\sf R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_+\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} {\mathcal{V}}_+\simeq {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{\overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_n \otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\sf Or}_0^*{\sf R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_+\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+)\simeq 
{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n} \otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}({\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+)\xrightarrow{L}\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}
$$
is hermitian in the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded sense, where the second isomorphism above makes use of the Real structure on the representation. A degree~$n$ representation with a reflection structure is \emph{reflection positive} if the above pairing restricts along $M\subset {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ to a positive pairing (again in the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded sense).
<!-- end defn-36 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:EFT3}
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the restriction of a reflection structure on a degree~$n$, $1|1$-Euclidean field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines a reflection structure on a degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$. The restriction of a degree~$n$ reflection positive $1|1$-Euclidean field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines a degree~$n$ reflection positive representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$.
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist} states that the reflection structure for the degree~$n$ twist $\mathscr{T}^{\otimes n}\colon 1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$ comes from the $*$-superalgebra structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$. If we then further examine the data in Proposition~\ref{lem:RPtwist} and Corollary~\ref{cor:degreenvalues}, the restriction of a reflection structure along~\eqref{eq:constantpathsubspace} evidentially determines a Real degree~$n$ representation for the real structure on ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ given by ${\sf R}\circ {\sf Or}$. The symmetry of the pairing in Definition~\ref{defn:rssP} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:hermitian}. Finally, we observe that the positivity condition in Definition~\ref{defn:RPFT} is equivalent to the positivity condition in Definition~\ref{defn:rssP}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- prop-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:selfadjoint} 
The ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{n}$-linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}_+$ associated with a degree~$n$ reflection positive representation is self-adjoint with respect to the pairing from Definition~\ref{defn:rssP}.
<!-- end prop-20 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
A reflection structure gives isomorphisms of vector bundles over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$, 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:rsisos}
{\mathcal{V}}_\mp\stackrel{\sim}{\to} {\sf Or}_0^*{\sf R}_0^*\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\pm.
\end{eqnarray} 
Relative to these isomorphisms, we have the identities 
$$
\rho_\pm(t,\theta)=({\sf or}^*{\sf r}^*\overline{\rho}_\mp)(t,\theta)=i^{\rm deg}\overline{\rho}_\mp(-t,i\theta).
$$
Taylor expanding the above expression (as in~\eqref{eq:AB}), we find that the superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}_-$ is sent to $-i^{{\rm deg}+1}\overline{{\mathbb{A}}_+}$ under the isomorphism~\eqref{eq:rsisos}. Then by the adjunction formula~\eqref{eq:initialadjunction} and the definition of the hermitian pairing~\eqref{eq:sesquilinear}, we obtain the desired self-adjointness property for ${\mathbb{A}}_+$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lem-22: body_md -->
For the Real super Lie category $({\sf sPath}_0(M),{\sf R})$, a Real structure for the degree~$n$ twist is determined by a real structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$.
<!-- end lem-22 -->
<!-- defn-37: body_md -->
\label{def:realCl}
Define an antilinear involution ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\to \overline{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}}_n$ by declaring the generators of the Clifford algebra in~\eqref{eq:Clifford} to be real, and take the extension to a ${\mathbb{C}}$-antilinear map.
<!-- end defn-37 -->
<!-- defn-38: body_md -->
\label{defn:rrsP}
Suppose we are given a degree~$n$ representation $E$ of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ with a pairing~$L$. For the Real structure for the degree~$n$ twist fixed by Definition~\ref{def:realCl}, define a \emph{real, reflection positive degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$} as a Real structure on $E$ relative to ${\sf R}$ (in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:Realrep}), a reflection structure on $E$ satisfying the reflection positivity condition, and the further condition that the pairing satisfies the reality condition
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:realcondition}
\langle x,y\rangle=(-1)^{|\overline{x}|} {\sf R}_0^*\overline{\langle \overline{x},\overline{y}\rangle}
\end{eqnarray}
