for $x,y\in \Gamma(V_+)$, and $\overline{x},\overline{y}$ their image under the isomorphism $V_+\xrightarrow{\sim}{\sf R}_0^*\overline{V}_+$.
<!-- end defn-38 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:reality}
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the restriction of a real, reflection positive, degree~$n$, $1|1$-Euclidean field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines a real, reflection positive degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$.
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
The reality data on the degree~$n$ representation $E$ of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ is clear. It remains to check the condition on the pairing. This follows from the argument in the proof of \cite[Theorem 6.48]{HST}, where the relation between the reflection and real structures in~\eqref{Eq:Orrelation} introduces the sign $(-1)^{|\overline{x}|}$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:realA} 
A real, reflection positive degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ equips the vector bundle $V=V_+$ with a real structure such that the pairing~\eqref{eq:realcondition} comes from an ordinary (i.e., not ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded) real pairing on the underlying real vector bundle and the self-adjoint superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}={\mathbb{A}}_+$ is a real superconnection.
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
A Real structure for a degree~$n$ representation with respect to the involution ${\sf R}$ gives isomorphisms of bundles of ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{\pm n}$-modules over ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$, 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:risos}
{\mathcal{V}}_\pm\stackrel{\sim}{\to} {\sf R}^*_0\overline{{\mathcal{V}}}_\pm,
\end{eqnarray} 
relative to the chosen real structure on ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$. This gives an ordinary real structure on $V_+,V_-\to M$. The super semigroup representations satisfy the identity
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:realdataonC}
\rho_\pm(t,\theta)=({\sf R}^*_1\overline{\rho}_\pm)(t,\theta).
\end{eqnarray}
Taylor expanding the above expression (as in~\eqref{eq:AB}), the associated superconnections are real. The condition~\eqref{eq:realcondition} implies that the pairing is real for pairings between even sections, zero for pairings between even and odd sections, and purely imaginary for pairings between odd sections. The translation between a super Hilbert space and a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded Hilbert space is (compare~\cite[page~91]{strings1})
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Eq:metric}
( v,w):=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} \langle v,w\rangle & v,w \in \Gamma(V_+)^{\rm ev} \\ i^{-1}\langle v,w\rangle & v,w\in \Gamma(V_+)^{\rm odd} \\ 0 & {\rm else} \end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
and so we see that the condition~\eqref{eq:realcondition} leads to a real pairing~\eqref{Eq:metric} in the usual sense.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- defn-39: body_md -->
\label{defn:Pfaffian}
The \emph{Pfaffian line bundle} ${\sf{Pf}}\to \mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ is the pullback along \eqref{eq:sloopover} of the odd line bundle classified by
$$
{\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2) \xrightarrow{p} {\rm pt}/\!\!/ {\mathbb{Z}}/2={\rm pt}/\!\!/ \{\pm 1\}\to {\rm pt}/\!\!/ {\mathbb{C}}^\times
$$
where $p$ is determined by the projections ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\to {\rm pt}$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2\to {\mathbb{Z}}/2$, and we take the standard ${\mathbb{C}}^\times$-action on $\Pi {\mathbb{C}}$, the trivial odd line bundle over ${\rm pt}$. The Pfaffian line bundle is natural for maps of stacks $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2) \to\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(N)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2)$ induced by maps of smooth manifolds $M\to N$.
<!-- end defn-39 -->
<!-- rmk-35: body_md -->
Identify the quotient stack ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ with the stack of metrized circles with periodic spin structure, where ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$ acts by the spin flip on the spinor bundle, and ${\mathbb{R}}$ acts by rotation of the circle. The Dirac operator on the circle for the chosen spin structure gives an ${\mathbb{R}}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$-equivariant family of operators over ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$. The terminology in Definition~\ref{defn:Pfaffian} comes from the fact that the restriction of ${\sf{Pf}}$ along the canonical inclusion ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}/\!\!/ {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$ is the Pfaffian line bundle of the family of Dirac operators. This Pfaffian line bundle appears in Stolz and Teichner's sketch of the degree~$n$ twist for the Euclidean bordism category without supersymmetry; see~\cite[\S5.3]{ST11}.
<!-- end rmk-35 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
For $n\in {\mathbb{Z}}$, let ${\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes n}$ denote the $n$th tensor power of the Pfaffian line bundle over $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2)$. Sections are in bijection with
$$
\Gamma(\mathcal{L}_0^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2);{\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes n}) \simeq \left\{Z,Z_\ell\in \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}))\mid \begin{array}{c} dZ=0, \ \partial_\ell Z=dZ_\ell \\ {\rm deg}(Z)=n \mod 2, \\ {\rm deg}(Z_\ell)=n-1\mod 2\end{array}\right\}.
$$
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Under the identification 
$$
C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}))
$$
sections of ${\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes n}$ can be identified with a differential form valued in $C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0})$ with equivariance properties for the action by ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2$. Choosing coordinates $(\ell,\lambda)$ on ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{>0}$ and Taylor expanding a section $s$ in the odd variable $\lambda$, consider the parameterization 
$$
s=\ell^{{\rm deg}/2}Z+2i\lambda \ell^{({\rm deg}+1)/2}Z_\ell,\qquad Z,Z_\ell\in\Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0})).
$$
By \cite[Proposition~1.4]{DBEChern}, ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$-invariance is equivalent to the conditions $dZ=0$ and $\partial_\ell Z=dZ_\ell$. The degree condition on $(Z,Z_\ell)$ comes from equivariance for the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-action which acts by $(-1)^{\rm deg}$ on differential forms and $(\ell,\lambda)\mapsto (\ell,\pm \lambda)$. The result follows.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- defn-40: body_md -->
\label{defn:tracestru}
A \emph{trace class representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ of degree~$n$} is the data of a degree~$n$ representation $E$ of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ and a section $(Z(E),Z(E)_\ell)\in \Gamma(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}_0(M);{\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes -n})$ satisfying the property 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:traceclass}\label{eq:constpartitionfun2}
&&
\resizebox{.9\textwidth}{!}{$Z(E)=\ell^{-{\rm deg}/2}{\sf Tr}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}(\rho_+|_{{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)})\in C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M;{\mathbb{C}}^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}))$}
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\sf Tr}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}$ denotes the Clifford super trace.
<!-- end defn-40 -->
<!-- lem-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:4periodic}
For a trace class degree~$n$ representation, $Z(E)\in \Omega_{\rm cl}^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}))$ is a closed differential form in degrees equal to the parity of~$n$ (i.e., either even or odd degree). When $E$ is a real field theory, $Z(E)$ is a real differential form. When $E$ is real and reflection positive, $Z(E)$ is real and concentrated in degrees equal to $n$ mod 4.
<!-- end lem-23 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
For the first, note that the element $\Gamma_n\in {\rm Cl}_n\subset {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ has parity equal to the parity of $n$, and so the endomorphism $\Gamma_n\circ \rho_+$ also has parity~$n$ mod~2. Hence, it follows for any degree~$n$ representation for which the trace~\eqref{eq:traceclass} is defined, the resulting function is even or odd according to this parity. The real structure preserves $\Gamma_n\in {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{n}$, and the reality condition~\eqref{eq:realdataonC} implies that $Z(E)$ be equal to its conjugate. Since $\Gamma_n\in {\rm Cl}_n$ determines a real trivialization (see~\eqref{eq:Gamma}), this amounts to demanding that $Z(E)\in C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0}))$ is real as a differential form, for the standard conjugation action on ${\mathbb{C}}$-valued differential forms. When $E$ is also reflection positive, we observe that $\Gamma_n\mapsto i^n\Gamma_n$ under the $*$-superalgebra structure~\eqref{eq:superstarCl}. This imposes an additional invariance property on $Z(E)$, implying that it takes values in 4-periodic differential forms.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lem-24: body_md -->
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, a choice of orientation on ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ determines an isomorphism ${\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes n} \simeq \mathscr{T}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2))$ between the Pfaffian line bundle and the valued of the degree~$n$ twist on $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}(M)/\!\!/ ({\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}\rtimes {\mathbb{Z}}/2)$. In particular, a degree~$n$ field theory determines a section of the dual of ${\sf{Pf}}^{\otimes n}$.
<!-- end lem-24 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
It suffices to take $M={\rm pt}$. Then the value of the twist on $\mathcal{L}^{1|1}({\rm pt})$ is the line bundle with fiber 
                                                                                                                                            
$$
{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{n}\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{- n}}{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\simeq {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n/[{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n]. 
$$
A choice of orientation $\Gamma_n\in \Lambda^{\rm top}({\mathbb{C}}^n)\simeq {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n/[{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n]$ trivializes this line, and so after this choice it remains to compute the equivariance structure. Under Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$-action is trivial, and the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-action is by parity. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:trace}
Assuming Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:twist}, the restriction of a degree~$n$ field theory along~\eqref{eq:twistedrestriction} determines a trace class degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$.
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The argument is similar to \cite[Lemma~3.20]{ST11}. In the terminology of \cite{STTraces}, the morphisms in the image of the composition
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:thickfamily}
{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\hookrightarrow {\rm Mor}({\sf sPath}_0(M))\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))
\end{eqnarray}
are \emph{thick}: this follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:duality}. The categorical trace of a thick morphism is an endomorphism of the monoidal unit. Proposition~\ref{prop:tracerelations} shows that this categorical trace is the image of the composition
$$
{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to \mathcal{L}_0^{1|1}(M)\to {\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M)).
$$
Applying a degree~$n$ field theory to these families, Corollary~\ref{cor:degreenvalues} shows that the categorical trace of the family~\eqref{eq:thickfamily} is sent to the composition 
$$
{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\xrightarrow{{{\rm id}}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}\otimes R_{t,0}^+}{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} ({\mathcal{V}}_+\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_-)\xrightarrow{\sigma}{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} ({\mathcal{V}}_-\otimes {\mathcal{V}}_+) \xrightarrow{L_0} \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}.
$$
The element $\Gamma_n$ provides an identification ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n} {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\simeq \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$ with the trivial line bundle, and the above composition becomes the Clifford super trace. Finally, using that nuclear Fr\'echet spaces have the approximation property~\cite[page~109]{Schaefer}, we find that the categorical trace above is independent of the choice of thickener~\cite[Theorem 1.7]{STTraces}, completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- defn-41: body_md -->
\label{def:hypothesis}
Let $E$ denote a degree~$n$ representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$, and let ${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$ denote the superconnections afforded by Lemma~\ref{prop:FTrestrict1}. Then $E$ is \emph{infinitesimally generated} if we have the equality of differential forms 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:partitionisChern}
{\sf Tr}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}(\rho_+|_{{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)})={\sf sTr}_{{\rm Cl}_n}(\exp(-t{\mathbb{A}}^2))\in \Omega^\bullet(M;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0})),
\end{eqnarray}
compare~\eqref{eq:constpartitionfun2}. 
                          
                                                       
     
An infinitesimally generated representation \emph{admits smooth energy cutoffs} if furthermore the superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_\pm$ admits smooth index bundles in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:superconncutoff}.
<!-- end defn-41 -->
<!-- rmk-36: body_md -->
We comment on the conditions imposed in Definition~\ref{def:hypothesis}. Although one expects a field theory to be determined by infinitesimal data (implying the condition~\eqref{eq:partitionisChern}), this is not automatic in the formalism~\cite{ST11} due to the failure of existence and uniqueness of solutions to differential equations in topological vector spaces; see Remark~\ref{rmk:SParinfinite}. 
                                                                           
The existence of smooth index bundles is more subtle. For a family of Dirac operators, the existence of an index bundle follows from ellipticity, using that eigensections of the Dirac Laplacian are smooth, e.g., see~\cite[Proposition~9.10]{BGV} or~\cite[III, Theorem~5.8]{LM}. As such, the existence of smooth cutoffs can be thought of as an ellipticity property for field theories. In higher dimensions, one can formulate similar smooth cutoff conditions for subspaces~$\mathcal{H}^{\vec\lambda}\subset \mathcal{H}$ indexed by both energies and momenta, with the number of cutoff indices equal to the dimension of the field theory.
<!-- end rmk-36 -->
<!-- prop-25: body_md -->
\label{prop:dataofeft2}
There is an equivalence of categories
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
{\rm sPar}\colon {\sf Vect}^{{\mathbb{A}}}_{{\rm Cl}_n,{\rm ind}}(M) \xrightarrow{\sim} 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)
\end{eqnarray}
from the category of real, ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear self-adjoint superconnections admitting smooth index bundles to the category~$1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$.
<!-- end prop-25 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
For a ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on a real super vector bundle $V\to M$, consider the representation of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ defined on the vector bundles with sections
$$
\Gamma(\mathcal{V}_+):=\Omega^\bullet(M;V_{\mathbb{C}}),\qquad \Gamma(\mathcal{V}_-):=\Omega^\bullet(M;\overline{V}_{\mathbb{C}})
$$
and super semigroup actions given by 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:expof}
e^{-t{\mathbb{A}}^2+\theta{\mathbb{A}}}\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0} \to {\rm End}(\Omega^\bullet(M;V_{\mathbb{C}})),\qquad e^{-t\overline{{\mathbb{A}}}^2+\theta\overline{{\mathbb{A}}}}\colon {\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0} \to {\rm End}(\Omega^\bullet(M;\overline{V}_{\mathbb{C}})).
\end{eqnarray}
A pairing for this representation is inherited from the hermitian pairing $\overline{V}_{\mathbb{C}}\otimes V_{\mathbb{C}}\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$ built in the usual way from the underlying metric on~$V$. The real and reflection structures are evident from the construction, as is the reflection positivity condition. The trace structure uses that $\exp(-t{\mathbb{A}}^2)\in \Omega^\bullet(M;{\rm End}(V_{\mathbb{C}}))$ is trace class (from the existence of smooth index bundles), and $Z_\ell$ is determined by the Chern--Simons form for the 1-parameter family of superconnections gotten from Getzler rescaling of~${\mathbb{A}}$. Existence of cutoffs follows by assumption. This constructs the functor ${\rm sPar}$ in~\eqref{eq:dataofeft} on objects. The construction on morphisms is straightforward: using~\ref{eq:expof}, isomorphisms between superconnections are sent to isomorphisms between representations of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$. The functor is full and faithful since isomorphisms of representations of ${\sf sPath}_0(M)$ are determined by isomorphisms of vector bundles. Finally, Proposition~\ref{prop:geodata} verifies that ${\rm sPar}$ is essentially surjective, and hence an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:florin1}
The groupoid of self-adjoint ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnections on finite-rank real vector bundles admits a functor ${\rm sPar}$ 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:littlesPar}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf Vect}^{\mathbb{A}}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\rm finite}}(M)$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {$1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {\small sPar}  (B);
                             
                                       
\path (0,-.05) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture} \qquad (V,{\mathbb{A}})\mapsto E_{V,{\mathbb{A}}}
\end{eqnarray}
determined by super parallel transport along nearly constant superpaths.
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
This follows immediately from Proposition~\ref{prop:dataofeft} by the existence of smooth index bundles in finite dimensions, e.g., see~\cite[\S9.1]{BGV}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- defn-42: body_md -->
Given $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ and $\lambda\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$, the \emph{$\lambda$-cutoff theory} $E_{<\lambda}\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(U_\lambda)$ is defined as the functor~\eqref{eq:littlesPar} applied to the super vector bundle $\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}\to U_\lambda$ with Clifford linear self-adjoint connection $\nabla^{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}}$, i.e., 
$$
E_{<\lambda}:=E_{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda},\nabla^{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}}} \in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(U_\lambda)
$$ 
in the notation of Corollary~\ref{prop:florin1}.
<!-- end defn-42 -->
<!-- lem-25: body_md -->
The partition function of $E$ and the partition function of the $\lambda$-cutoff theory are related by
$$
Z(E)|_{U_\lambda}=Z_{E^{<\lambda}}+d\eta_\lambda\in \Omega^\bullet(U_\lambda;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0})).
$$
<!-- end lem-25 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
This follows from the construction of the $\eta$-forms~\eqref{eq:improperintegral}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- prop-26: body_md -->
\label{prop:RGcutoff}\label{lem:RGcutoff}  The existence of cutoffs is preserved under the renormalization group flow: for $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$, the $\lambda$-cutoff of~${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$ is canonically isomorphic to the $\mu\lambda$-cutoff of $E$
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:RGcutoff}
{\sf RG}^\mu(E)_{<\lambda}\simeq E_{<\mu\lambda}\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(U_{\mu\lambda}).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end prop-26 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Using Proposition~\ref{prop:RGcutoff}, the description of the ${\sf RG}$-action in terms of Getzler rescaling allows us to analyze cutoffs. Unraveling Definition~\ref{defn:effective}, the $\mu\lambda$-cutoff for $E$ is the same data as the $\lambda$-cutoff for ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$: the cutoff bundles are the \emph{same} subspace of $\mathcal{H}\to U_\lambda$ with the \emph{same} connection (note ${\mathbb{A}}_1$ is invariant under the ${\sf RG}$-flow). Hence, there is indeed a canonical isomorphism~\eqref{eq:RGcutoff}, and furthermore ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$ satisfies properties (1) and (2) of Definition~\ref{defn:effective}. Property (3) follows from the Getzler rescaling description of the ${\sf RG}$-action, where the partition function of ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$ is computed by the Getzler-rescaled superconnection. Finally, by a change of variables one identifies the integral~\eqref{eq:improperintegral} for~$E$ and $\lambda\mu$ with the integral for ${\sf RG}^\mu (E)$ and $\lambda$. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- defn-43: body_md -->
An object $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ \emph{flows to zero} under the renormalization group flow if for all $\lambda\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ and compact submanifolds $K\subset M$, there exists $\mu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ such that ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)|_K$ has the zero theory as its $\lambda$-cutoff, i.e., $K\subset U_\lambda$ and $\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}|_K=\{0\}$.
<!-- end defn-43 -->
<!-- lem-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:RGlimit}  
An object $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ flows to zero under the renormalization group flow if and only if the degree zero component of its associated superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}_{0}$ is invertible.
<!-- end lem-26 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
It suffices to prove the lemma when $M$ is compact. Let $\nu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ be the minimum eigenvalue of ${\mathbb{A}}_{0}^2$. If $\nu>0$ (i.e., ${\mathbb{A}}_{0}$ is invertible), for any $\lambda$ we may choose some $\mu\gg 0$ such that $\mu\nu>\lambda$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:RGcutoff} the $\lambda$-cutoff theory of ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$ is the zero theory. Conversely, if there exists some $\mu$ such that ${\sf RG}^\mu(E)$ has the zero bundle as its cutoff bundle, then $\mu\nu$ must be larger than $\lambda$, and hence $\nu\ne 0$ and ${\mathbb{A}}_0$ is invertible.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- defn-44: body_md -->
For $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$, choose a discrete subset $\Lambda\subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ such that $\{U_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$ is a locally finite cover. Then define the differential cocycle 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:IndexLambda}
{\rm Index}(E,\Lambda)=\{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda},\nabla^{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}},g_{\lambda\mu},e_{\lambda\mu},\eta_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \in \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M),
\end{eqnarray}
in the description of differential ${\rm KO}$-theory from \cite[\S7]{DBEBis}.
<!-- end defn-44 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
The index map~\eqref{eq:IndexLambda} applied to the self-adjoint superconnection underlying $E\in 1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ gives a map of the desired type, but a priori depends on a choice of subset $\Lambda\subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ determining a choice of locally finite subcover~$\{U_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$. To show that the differential KO-class is independent of this choice, one applies the same argument that proves the differential families index is well-defined~\cite[\S8.3]{DBEBis}. To review this argument, for a different choice $\Lambda'\subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$, we can compare the resulting ${\rm Cl}_{-n}$-bundles on the mutual refinement $\{U_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in (\Lambda\bigcup \Lambda')}$. For $\lambda<\lambda'$, we obtain inclusions~\eqref{eq:compatibilitydata} of ${\rm Cl}_{-n}$-bundles with commuting ${\rm Cl}_{-1}$-actions on the orthogonal complement to the inclusion. This gives the data of a stable equivalence of ${\rm Cl}_{-n}$-bundles. By~\cite[Lemma~5.9]{DBEBis}, the ${\rm Cl}_{-n}$-bundles are therefore concordant and the differential KO-classes agree. This shows that~\eqref{eq:IndexLambda} is independent of the choice of $\Lambda$, and the index map is well-defined. 

                                                                                                                                                                          
     
                                                      
     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

By Lemma~\ref{lem:RGlimit}, objects in $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)$ that are sent to zero under the RG flow are also sent to the zero class under the composition
$$
1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)\to \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)\to {\rm KO}^n(M),
$$
since the degree zero part of their associated superconnection is invertible, and hence the underlying KO-class is trivial. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- prop-27: body_md -->
\label{prop:fei}
The composition of the first two arrows
\begin{eqnarray}\nonumber
{\sf Vect}^{\mathbb{A}}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n,{\rm finite}}(M)\stackrel{{\rm sPar}}{\to}1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^n(M)\stackrel{{\rm Index}}{\longrightarrow} \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)\stackrel{{\rm curv}}{\to}\Omega^\bullet_{\rm cl}(M)
\end{eqnarray}
sends a Clifford linear superconnection to the expected differential ${\rm KO}$-class, and hence the above composition sends a ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ to the differential form ${\sf sTr}_{{\rm Cl}_n}(e^{-
{\mathbb{A}}^2})$ representing its Chern character.
<!-- end prop-27 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Without loss of generality, we may assume $M$ is compact. Choosing a cutoff valued~$\lambda$ larger than the maximum eigenvalue of ${\mathbb{A}}_0^2$, the index construction sends a vector bundle with Clifford linear superconnection to the associated differential class in $\widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)$, and the curvature of this class is as stated above. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Using Proposition~\ref{prop:dataofeft}, for a family $\pi\colon X\to M$ of Riemannian spin manifolds and $E\to X$ a real vector bundle the ${\rm Cl}_{-n}$-linear superconnection~\eqref{eq:Bismutsuper} acting on the Fr\'echet bundle $V=\pi_*({\mathbb{S}}\times E)\otimes {\mathbb{C}}$ determines an object of $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^{-n}(B)$ via the representation of positively oriented superpaths,
$$
\rho_+(t,\theta)=\exp(-t{\mathbb{A}}^2+\theta {\mathbb{A}}).
$$
The pairing and reflection positivity data are inherited from the hermitian pairing on $\pi_*({\mathbb{S}}\times E)\otimes {\mathbb{C}}$. The real structure comes from complex conjugation on $\pi_*({\mathbb{S}}\times E)\otimes {\mathbb{C}}$. The standard properties of the Bismut superconnection reviewed in~\S\ref{sec:dKO} imply the existence of a differential index bundle, so we do indeed obtain an object in $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^{-n}(M)$. Finally, applying the index map~\eqref{eq:IndexLambda} to this object of $1|1\hbox{-{\sf eft}}^{-n}(B)$ is precisely the (real) family Clifford index~\cite[Theorem~1.3]{DBEBis}. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- defn-45: body_md -->
A \emph{real structure} on a super vector space $V$ is an isomorphism $r\colon V\stackrel{\sim}{\to} \overline{V}$ of super vector spaces such that $\overline{r}\circ r={{\rm id}}_V$. The \emph{real subspace} associated with a real structure is the fixed point set $V_{\mathbb{R}}\subset V$ for $r$.
<!-- end defn-45 -->
<!-- defn-46: body_md -->
\label{defn:sesquilinear} A \emph{hermitian form} on a super vector space $V$ is the data of a map $\langle-,-\rangle\colon \overline{V}\otimes V\to {\mathbb{C}}$ making the diagram commute, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$\overline{V}\otimes V$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\mathbb{C}}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.25) {$V\otimes \overline{V}$};
\node (D) at (4,-1.25) {$\overline{{\mathbb{C}}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$\langle-,-\rangle$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\sigma$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$\overline{\langle-,-\rangle}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$(\overline{\phantom{A}})$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{eqnarray}
or equivalently, satisfying the formula $\langle x,y\rangle =(-1)^{|x||y|}\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}$ for homogeneous elements. A hermitian form is \emph{positive} if 
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle x,x\rangle>0, & x\ne 0 \ {\rm even} \quad {\rm and} \quad i^{-1}\langle x,x\rangle>0, & x\ne 0 \ {\rm odd.}\label{eq:positivitypairing}
\end{eqnarray}
A \emph{real} hermitian form on a super vector space with real structure is a hermitian form that when restricted to $(V_{\mathbb{R}})^{\rm ev}\subset V$ takes values in ${\mathbb{R}}\subset {\mathbb{C}}$ and when restricted to $(V_{\mathbb{R}})^{\rm odd}\subset V$ takes values in $i^{-1}{\mathbb{R}}\subset {\mathbb{C}}$.
<!-- end defn-46 -->
<!-- defn-47: body_md -->
Let $V$ be a super vector space equipped with a positive hermitian form~$\langle-,-\rangle$. The \emph{super adjoint} of a linear map $T\colon V\to V$ is characterized by
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle x,T y\rangle =(-1)^{|x||T|}\langle T^*x,y\rangle. \label{eq:superadjoint}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-47 -->
<!-- ex-8: body_md -->
Let $V$ be a super vector space with hermitian inner product. Then the super algebra ${\rm End}(W)$ has the structure of a $*$-superalgebra determined by the super adjoint~\eqref{eq:superadjoint}. A real structure on $W$ determines a real structure on ${\rm End}(W)$ for which this $*$-structure is real.
<!-- end ex-8 -->
<!-- ex-9: body_md -->
The Clifford algebras ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:Clifford} have the structure of $*$-superalgebras using~\eqref{eq:superstarCl}. Complex conjugation gives ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ the structure of a real super algebra for which this $*$-structure is real.
<!-- end ex-9 -->
<!-- ex-10: body_md -->
\label{ex:superstar}
For a super vector space $V$ with positive hermitian form $\langle-,-\rangle$, the super algebra ${\rm End}(V)$ has the structure of a $*$-superalgebra via the super adjoint. It has the structure of a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded $*$-algebra via the adjoint with respect to the (ungraded) inner product determined by~\eqref{eq:ordinarypairing}. These two notion of $*$-structure are related by~\eqref{eq:superadjointtrans}.
<!-- end ex-10 -->
<!-- ex-11: body_md -->
\label{ex:Cliffordstar}
In the case of the Clifford algebras ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$, we obtain a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded $*$-algebra via the ${\mathbb{C}}$-antilinear extension of the map on generators,
\begin{eqnarray}
f_j^\dagger=-f_j,\qquad e_j^\dagger=e_j.\label{eq:starCl}
\end{eqnarray}
This differs from the $*$-superalgebra structure~\eqref{eq:superstarCl} by a factor of $i$.
<!-- end ex-11 -->
<!-- ex-12: body_md -->
\label{ex:leftright}
A \emph{Clifford module} is a graded module over a Clifford algebra ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$. The canonical isomorphism ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n^{\sf{op}}\simeq {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}$ leads to equivalences of categories 
\begin{eqnarray}
{}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-m}}{\sf Mod}\simeq {}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}{\sf Mod}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_m}\simeq {\sf Mod}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-n}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_m}\label{eq:Cliffmods}
\end{eqnarray}
which will allow us to translate any Clifford (bi)module into a left Clifford module.
<!-- end ex-12 -->
<!-- defn-48: body_md -->
A module $V$ over a  $*$-superalgebra $A$ is \emph{self-adjoint} if the structure map $A\to {\rm End}(V)$ is a $*$-homomorphism for a specified hermitian form on $V$.
<!-- end defn-48 -->
<!-- rmk-37: body_md -->
When $A={\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n$ with the $*$-superalgebra structure~\eqref{eq:superstarCl}, the above definition is equivalent to~\cite[Definition~3.3]{BGV} via the translation to ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded $*$-algebras in Examples~\ref{ex:superstar} and~\ref{ex:Cliffordstar}.
<!-- end rmk-37 -->
<!-- ex-13: body_md -->
\label{ex:Morita1}
Define a left ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{1}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-1}$-module whose underlying super vector space is ${\mathbb{C}}^{1|1}$ with action determined by
\begin{eqnarray}
f\mapsto\left[\begin{array}{cc} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{array}\right],\qquad e \mapsto\left[\begin{array}{cc} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{array}\right].\label{eq:Cl11bimod}
\end{eqnarray}
The assignment~\eqref{eq:Cl11bimod} induces an isomorphism of super algebras, ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{1}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-1}\simeq {\rm End}({\mathbb{C}}^{1|1})$. In other words, ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{1}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-1}$ is Morita equivalent to ${\mathbb{C}}$. 
This ${\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{1}\otimes {\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_{-1}$-action is self-adjoint for the graded hermitian pairing on ${\mathbb{C}}^{1|1}$ coming from the standard hermitian pairing on ${\mathbb{C}}^2$ under~\eqref{eq:ordinarypairing}.
<!-- end ex-13 -->
<!-- ex-14: body_md -->
\label{ex:Roneonege}
                                                                                                                                          
Let ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ denote the supermanifold whose underlying topological space is ${\mathbb{R}}$, and structure sheaf is the sheaf of sections of $\Lambda^\bullet \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}^\vee$, where~$\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$ is the trivial complex line bundle on ${\mathbb{R}}$. Then define ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\ge 0}$ and ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}_{\le 0}$ by restricting the structure sheaf of ${\mathbb{R}}^{1|1}$ to ${\mathbb{R}}_{\ge 0}\subset {\mathbb{R}}$ and ${\mathbb{R}}_{\le 0}\subset{\mathbb{R}}$.
<!-- end ex-14 -->
<!-- ex-15: body_md -->
For a complex vector bundle $E\to N$ over an ordinary manifold $N$, let $\Pi E$ denote the supermanifold whose structure sheaf of ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded algebras is given by 
$$
U\mapsto C^\infty(U):=\Gamma(U;\Lambda^\bullet E^\vee),\qquad U\subset N. 
$$
Every supermanifold $S$ is isomorphic to $\Pi E$ for some vector bundle $E\to N=S_{\rm red}$~\cite{Batchelor}.
<!-- end ex-15 -->
<!-- ex-16: body_md -->
The supermanifold ${\mathbb{R}}^{n|m}$ is the locally ringed space with underlying topological space $({\mathbb{R}}^{n|m})_{\rm red}={\mathbb{R}}^n$ and structure sheaf the sheaf of sections of $\Lambda^\bullet (\underline{{\mathbb{C}}}^m)^\vee$, the trivial rank $m$ complex vector bundle on ${\mathbb{R}}^n$. The $S$-points of ${\mathbb{R}}^{n|m}$ are
$$
{\mathbb{R}}^{n|m}(S)\simeq \{t_1,\dots, t_n\in C^\infty(S)^{\rm ev}, \ \theta_1,\dots, \theta_m \in C^\infty(S)^{\rm odd} \mid (f_i)_{\rm red} =\overline{(f_i)}_{\rm red}\in C^\infty(S_{\rm red})\}
$$
where the reality condition on the $f_i$ is imposed on the reduced manifold of $S$.
<!-- end ex-16 -->
<!-- ex-17: body_md -->
Define ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ as the presheaf on supermanifolds whose value on $S$ is the set of maps $S\times {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\to M$; this supermanifold is representable~${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\simeq \Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}$, e.g., see~\cite[Proposition~3.1]{HKST}. Consider the precomposition action of ${\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$ on itself by translation,
$$
{\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}\times {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M). 
$$
Differentiation at $0\in {\mathbb{R}}^{0|1}$ gives an odd vector field on ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$. Under the isomorphism $C^\infty({\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M))\simeq C^\infty(\Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}})\simeq \Omega^\bullet(M)$, this vector field is the de~Rham differential, acting on forms as an odd derivation.
<!-- end ex-17 -->
<!-- ex-18: body_md -->
\label{ex:mappingsheaf}
Given supermanifolds $\Sigma$ and $X$, define the mapping object 
$$
{\sf Map}(\Sigma,X)\colon {\sf SMfld}^{\sf{op}}\to {\sf Set},\qquad {\sf Map}(\Sigma,X)(S):={\sf SMfld}(S\times \Sigma,X)
$$
as a generalized supermanifold with the indicated $S$-points.
<!-- end ex-18 -->
<!-- ex-19: body_md -->
\label{ex:tvspresheaf}
Given a ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded topological vector space ${\mathcal{V}}$, define a generalized supermanifold by the $S$-points 
$$
{\mathcal{V}}\colon {\sf SMfld}^{\sf{op}}\to {\sf Set},\qquad  {\mathcal{V}}(S):=(C^\infty(S)\otimes {\mathcal{V}})^{\rm ev}
$$ 
where the tensor product is the ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded projective tensor product.
<!-- end ex-19 -->
<!-- defn-49: body_md -->
\label{defn:realsmfld}
There is an involution on the category of supermanifolds, 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:conjugationfunctor}
(\overline{\phantom{-}})\colon {\sf SMfld}\to {\sf SMfld},\qquad S\mapsto \overline{S}
\end{eqnarray}
sending a supermanifold to the same locally ringed space but whose sheaf has complex numbers acting through complex conjugation. A \emph{real structure} on a supermanifold $S$ is an isomorphism $r_S\colon S\stackrel{\sim}{\to} \bar S$ such that $\overline{r}\circ r={{\rm id}}_S$. A map $f\colon S'\to S$ between supermanifolds with real structure is \emph{real} if $r_S\circ f=f\circ r_{S'}$.
<!-- end defn-49 -->
<!-- ex-20: body_md -->
\label{ex:real}
For a complex vector bundle $E\to N$, a real structure on $E$ (as a vector bundle) determines a real structure on $\Pi E$ (as a supermanifold) 
$$
C^\infty(\Pi E)\simeq \Gamma(N;\Lambda^\bullet E^\vee)\simeq \Gamma(N;(\Lambda E_{\mathbb{R}}^\vee)\otimes {\mathbb{C}}) \qquad (E_{\mathbb{R}})\otimes {\mathbb{C}}\simeq E. 
$$
Indeed, complex conjugation determines a ${\mathbb{C}}$-antilinear map $C^\infty(\Pi E)\to C^\infty(\Pi E)$ which provides an isomorphism of supermanifolds $\Pi E\stackrel{\sim}{\to} \overline{\Pi E}$.
<!-- end ex-20 -->
<!-- lem-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:sVect}For any vector bundle ${\mathcal{V}}\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$, there is an isomorphism ${\mathcal{V}} \simeq p^*V$ where $V\to M$ is a vector bundle on $M$.
<!-- end lem-27 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Let $i\colon M\hookrightarrow {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$ denote the inclusion of the reduced manifold. Given a vector bundle ${\mathcal{V}}\to {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$, our candidate for $V\to M$ in the statement is $V:=i^*{\mathcal{V}}$. Indeed, the composition $i\circ p$ is homotopic to the identity on ${\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)$. For example, consider the homotopy ${\mathbb{R}}\times \Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}\to \Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}$ that rescales the odd fibers of $\Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}\to M$ by a scalar $t\in {\mathbb{R}}$; in the functor of points this map is $(t,x,\psi)\mapsto (x,t\psi)$ for $t\in {\mathbb{R}}(S)$ and $(x,\psi)\in \Pi TM_{\mathbb{C}}(S)\simeq {\sf Map}({\mathbb{R}}^{0|1},M)(S)$. Now we use that pullbacks along homotopic maps yield isomorphic vector bundles,
                                                                                                                                 
concluding that $p^*V=p^*i^*{\mathcal{V}}\simeq (i\circ p)^*{\mathcal{V}}$ is isomorphic to~${\mathcal{V}}$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- rmk-38: body_md -->
\label{rmk:extenddown}
The $d=2$ case of conjecture~\eqref{eq:conjecture} requires a generalization of the definitions below to fully-extended $2|1$-dimensional Euclidean field theories of degree~$n$. In particular, this requires that one enhance the $2|1$-Euclidean bordism category to (some flavor of) bicategory that encodes cutting and gluing of $2|1$-Euclidean manifolds with corners. The framework for such a definition is a subject of current investigation, and likely to depart in various ways from prior approaches. Indeed, extending  the definitions in~\cite{ST11} to bicategories internal to symmetric monoidal stacks seems rather unwieldy. At present, smooth bordism categories inspired by iterated Segal spaces seem more tractable, e.g., see~\cite{ClaudiaTheo,GradyPavlov,LudewigStoffel,BEPTFT}.
<!-- end rmk-38 -->
<!-- defn-50: body_md -->
\label{defn:rigid} A \emph{family of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-supermanifolds} is data
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item a smooth submersion $p\colon Y\to S$;
        \item a maximal atlas $\{U_i\}$ of $Y$ equipped with open embeddings $\varphi_i \colon U_i \hookrightarrow S \times {\mathbb{M}}$ over~$S$;
        \item transition data $g_{ij}\colon p(U_i\bigcap U_j)\to G$. 
    \end{enumerate}
The embeddings $\varphi_i$ are required to be compatible with transition data $g_{ij}$ (using the $G$-action on ${\mathbb{M}}$) and the transition data must satisfy a further cocycle condition. 

An \emph{isometry} between $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-families is a pullback $f\colon Y\to Y'$ over a base change $S\to S'$ with the property that the restriction of $f$ to the atlases determining the $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-structures is given by the action of~$G$ on open subspaces of ${\mathbb{M}}$. The collection of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-supermanifolds and isometries defines a stack $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-${\sf SMfld}$ on the site of supermanifolds; see~\cite[\S2.8]{ST11} and~\cite[Remark A.23]{Powerops}.


A \emph{family of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-pairs} is a $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-family $Y\to S$ with a codimension~1 submanifold $Y^c\subset Y$ over $S$ with the property that in a chart for the $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-structure, the image of $U_i\bigcap Y^c\subset U_i$ under  $\varphi_i$ lands in the subspace $S\times {\mathbb{M}}^c\subset S\times {\mathbb{M}}$. Isometries between $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-pairs are isometries of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-supermanifolds $Y\to Y'$ such that $Y^c \subset Y$ is sent to $Y'^c\subset Y'$. This determines a stack on the site of supermanifolds whose objects are $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-pairs.
<!-- end defn-50 -->
<!-- ex-21: body_md -->
\label{ex:modelgeom}
Let ${\mathbb{A}}^d$ be affine $d$-space, regarded as a Riemannian spin manifold. Its group of spin structure preserving isometries is ${\mathbb{R}}^d\rtimes {\rm Spin}(d)$, where ${\rm Spin}(d)$ acts on ${\mathbb{R}}^d$ through the double cover ${\rm Spin}(d)\to {\rm SO}(d)$. The \emph{$d$-dimensional Euclidean geometry} is defined by the triple $(G,{\mathbb{M}},{\mathbb{M}}^c)=({\mathbb{R}}^d\rtimes {\rm Spin}(d),{\mathbb{A}}^d,{\mathbb{A}}^{d-1})$, where ${\mathbb{A}}^{d-1}\subset {\mathbb{A}}^d$ comes from the standard inclusion of a totally geodesic hyperplane; after a choice of basepoint this is the standard inclusion ${\mathbb{R}}^{n-1}\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$. The stack $({\mathbb{R}}^d\rtimes {\rm Spin}(d),{\mathbb{A}}^d)$-${\sf SMfld}$ of $d$-dimensional Euclidean manifolds has as objects fiber bundles $Y\to S$ of $d$-manifolds endowed with flat Riemannian metrics and spin structures. The stack of $d$-dimensional Euclidean pairs has as objects fiber bundles $Y\to S$ of $d$-manifolds endowed with flat Riemannian metrics and spin structures together with a family of totally geodesic codimension~1 submanifolds $Y^c\subset Y$ over~$S$.
<!-- end ex-21 -->
<!-- lem-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:GMaddstructure1}
Fix a rigid geometry $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$. Given a homomorphism $g\colon G\to G$ and a $G$-equivariant map $f\colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ relative to $g$ that preserves the image of the inclusion ${\mathbb{M}}^c\subset {\mathbb{M}}$, there is a uniquely determined map of stacks
$$
F\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld} \to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-}{\sf SMfld}.
$$
<!-- end lem-28 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
The proof is the same argument as~\cite[Lemma 6.19]{HST}. Suppose we are given an $S$-family of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-manifolds $Y\to S$. We obtain a new $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-family $f(Y\to S)$ given by the same fibration $Y\to S$, but where local charts $U_i\subset Y$ are modified by postcomposition with $f$,
$$
Y\supset U\stackrel{\varphi_i}{\hookrightarrow} {\mathbb{M}}\times S\stackrel{f\times {{\rm id}}_S}{\to} {\mathbb{M}}\times S. 
$$
Because $f$ is $G$-equivariant relative to $g$, the gluing data $g^{-1}g_{ij}g$ determines a $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-structure on $Y$. Similarly, because $f$ preserves the image of ${\mathbb{M}}^c\subset {\mathbb{M}}$, it determines an endofunctor on the category of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-pairs. Since the underlying map on the family $Y\to S$ is the identity map, these endofunctors of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-manifolds determine maps of stacks.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- defn-51: body_md -->
\label{defn:realFT}
                                                                                                                                                             
A \emph{real structure} on a rigid geometry $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$ is a real structure on ${\mathbb{M}}^c$, ${\mathbb{M}}$ and $G$ such that all the maps defining the rigid geometry are real in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:realsmfld}.
<!-- end defn-51 -->
<!-- defn-52: body_md -->
\label{defn:internalcat}
A \emph{category ${\sf C}$ internal to symmetric monoidal stacks} is the data of symmetric monoidal stacks ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ of objects and morphisms with source, target, unit, and composition functors
$$
{\sf s},{\sf t}\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\quad {\sf u}\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf C}),\quad {\sf m}\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})} {\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf C})
$$
along with additional coherence data (e.g., associator and unitor) satisfying compatibility properties.
<!-- end defn-52 -->
<!-- defn-53: body_md -->
\label{defn:internalfunctor}
For ${\sf C}$, ${\sf D}$ categories internal to symmetric monoidal stacks, an \emph{internal functor} $F=(F_0,F_1,\mu,\varepsilon)\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ is defined as morphisms of stacks $F_0\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Ob}({\sf D})$, $F_1\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf D})$, and 2-commuting data, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})} {\rm Mor}({\sf C})$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf D})}{\rm Mor}({\sf D})$};
\node (D) at (4,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D})$};
\node (E) at (2,-.75) {$\mu \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {${\sf m}$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$F_1\times F_1 $} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf m}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$F_1$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}
\qquad \begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\rm Ob}({\sf D})$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$};
\node (D) at (4,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D}).$};
\node (E) at (2,-.75) {$\varepsilon \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$F_0$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {${\sf u}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$F_1$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf u}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:internalfunctordiag}
\end{eqnarray}
These data are required to satisfy further properties involving the associators and unitors.
<!-- end defn-53 -->
<!-- defn-54: body_md -->
\label{rmk:twistedcategory}
An \emph{internal natural transformation} $(\eta,\rho)\colon F\Rightarrow G$ between internal functors $F,G\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ is a morphism of stacks $\eta\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf D})$ and 2-commuting data $\rho$
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$};
\node (B) at (6,0) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf D})}{\rm Mor}({\sf D})$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf D})}{\rm Mor}({\sf D})$};
\node (D) at (6,-1.5) {${\rm Mor}({\sf D}).$};
\node (E) at (3,-.75) {$\rho \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$\eta\circ {\sf t} \times F_1$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$G_1\times \eta\circ {\sf s} $} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {${\sf m}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {${\sf m}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{diag:nu}
\end{eqnarray}
These data are required to satisfy additional coherence properties. Define an \emph{isomorphism between internal natural transformations} $(\eta,\rho)\Rightarrow (\eta',\rho')$ as the the data of 2-morphism $\eta\Rightarrow \eta'$ between maps of stacks with respect to which~$\rho$ and~$\rho'$ are compatible.
<!-- end defn-54 -->
<!-- defn-55: body_md -->
\label{defn:superLiecat}
A \emph{super Lie category} is a category internal to supermanifolds whose source and target maps are submersions. For a super Lie category ${\sf C}$, let ${\rm Ob}({\sf C})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf C})$ denote the supermanifolds of objects and morphisms, and let
$$
{\sf u}\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf C}), \ {\sf s},{\sf t},\colon{\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Ob}({\sf C}),\ {\sf c}\colon{\rm Mor}({\sf C})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf C})}{\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf C})
$$
denote the unit, source, target, and composition maps, respectively. A \emph{smooth functor} $F\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ is a pair of maps of supermanifolds $F_0\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Ob}({\sf D})$, $F_1\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf D})$ satisfying the axioms for a functor between categories. A \emph{smooth natural transformation} $\eta\colon F\Rightarrow G$ is a map of supermanifolds $\eta\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf C})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf D})$ satisfying the axioms for a natural transformation between functors. Super Lie categories, smooth functors, and smooth natural transformations form a strict 2-category.
<!-- end defn-55 -->
<!-- ex-22: body_md -->
Any supermanifold determines a discrete super Lie category, i.e., a super Lie category with only identity morphisms.
<!-- end ex-22 -->
<!-- rmk-39: body_md -->
\label{rmk:badcat}
Categories internal to stacks, internal functors, and internal natural transformations are not as well-behaved as one might hope. For example, an internal functor ${\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ that is (appropriately) essentially surjective and fully faithful need not have an inverse functor. For example, let ${\sf C}$ be the \v{C}ech groupoid of an open cover of $X$ and ${\sf D}$ be the (discrete) internal category determined by~$X$; the evident internal functor ${\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ has an inverse internal functor if and only if the cover admits a section. The ``correct" framework for categories internal to stacks therefore requires a localization at an appropriate class of weak equivalences, analogous to the localization relating the 2-category of Lie groupoids with geometric stacks~\cite{Pronk}. For the manipulations in this paper, it suffices to work with categories internal to stacks before such a localization.
<!-- end rmk-39 -->
<!-- defn-56: body_md -->
\label{defn:interinvol}
Fix an involution ${\sf SMfld}\to {\sf SMfld}$ on the category of supermanifolds. For a category ${\sf C}$ internal to (symmetric monoidal) stacks on the site of supermanifolds, an \emph{internal involution} is the data of an internal functor $\tau\colon {\sf C} \to {\sf C}$ covering the fixed involution of supermanifolds, an internal natural isomorphism $\eta \colon {{\rm id}}_{\sf C}\Rightarrow \tau\circ\tau$, and an isomorphism $\delta$ between internal natural isomorphisms $\tau\Rightarrow \tau$ in the diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (B) at (3,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (C) at (6,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (D) at (9,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (E) at (3,.5) {$\eta \ \Downarrow$};
\node (E) at (6,-.5) {$\eta \ \Uparrow$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$\tau$} (B);
\draw[->,bend left] (A) to node [above] {${{\rm id}}_{\sf C}$} (C);
\draw[->,bend right] (B) to node [below] {${{\rm id}}_{\sf C}$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [above] {$\tau$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [above] {$\tau$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
The isomorphism $\delta$ between internal natural transformations satisfies a compatibility condition with $\eta$ for the quadruple composition $\tau\circ\tau\circ\tau\circ\tau$.
<!-- end defn-56 -->
<!-- defn-57: body_md -->
\label{defn:equivariancedata}
Let $({\sf C},\tau_{\sf C},\eta_{\sf C},\delta_{\sf C})$ and $({\sf D},\tau_{\sf D},\eta_{\sf D},\delta_{\sf D})$ be internal categories with internal involution, and let $F\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ be a functor. \emph{Equivariance data} for $F$ is an internal natural transformation~$\phi\colon F\circ \tau_{\sf C}\Rightarrow \tau_{\sf D}\circ F$, i.e., 2-commuting data
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\sf D}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf C}$};
\node (D) at (4,-1.5) {${\sf D}$};
\node (E) at (2,-.75) {$\phi \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$F$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\tau_{\sf C}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$F$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\tau_{\sf D}$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:equivariantfunctor}
\end{eqnarray}
   
                                                                                                                        
   
 
     
                                           
                          
                                                              
                                                                 
                                                    
                                                   
                                             
                                       
                                               
     
and an isomorphism $\beta\colon \phi^2\circ \eta_{\sf C}\rightarrow \eta_{\sf D}$ between internal natural transformations in the diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {${\sf C}$};
\node (B) at (4,0) {${\sf D}$};
\node (C) at (0,-1.5) {${\sf C}$};
\node (D) at (4,-1.5) {${\sf D}$};
\node (F) at (0,-3) {${\sf C}$};
\node (G) at (4,-3) {${\sf D}$};
\node (E) at (2,-.75) {$\phi \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\draw[->,bend right=50] (A) to node [left] {${{\rm id}}_{\sf C}$} (F);
\draw[->,bend left=50] (B) to node [right] {${{\rm id}}_{\sf D}$} (G);
\draw[->] (A) to node [above] {$F$} (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\tau_{\sf C}$} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to node [below] {$F$} (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\tau_{\sf D}$} (D);
\draw[->] (C) to node [left] {$\tau_{\sf C}$} (F);
\draw[->] (F) to node [below] {$F$} (G);
\draw[->] (D) to node [right] {$\tau_{\sf D}$} (G);
\node (H) at (2,-2.25) {$\phi \ \ensuremath{\rotatebox[origin=c]{30}{$\Rightarrow$}}$};
\node (I) at (-.45,-1.5) {$\stackrel{\eta_{\sf C}}{\Rightarrow}$};
\node (I) at (4.45,-1.5) {$\Leftarrow$};
\path (0,-1.5) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:equivariantfunctor2}
\end{eqnarray}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
where $\beta$ is compatible with $\delta_{\sf C}$ and $\delta_{\sf D}$.
<!-- end defn-57 -->
<!-- defn-58: body_md -->
\label{defn:equivariancedata2}
Let  $({\sf C},\tau_{\sf C},\eta_{\sf C},\delta_{\sf C})$ and $({\sf D},\tau_{\sf D},\eta_{\sf D},\delta_{\sf D})$ be internal categories with internal involution, and let $F,G\colon {\sf C}\to {\sf D}$ be internal functors with equivariance data $(\phi_F,\beta_F)$ and $(\phi_G,\beta_G)$. \emph{Equivariance data} for an internal natural transformation $E\colon F\Rightarrow G$ is an isomorphism $\sigma\colon \phi_G\circ E\simeq E\circ \phi_F$  of natural transformations compatible with~$\beta_F$ and~$\beta_G$.
<!-- end defn-58 -->
<!-- defn-59: body_md -->
\label{defn:GBord}
Define a category $(G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)$ internal to symmetric monoidal stacks as follows. 

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent \underline{An object of the stack ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ is an equivalence class of the data:}
\begin{enumerate}
\item a $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-pair $Y^c\subset Y\to S$ where $Y^c\to S$ is proper;
\item a partition into two components $Y^+\coprod Y^-\simeq Y\setminus Y^c\subset Y$; and
\item a map of supermanifolds $\phi\colon Y\to M$.
\end{enumerate}
The supermanifold $Y^c$ is called the \emph{core}. The supermanifold $Y\supset Y^c$ in which the core sits is the \emph{collar}. The collar is partitioned into an \emph{outgoing} component $Y^+$ and an \emph{incoming} component~$Y^-$.
                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
We apply the following equivalence relation to these data: 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:equivalencerelation}
&&(Y^c\subset Y, Y^\pm,\phi)\sim (Y^c\subset Y, Y^\pm,\phi') \iff (\phi)|_{W^+\bigcup Y^c}=(\phi')|_{W^+\bigcup Y^c}
\end{eqnarray}
where $W\subset Y$ is an open submanifold containing $Y^c\subset Y$, and $W^+=W\bigcap Y^+$. In short, we only remember the data of the map $\phi$ on a half-open germ of a neighborhood of $Y^c\subset Y$ of the outgoing collar. We often abbreviate the data of an object of ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ to $\phi\colon Y\to M$. 

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent\underline{A morphism in ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$}, denoted $(Y^c_0\subset Y_0,Y^\pm_0,\phi_0)\to (Y^c_1\subset Y_1,Y^\pm_1,\phi_1)$ is an equivalence class of open submanifolds $V_0\subset Y_0$ and $V_1\subset Y_1$ containing the cores and isometries $f\colon V_0\to V_1$ in the commutative diagram
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (AA) at (-2,0) {$Y_0^c$};
\node (BB) at (-2,-1) {$Y_1^c$};
\node (A) at (0,0) {$V_0$};
\node (B) at (2,0) {$Y_0$};
\node (C) at (0,-1) {$V_1$};
\node (D) at (2,-1) {$Y_1$};
\node (E) at (4,-.5) {$M$.};
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (AA) to (A);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (BB) to (C);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (A) to (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$f$} (C);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (C) to (D);
\draw[->] (AA) to node [left] {$f|_{Y_0^c}$} (BB);
\draw[->] (B) to node [above] {$\phi_0$} (E);
\draw[->] (D) to node [below] {$\phi_1$} (E);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
These data are subject to the equivalence relation that $f\colon V_0\to V_1$ and $f'\colon V_0'\to V_1'$ represent the same isomorphism if $f|_{V_0\bigcap V_0'}=f'|_{V_0\bigcap V_0'}$. 

                                                                                                                                                                                                    
Disjoint union endows ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ with a symmetric monoidal structure. 

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent \underline{An object of the stack ${\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ is given by the data:}
\begin{enumerate}
\item a $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-family $\Sigma\to S$,
\item a map of supermanifolds $\Phi\colon \Sigma\to M$,
\item a pair of objects of ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$, denoted $\phi_{\rm in}\colon Y_{\rm in}\to M$, $\phi_{\rm out}\colon Y_{\rm out}\to M$, 
\item spans of smooth maps $Y_{{\rm out}} \hookleftarrow W_{{\rm out}} \stackrel{i_{{\rm out}}}{\to} \Sigma\stackrel{i_{{\rm in}}}{\leftarrow}  W_{{\rm in}} \hookrightarrow Y_{{\rm in}}$, where $W_{{\rm out}/{\rm in}}\hookrightarrow Y_{{\rm out}/{\rm in}}$ are open embeddings. 
\end{enumerate}
Define the notation
$$
W^{\pm}_{\rm in/out}:= Y^{\pm}_{\rm in/out}\bigcap W_{\rm in/out},\quad i^-_{\rm in}=i_{\rm in}|_{W^-_{\rm in}},\quad  i^-_{\rm out}=i_{\rm out}|_{W^-_{\rm out}}.
$$
Then $\Sigma^c:=\Sigma\setminus (i_{\rm in}(W_{\rm in}^-)\cup i_{\rm out}(W_{\rm out}^+))$ is the \emph{core}. The above data are require to satisfy
\begin{enumerate}
\item the image $W_{\rm in/out}\hookrightarrow Y_{\rm in/out}$ contains a neighborhood of the core $Y^c_{\rm in/out}$;
\item $\Sigma^c\to S$ is proper;
\item $i^-_{\rm in}$ and $i^-_{\rm out}$ are isometries onto their image in $\Sigma\setminus i_{\rm out}(W_{\rm out}^+\cup Y_{\rm out}^c)$; and
\item the maps $\phi_{\rm in/out}\colon Y_{\rm in/out} \to M$ are compatible with $\Phi\colon \Sigma\to M$. 
\end{enumerate}
Similar to~\eqref{eq:equivalencerelation}, we impose an equivalence relation on objects
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:equivalencerelation2}
&&(\Sigma,Y_{\rm in},Y_{\rm out},\Phi_1)\sim (\Sigma,Y_{\rm in},Y_{\rm out},\Phi_2)\iff (\Phi_1)|_{W^+_{\rm out}\bigcup \Sigma^c}=(\Phi_2)|_{W^+_{\rm out}\bigcup \Sigma^c}
\end{eqnarray}
so again the equivalence class of $\Phi$ is only the data of a half-open neighborhood of the core $\Sigma^c\to M$ inside the outgoing collar. 

\vspace{.1in}

                                                                                                                                    
\noindent\underline{A morphism in ${\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$} is an equivalence classes of open sub supermanifolds $\Omega_i\subset \Sigma_i$, $V_{i,{\rm in}}\subset Y_{i,{\rm in}}$, $V_{i,{\rm out}}\subset Y_{i,{\rm out}}$ satisfying
$$
\Sigma_i^c\subset \Omega_i\subset \Sigma_i,\quad Y_{i,{\rm in}}^c\subset V_{i,{\rm in}}\subset W_{i,{\rm in}}\bigcap i^{-1}_{\rm in}(\Omega_i)\subset Y_{i,{\rm in}},\quad Y_{i,{\rm out}}^c\subset V_{i,{\rm out}}\subset W_{i,{\rm out}}\bigcap i^{-1}_{\rm out}(\Omega_i)\subset Y_{i,{\rm out}}
$$ 
and isometries $f_{\rm in} \colon V_{0,{\rm in}}\to V_{1,{\rm in}}$, $f_{\rm out} \colon V_{0,{\rm out}}\to V_{1,{\rm out}}$ and $F\colon \Omega_0\to \Omega_1$ in the commutative diagram of supermanifolds over $M$
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (-2,0) {$Y_{0,{\rm out}}^c$};
\node (B) at (-2,-1) {$Y_{1,{\rm out}}^c$};
\node (C) at (0,0) {$V_{0,{\rm out}}$};
\node (D) at (2,0) {$\Omega_0$};
\node (E) at (0,-1) {$V_{1,{\rm out}}$};
\node (F) at (2,-1) {$\Omega_1$};
\node (G) at (6,0) {$Y_{0,{\rm in}}^c$};
\node (H) at (6,-1) {$Y_{1,{\rm in}}^c$};
\node (I) at (4,0) {$V_{0,{\rm in}}$};
\node (J) at (4,-1) {$V_{1,{\rm in}}$};
\draw[->] (G) to node [right] {$f_{\rm in}|_{Y_{0,{\rm out}}^c}$} (H);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$f_{\rm out}|_{Y_{0,{\rm in}}^c}$} (B);
\draw[->,left hook-latex] (C) to (A);
\draw[->,left hook-latex] (E) to (B);
\draw[->] (E) to (F);
\draw[->] (C) to (D);
\draw[->] (I) to (D);
\draw[->] (J) to (F);
\draw[->] (C) to node [left] {$f_{\rm out}$} (E);
\draw[->] (I) to node [left] {$f_{\rm in}$} (J);
\draw[->] (D) to node [left] {$F$} (F);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (I) to (G);
\draw[->,right hook-latex] (J) to (H);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:dataofmorphismofmorphism}
\end{eqnarray}
where we also require $F$ preserves the core of the bordism, $F|_{\Sigma^c_0}\colon \Sigma^c_0\to \Sigma_1^c\subset \Omega_1$. These data are equivalent~$(f,g,F)\sim (f',g',F')$ when
$$
f_{\rm in} |_{V_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_{0,{\rm in}}'}=f'_{\rm in} |_{V_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_{0,{\rm in}}'},\quad f_{\rm out} |_{V_{0,{\rm out}}\bigcap V_{0,{\rm out}}'}=f'_{\rm in} |_{V_{0,{\rm out}}\bigcap V_{0,{\rm out}}'},\quad F|_{\Omega_0\bigcap \Omega_0'}=F'|_{\Omega_0\bigcap \Omega_0'}.
$$
Disjoint union endows ${\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ with a symmetric monoidal structure. We often abbreviate the data of an object of ${\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))$ to $Y_{\rm in}\coprod Y_{\rm out} \to \Sigma\xrightarrow{\Phi} M$, or even more succinctly to $\Phi\colon \Sigma\to M$. 

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent \underline{Unit, source, and target functors} are given by the assignments on objects
$$
{\sf u}(Y\to M)=(Y\coprod Y\stackrel{{\rm fold}}{\to} Y\to M), \qquad {\sf s}(Y_{\rm in}\coprod Y_{\rm out} \to \Sigma\to M)=(Y_{\rm in}\to M)
$$
$$
{\sf t}(Y_{\rm in}\coprod Y_{\rm out} \to \Sigma\to M)=(Y_{\rm out}\to M),
$$
with similar assignments on morphisms. For any $S$, let $\emptyset\in {\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))(S)$ and $\emptyset\in {\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))(S)$ denote the empty object over~$S$, i.e., the symmetric monoidal unit over~$S$ for these symmetric monoidal stacks. 


\vspace{.1in}

\noindent \underline{Composition} is given by gluing bordisms along collars; see~\cite[page~20]{ST11} and \cite[Definition~6.5]{HST}.
<!-- end defn-59 -->
<!-- lem-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:isofibration}
The source and target functors 
$$
{\sf s},{\sf t}\colon {\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))\to {\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))
$$ 
are fibrations of stacks.
<!-- end lem-29 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
We recall that a map of stacks is a fibration if it induces a fibration of groupoids over each supermanifold $S$, e.g., see~\cite{Hollander}. We prove the statement of the lemma for the functor ${\sf s}$; the case for ${\sf t}$ is similar. 
It suffices to show that for any isomorphism~$f\colon {\sf s}(\Sigma_0,\Phi_0)\to (Y_1,\phi_1)$ in ${\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M'))(S)$ where
$$
(Y_1,\phi_1)\in {\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M'))(S), \quad (\Sigma_0,\Phi_0)\in {\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M'))(S),
$$ 
there exists an isomorphism $(f,g,F)\colon (\Sigma_0,\Phi_0)\to (\Sigma_1,\Phi_1)$ in ${\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M'))(S)$ with ${\sf s}(f,g,F)=f$. We recall that the notation $\Sigma_0$ for a cobordism is an abbreviation for the data 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:olddata}
(Y_{0,{\rm out}} \hookleftarrow W_{0,{\rm out}} \stackrel{i_{0,{\rm out}}}{\hookrightarrow} \Sigma_0\stackrel{i_{0,{\rm in}}}{\hookleftarrow}  W_{0,{\rm in}} \hookrightarrow Y_{0,{\rm in}},\Phi_0\colon \Sigma_0\to M).
\end{eqnarray}
Similarly, $f\colon {\sf s}(\Sigma_0,\Phi_0)\to (Y_1,\phi_1)$ is an abbreviation for the data of open sub supermanifolds $V_0\subset Y_0$, $V_1\subset Y_1$ containing the core and an isometry $f\colon V_0\to V_1$ preserving the cores. 

Using the notation above, we define $(\Sigma_1,\Phi_1)$ by the data 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:newdata}
(Y_{0,{\rm out}} \hookleftarrow W_{0,{\rm out}} \stackrel{i_{0,{\rm out}}}{\hookrightarrow} \Sigma_0\stackrel{i_{0,{\rm in}}\circ f^{-1}}{\hookleftarrow}  f(W_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_0) \hookrightarrow Y_{1},\Phi_0\colon \Sigma_0\to M).
\end{eqnarray}
where the relevant properties are inherited from~\eqref{eq:olddata}. 
Next define an isomorphism $(\Sigma_0,\Phi_0)\to (\Sigma_1,\Phi_1)$ by taking $V_{0,{\rm out}}=V_{1,{\rm out}}=W_{{\rm out}}$, $\Omega_0=\Omega_1=\Sigma_0$, $V_{0,{\rm in}}=W_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_0$, $V_{1,{\rm in}}=f(W_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_0)$, $f_{\rm out}={{\rm id}}_{W_{{\rm out}}}$, $F={{\rm id}}_{\Sigma_0}$ and $f_{\rm in}=f|_{W_{0,{\rm in}}\bigcap V_0}$. By construction, the diagram~\eqref{eq:dataofmorphismofmorphism} commutes with this data and the requisite properties are satisfied to define an isomorphism in ${\rm Mor}(1|1\hbox{-}{\sf EBord}(M))$. The source functor applied to this isomorphism agrees with $(f,V_0,V_1)$ on restriction to $V_0\bigcap W_{0,{\rm in}}$ and $f(V_0\bigcap W_{0,{\rm in}})$, so this morphism is equal to~$f$ because morphisms are defined as equivalence classes. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lem-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:naturalityofGBord}
A map $f\colon M\to M'$ of smooth manifolds induces an internal functor 
$$
f_*\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M'),\qquad \begin{array}{ccc} (\phi\colon Y\to M) & \mapsto & (f\circ \phi\colon Y\to M') \\ (\Phi\colon \Sigma\to M)&\mapsto & (f\circ \Phi\colon \Sigma\to M')\end{array}
$$ 
and these internal functors are compatible with composition of maps between manifolds.
<!-- end lem-30 -->
<!-- defn-60: body_md -->
\label{defn:TV}
Define the category~${\sf {Vect}}$ internal to symmetric monoidal stacks as follows. The stack ${\rm Ob}({\sf {Vect}})$ classifies bundles of ${\mathbb{Z}}/2$-graded, nuclear Fr\'echet spaces over~${\mathbb{C}}$, i.e., locally free sheaves of nuclear Fr\'echet super vector spaces. The stack ${\rm Mor}({\sf {Vect}})$ has objects maps between vector bundles, and as morphisms commuting squares 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$V$};
\node (B) at (3,0) {$W$};
\node (C) at (0,-1) {$V'$};
\node (D) at (3,-1) {$W'$};
\draw[->] (A) to (B);
\draw[->] (A) to node [left] {$\simeq $} (C);
\draw[->] (C) to (D);
\draw[->] (B) to node [right] {$\simeq$} (D);
\path (0,-.75) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{diag:unitary}
\end{eqnarray}
whose horizontal arrows are maps of vector bundles and whose vertical arrows are fiberwise isomorphisms of vector bundles, i.e., pullbacks along base changes. There are functors ${\sf s,t}\colon {\rm Mor}({\sf {Vect}})\to {\rm Ob}({\sf {Vect}})$ from restricting to the left and right halves of the square~\eqref{diag:unitary}. Finally, endow ${\rm Ob}({\sf {Vect}})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf {Vect}})$ with symmetric monoidal structures from the projective tensor product of topological vector bundles.
<!-- end defn-60 -->
<!-- rmk-40: body_md -->
The above deviates from the definition in~\cite{ST11} in two ways. First, we only work with vector bundles rather than general sheaves of topological vector spaces (i.e., we impose a locally free condition). Second, we specialize from general locally convex topological vector spaces to nuclear Fr\'echet spaces. We make this choice in order to guarantee that certain formal categorical structures in the functorial definition of quantum field theory agree with standard structures in physics: Fr\'echet spaces have the \emph{approximation property}~\cite[page~109]{Schaefer}, leading to a well-behaved theory for traces of nuclear operators, see~\cite[\S4.5]{STTraces}. It also happens that all the desired constructions in index theory result in vector bundles of nuclear Fr\'echet spaces, so this restriction does not any exclude any of the desired examples. We refer to~\cite[Appendix~2]{costbook} for a succinct overview of nuclear Fr\'echet spaces. Stolz and Teichner's motivation to work with more general sheaves of topological vector spaces is explained in Remark~\ref{rmk:concordance}.
<!-- end rmk-40 -->
<!-- defn-61: body_md -->
\label{defn:Morita}
Define the \emph{internal Morita category}~${\sf {Alg}}$ as a category internal to symmetric monoidal stacks as follows. The stack ${\rm Ob}({\sf {Alg}})$ classifies locally trivial bundles of nuclear Fr\'echet super algebras and isomorphisms of algebra bundles. The stack ${\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$ classifies locally trivial bundles of nuclear Fr\'echet bimodules over topological algebras. Composition comes from the projective tensor product of bimodule bundles,
$$
{\sf c} \colon {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})\times_{{\rm Ob}({\sf {Alg}})}{\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}}),\qquad {\sf c}(B,B')=B\otimes_A B'.
$$ 
Viewing an algebra bundle as a bimodule over itself constructs the unit map ${\sf u}\colon {\rm Ob}({\sf {Alg}})\to {\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$. Endow ${\rm Ob}({\sf {Alg}})$ and ${\rm Mor}({\sf {Alg}})$ with monoidal structures from the projective tensor product of algebra and bimodule bundles over the structure sheaf of the base.
<!-- end defn-61 -->
<!-- ex-23: body_md -->
\label{ex:one} Given any category ${\sf C}$ internal to symmetric monoidal stacks, there is an internal functor
$$
\mathbbold{1} \colon {\sf C}\to {\sf {Alg}}
$$
defined as follows. For $Y\in {\rm Ob}({\sf C})(S)$, assign the trivial algebra bundle on~$S$, i.e., the sheaf of algebras whose global sections are $C^\infty(S)$. For $\Sigma\in {\rm Mor}({\sf C})(S)$, assign the trivial bimodule bundle over $S$, i.e., the sheaf of bimodules whose global sections are $C^\infty(S)$ as a bimodule over $C^\infty(S)$. The 2-commuting data $\mu$ is determined by the canonical isomorphism $C^\infty(S)\otimes_{C^\infty(S)} C^\infty(S)\simeq C^\infty(S)$, while the 2-commuting data~$\epsilon$ comes from the canonical identification of the algebra $C^\infty(S)$ with the identity bimodule over itself.
<!-- end ex-23 -->
<!-- defn-62: body_md -->
\label{defn:FTmain}
A \emph{geometric field theory over $M$} is an internal functor
\begin{eqnarray}
E\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to {\sf {Vect}}.\label{eq:GFT}
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-62 -->
<!-- defn-63: body_md -->
\label{defn:FTmain2}
A \emph{twisted geometric field theory over $M$} is an internal natural transformation~$E$
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(basepoint)];
\node (A) at (0,0) {$(G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)$};
\node (B) at (5,0) {${\sf {Alg}}$};
\node (C) at (2.5,0) {$E \Downarrow$};
\draw[->,bend left=15] (A) to node [above] {$\mathbbold{1}$} (B);
\draw[->,bend right=15] (A) to node [below] {$\mathscr{T}$} (B);
\path (0,0) coordinate (basepoint);
\end{tikzpicture}\label{eq:twistedGFT}
\end{eqnarray}
where $\mathscr{T}$ is a \emph{twist functor} and $\mathbbold{1}$ is defined in Example~\ref{ex:one}. Twisted field theories are the objects of a groupoid whose morphisms are isomorphisms between internal natural transformations.
<!-- end defn-63 -->
<!-- rmk-41: body_md -->
An (untwisted) geometric field theory in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:FTmain} determines a twisted field theory in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:FTmain2} for the trivial twist functor $\mathscr{T}=\mathbbold{1}$~\cite[Lemma~5.7]{ST11}.
<!-- end rmk-41 -->
<!-- lem-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:GMaddstructure}
Fix a rigid geometry $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$. Given a homomorphism $g\colon G\to G$ and a $G$-equivariant map $f\colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ relative to $g$ that preserves the image of the inclusion ${\mathbb{M}}^c\subset {\mathbb{M}}$, there is a uniquely determined internal functor
$$
F\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M). 
$$
<!-- end lem-31 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
The endofunctors of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-manifolds from Lemma~\ref{lem:GMaddstructure1} determine maps of stacks,
$$
F_0\colon {\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))\to {\rm Ob}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)), \quad (Y\to S,\phi)\mapsto (f(Y\to S),\phi) $$$$ F_1\colon {\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M))\to {\rm Mor}((G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)),\quad (\Sigma\to M,\Phi)\mapsto (f(\Sigma\to M),\Phi),
$$
by taking the same collar data on bordisms, but different $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-structures. 
By construction, these maps of stacks are (strictly) compatible with source, target, unit, and composition functors defining $(G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- ex-24: body_md -->
\label{ex:flips}
In the context of Lemma~\ref{lem:GMaddstructure}, suppose that ${\sf fl} \colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ is an involution commuting with the action of $G$ and preserving ${\mathbb{M}}^c\subset {\mathbb{M}}$. This endows every family of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-manifolds with an involution. In practice, an involution ${\sf fl}\colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ comes from a \emph{spin flip} automorphism, e.g., see~\cite[\S6.7, Lemma 6.39]{HST},~\cite[Example~2.39 and \S4.1]{ST11} and~\eqref{eq:spinflipfor11}. Following~\cite[\S2.6]{ST11}, such an involution~${\sf fl}$ allows one to regard the bordism category as a category internal to symmetric monoidal stacks with involution.
<!-- end ex-24 -->
<!-- defn-64: body_md -->
\label{defn:flips}
                                                                                                                                                                                
Fix a rigid geometry $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$ with an involution ${\sf fl}\colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ as in Example~\ref{ex:flips}.  A \emph{flip-preserving geometric field theory} is a functor~\eqref{eq:GFT} internal to the category of symmetric monoidal stacks with involution. Similarly, one defines \emph{flip-preserving twists} and \emph{flip-preserving twisted geometric field theories} as functors and natural transformations internal to symmetric monoidal stacks with involution.
<!-- end defn-64 -->
<!-- ex-25: body_md -->
\label{ex:orientationGM}
Fix an orientation on the manifold ${\mathbb{M}}_{\rm red}$, and suppose that ${\sf or} \colon {\mathbb{M}}\to {\mathbb{M}}$ is a $G$-equivariant map with the property that ${\sf or}_{\rm red}\colon {\mathbb{M}}_{\rm red}\to {\mathbb{M}}_{\rm red}$ is an orientation reversing map and ${\sf or}^2={\sf fl}$ is the spin flip. Then Lemma~\ref{lem:GMaddstructure} determines an \emph{orientation reversal functor}
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf Or}\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\label{eq:orientationreversalGM}
\end{eqnarray}
with a natural isomorphism ${\sf Or}\circ {\sf Or}\Rightarrow {{\rm id}}$ (via the spin flip). Indeed, ${\sf Or}$ determines an internal involution in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:interinvol}.
<!-- end ex-25 -->
<!-- ex-26: body_md -->
\label{ex:realGM}
Given an $S$-family of $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-supermanifolds $(Y\to S)$, a real structure on the rigid geometry $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$ gives a unique $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$-stucture for the $\overline{S}$-family $(\overline{Y}\to \overline{S})$. This extends to an internal functor 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\sf R}\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M),\qquad (S\leftarrow Y\to M)\mapsto (\overline{S}\leftarrow \overline{Y}\to \overline{M}\simeq M).\label{eq:realstru}
\end{eqnarray}
The identification $\overline{M}\simeq M$ uses that $M$ is an ordinary manifold, and hence has a canonical real structure when regarded as a supermanifold. Via the forgetful functor $(G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to {\sf SMfld}$ that sends an $S$-family of bordisms to $S$, the internal functor~\eqref{eq:realstru} covers the conjugation functor on supermanifolds. We observe that ${\sf R}$ determines an internal involution in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:interinvol}.
<!-- end ex-26 -->
<!-- defn-65: body_md -->
\label{defn:RP0}
Let $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$ be a rigid geometry with a chosen real structure and orientation reversing automorphism. 
A \emph{reflection structure} for a twist $\mathscr{T}$ is equivariance data for the involutions ${\sf R}\circ {\sf Or}$ and $(\overline{\phantom{-}})$.
