                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
A \emph{reflection structure} for a twisted field theory $E\colon \mathbbold{1}\to \mathscr{T}$ is equivariance data for the internal natural transformation $E$.
<!-- end defn-65 -->
<!-- rmk-42: body_md -->
Roughly, a reflection structure stipulates that orientation reversal of bordisms correspond to complex conjugation of vector spaces (which is data). In tandem with this structure is the \emph{reflection positivity property}, which demands that a certain hermitian pairing is positive. Suggestively we write this pairing as
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:ahermpairing}
\overline{E(Y)}\otimes E(Y) \stackrel{h\otimes {{\rm id}}}{\simeq} E(\overline{Y})\otimes E(Y) \stackrel{E(\Sigma)}{\to} {\mathbb{C}}
\end{eqnarray}
where the isomorphism $h$ comes from the reflection structure, and $\Sigma$ is a bordism with boundary $\overline{Y}\coprod Y$ where $Y$ is the orientation reversal of $Y$. Then the positivity property is the positivity of the pairing~\eqref{eq:ahermpairing}. 
                                                                                                                                                       
We provide the precise property for $1|1$-Euclidean field theories in Definition~\ref{defn:RPFT}.
<!-- end rmk-42 -->
<!-- defn-66: body_md -->
\label{defn:Real0}
Let $(G,{\mathbb{M}})$ be a rigid geometry with a chosen real structure, and $\mathscr{T}\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to {\sf {Alg}}$. A \emph{real structure} for $\mathscr{T}$ is equivariance data for the involutions ${\sf R}$ and $(\overline{\phantom{-}})$. Given a twisted field theory $E\colon \mathbbold{1}\to \mathscr{T}$, a \emph{real structure} on $E$ is equivariance data for the internal natural transformation.
<!-- end defn-66 -->
<!-- ex-27: body_md -->
\label{ex:RGgeneral}
In many cases, there is a nontrivial ${\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$-action on ${\mathbb{M}}$ that commutes with the $G$-action. For example, the Euclidean rigid geometries from Example~\ref{ex:modelgeom} admit such a structure from the standard dilation action on ${\mathbb{R}}^d$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:GMaddstructure}, this leads to the action of the \emph{renormalization group},
\begin{eqnarray}
{\sf RG}^\mu\colon (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\to (G,{\mathbb{M}})\hbox{-{\sf Bord}}(M)\qquad \mu\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0},\label{eq:generalRG}
\end{eqnarray}
which then acts on the category of (twisted) field theories by precomposition with the internal functor~\eqref{eq:generalRG}.
<!-- end ex-27 -->
<!-- defn-67: body_md -->
\label{defn:superconn}
Let $V\to M$ be a complex vector bundle. A \emph{superconnection}~${\mathbb{A}}$ on $V$ is an odd, ${\mathbb{C}}$-linear map of Fr\'echet spaces satisfying a Leibniz rule
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\mathbb{A}}\colon \Omega^\bullet(M;V)\to \Omega^\bullet(M;V),\quad {\mathbb{A}}(\alpha\cdot v)=d\alpha \cdot v+(-1)^{|\alpha|} \alpha \cdot {\mathbb{A}} v\label{eq:ordsuperconn}
\end{eqnarray}
where $v\in \Omega^\bullet(M;V)$ and $\alpha\in \Omega^\bullet(M)$.
<!-- end defn-67 -->
<!-- defn-68: body_md -->
Suppose that $\langle-,-\rangle\colon\overline{V}\otimes V\to \underline{{\mathbb{C}}}$ is a (super) hermitian pairing, where~$\otimes$ is the projective tensor product. Then a superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on $V$ is \emph{self-adjoint} if 
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle \overline{{\mathbb{A}}}_1x,y\rangle+(-1)^{|x||y|}\langle x,{\mathbb{A}}_1y\rangle=d\langle x,y\rangle,\qquad {\mathbb{A}}_{k}^*=i^{k+1}\overline{{\mathbb{A}}}_k,\label{eq:supersa}
\end{eqnarray}
where ${\mathbb{A}}_k^*$ is the super adjoint of ${\mathbb{A}}_k$.
<!-- end defn-68 -->
<!-- rmk-43: body_md -->
Translating from super adjoints to ordinary adjoints as in~\eqref{eq:superadjointtrans}, the above is equivalent to the standard definition of self-adjoint superconnection~\cite[page 117]{BGV}.
<!-- end rmk-43 -->
<!-- defn-69: body_md -->
\label{defn:chernform}
The \emph{Chern form} of a ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnnection is the Clifford super trace (which need not exist for infinite rank bundles)
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:theChernchar}
{\rm Ch}({\mathbb{A}}):={\sf sTr}_{{\mathbb{C}}{\rm l}_n}(e^{-u{\mathbb{A}}(u)^2})\in \Omega^\bullet(M;{\mathbb{C}}[u^{\pm 2}])).
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end defn-69 -->
<!-- lem-32: body_md -->
When it exists, the Chern form of a ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ is closed and has total degree $n$.
<!-- end lem-32 -->
<!-- defn-70: body_md -->
A \emph{topological category} is a category in which the objects and morphisms are topological spaces for which the structure maps (source, target, unit, composition) are continuous. For a topological category $\mathcal{C}$, let~$\mathcal{C}_0$ denote the space of objects and $\mathcal{C}_1$ the space of morphisms.
<!-- end defn-70 -->
<!-- defn-71: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the category whose objects are finite-dimensional ${\rm Cl}_{n}$-submodules $W\subset \mathcal{H}_n$ and whose morphisms are
\begin{eqnarray}
&&{\rm Mor}(W_0,W_1):=\left\{ \begin{array}{cl} \begin{array}{c} {\rm Cl}_{n}\otimes {\rm Cl}_{-1}-{\rm action\ on\ } W_0^\perp \\ {\rm extending\ the }\ {\rm Cl}_{n}{\rm-action}\end{array}  & {\rm if} \ W_0\subseteq W_1\subset \mathcal{H}_n \\
\null\\
\emptyset & {\rm else} \end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray}
where $W_0^\perp\subseteq W_1$ denotes the orthogonal complement of the subspace $W_0\subseteq W_1$. Composition for a nested inclusion $W_0\subseteq W_1\subseteq W_2$ uses the direct sum of Clifford modules to obtain a ${\rm Cl}_{n}\otimes {\rm Cl}_{-1}$-module structure on the orthogonal complement of $W_0\subseteq W_2$. Endow the objects and morphisms of $\mathcal{M}_n$ with the subspace topology for the embeddings
\begin{eqnarray}
{\rm Obj}(\mathcal{M}_n)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_n),\qquad {\rm Mor}(\mathcal{M}_n)\hookrightarrow \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_n)^{\times 3} \label{eq:bddops}
\end{eqnarray}
where the first inclusion identifies a submodule $W_0\subset \mathcal{H}_n$ with the (finite-rank) projection~$\mathcal{H}_n\to W_0$. For the second inclusion, a triple $(W_0,W_1,e)$ determines a pair of finite rank projection operators and a bounded operator~$e$.
<!-- end defn-71 -->
<!-- defn-72: body_md -->
The \emph{nerve} of a topological category $\mathcal{C}$ is the simplicial space whose $k$-simplices are $N_k\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}_k$ for $k=0,1$, and for $k>1$ are length $k$ chains of composable morphisms
\begin{eqnarray}
N_k\mathcal{C}&=&\{x_0\stackrel{f_1}{\to}x_1\stackrel{f_2}{\to}x_2\stackrel{f_3}{\to}\cdots \stackrel{f_k}{\to}x_k\mid x_i\in \mathcal{C}_0, f_i\in \mathcal{C}_1\}\nonumber\\&=&\mathcal{C}_1\times_{\mathcal{C}_0}\cdots \times_{\mathcal{C}_0} \mathcal{C}_1,\nonumber 
\end{eqnarray}
topologized as the fibered product.
                                                                                                                                       
The face maps in  $N_\bullet \mathcal{C}$ are determined by composing morphisms, and degeneracies are determined by the unit map in $\mathcal{C}$.
<!-- end defn-72 -->
<!-- prop-28: body_md -->
\label{prop:ABScat}
The classifying space ${\rm B} \mathcal{M}_n$ represents the functor ${\rm KO}^{n}(-)$.
<!-- end prop-28 -->
<!-- defn-73: body_md -->
\label{ex:opencover0}
For $Z$ a topological space and $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ an open cover, the \emph{\v{C}ech category}, denoted $\check{{\rm C}}(U_i)$, is the topological category whose objects are $\check{{\rm C}}(U_i)_0=\coprod_{\sigma} U_\sigma$ and whose morphisms are the space $\check{{\rm C}}(U_i)_1=\coprod_{\sigma\subseteq \tau} U_\tau$. The source and target maps are determined by the projection and inclusion $U_\tau\subseteq U_\sigma$, the unit is induced by the identity map $U_\sigma \to U_\sigma$, and composition comes from nested inclusions.
<!-- end defn-73 -->
<!-- lem-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:Cechrealize}
                                                                                                                                    
   
                                                                                                         
   
                  
For $Z$ a topological space and $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ an open cover, the canonical map 
\begin{eqnarray}
{\rm B} \check{C}(U_i)\stackrel{\sim}{\to} Z,\label{eq:Segalwe}
\end{eqnarray} 
is a homotopy equivalence.
<!-- end lem-33 -->
<!-- defn-74: body_md -->
A \emph{${\rm Cl}_n$-bundle} on a manifold $M$ is data 
\begin{enumerate}
\item an open cover $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ of $M$,
\item for each finite subset $\sigma \subset I$, a metrized super vector bundle $W_\sigma\to U_\sigma$ with ${\rm Cl}_n$-action such that the fibers of $W_\sigma$ are self-adjoint ${\rm Cl}_n$-modules;
\item for each $\sigma\subset \tau$, a ${\rm Cl}_n$-equivariant, injective map of super vector bundles $g_{\sigma\tau}\colon W_\tau\hookrightarrow W_\sigma$, together with a ${\rm Cl}_{n}\otimes {\rm Cl}_{-1}$-action on $W_\tau^\perp\subset W_\sigma$ on the orthogonal complement of the image extending the ${\rm Cl}_n$-action.
\end{enumerate}
For $\sigma\subset \tau\subset \rho $, we require an equality of maps $g_{\sigma\tau}\circ g_{\tau\rho}=g_{\sigma\rho}\colon W_\rho\hookrightarrow W_\sigma$, and  that the ${\rm Cl}_{-1}$-action on $W_\rho^\perp\subset W_\tau \hookrightarrow W_\sigma$ restricts from the ${\rm Cl}_{-1}$-action on~$W_\tau^\perp\subset W_\sigma$.
<!-- end defn-74 -->
<!-- cor-7: body_md -->
\label{eq:cormaptoKO}
Given a ${\rm Cl}_n$-bundle on $M$, there exists a continuous functor
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:constructtoKO}
 \check{{\rm C}}(U_i)\to \mathcal{M}_n
\end{eqnarray}
that is unique up to a contractible space of choices. After realization, this determines a map $M\to B\mathcal{M}_n\simeq {\rm KO}^n$ into the $n$th space of ${\rm KO}$ spectrum.
<!-- end cor-7 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
The functor~\eqref{eq:constructtoKO} comes from choosing a ${\rm Cl}_n$-equivariant embedding $W_\sigma\subset \mathcal{H}_n\times U_\sigma$ over $U_\sigma$ for each $\sigma\subset I$. By Kuiper's theorem~\cite{Kuiper}, the space of such choices is contractible. Then the corollary follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:ABScat} and Lemma~\ref{lem:Cechrealize}.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lem-34: body_md -->
\label{prop:CechdeRham}
Given a ${\rm Cl}_n$ bundle on $M$, choices of self-adjoint ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnections ${\mathbb{A}}_\sigma$ on each $W_\sigma$ uniquely determine a \v{C}ech--de~Rham representative of the Pontryagin character ${\rm Ch}(W)\in {\rm H}^\bullet(M;{\mathbb{R}}[u,u^{-1}])$ of $[W]=[\{U_\sigma,W_\sigma,g_{\sigma\tau},e_{\sigma\tau}\}]\in {\rm KO}^n(M)$.
<!-- end lem-34 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Over each $U_i$, a choice of superconnection on $W_i$ gives a differential form ${\rm Ch}_n({\mathbb{A}}_i)\in \Omega^\bullet(U_i;{\mathbb{R}}[u,u^{-1}])$ of total degree~$n$. The data $g_{\sigma\tau},e_{\sigma\tau}$ allow one to extend this to a \v{C}ech--de~Rham cocycle.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- defn-75: body_md -->
\label{defn:superconngeneral}
A \emph{differential refinement} of a ${\rm Cl}_n$-bundle $V=\{V_\sigma,g_{\sigma\tau},e_{\sigma\tau}\}$ defined relative to an open cover $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ is data
\begin{enumerate}
\item[i.] for each $\sigma\subset I$, a self-adjoint ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}_\sigma$ on $V_\sigma\to U_\sigma$, and
\item[ii.] a closed global form $ {\rm Ch}(V,{\mathbb{A}},\phi)\in \Omega^\bullet(M;{\mathbb{R}}[\alpha^{\pm 1}])$ of total degree~$n$;
\item[iii.] a coboundary $\{\phi_\sigma\in \Omega^\bullet(U_\sigma;{\mathbb{R}}[\alpha^{\pm 1}])\}$ between ${\rm Ch}(V,{\mathbb{A}},\phi)$ and the \v{C}ech--de~Rham cocycle ${\rm Ch}_n(\{U_i\},{\mathbb{A}}_i)\in \Omega^\bullet(U_*;{\mathbb{R}}[u^{\pm 1}])$ in Lemma~\ref{prop:CechdeRham}.
\end{enumerate}
A differential refinement of a ${\rm Cl}_n$-bundle is a \emph{differential cocycle} denoted by $(V,{\mathbb{A}},\phi)=\{(V_\sigma,{\mathbb{A}}_\sigma,\phi_\sigma),(g_{\sigma\tau},e_{\sigma\tau})\}$.
<!-- end defn-75 -->
<!-- defn-76: body_md -->
\label{defn:superconncutoff}
A self-adjoint Clifford linear superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ \emph{admits smooth index bundles} if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item the collection of subsets $\{U_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:Ulambda2} form a smooth open cover;
\item the subsets $\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}\subset \mathcal{H}|_{U_\lambda}\to U_\lambda$ are smooth vector bundles;
\item the composition defines a smooth connection:
$$
\nabla^{<\lambda}:=p^\lambda\circ {\mathbb{A}}^{[1]}|_{U_\lambda}\circ p^\lambda\colon \Gamma(\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda})\to \Omega^1(U_\lambda;\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}),
$$
\item the limit of Chern--Simons forms
\begin{eqnarray}
\eta_{\lambda}(t):=\lim_{r\to \infty} \int_1^r {\sf sTr}_{{\rm Cl}_n}(\frac{d{\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)}{ds}\exp({\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)))ds \in \Omega^\bullet(U_\lambda ;C^\infty({\mathbb{R}}_{>0})[u^{\pm 1}])\label{eq:improperintegral}
\end{eqnarray}
exists and satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:satisfies}
d\eta_\lambda(t)={\rm Ch}({\mathbb{A}}(t))|_{U_\lambda}-{\rm Ch}(\nabla^{<\lambda})
\end{eqnarray}
where in~\eqref{eq:improperintegral}, ${\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)$ is the 1-parameter family of superconnnections on $V|_{U_\lambda} \oplus \Pi \mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}$,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:nullconcordFT}
&&{\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)={\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)^{[0]}+{\mathbb{A}}^{[1]} \oplus \nabla^{<\lambda} +\sum_{i>1} s^{-i} {\mathbb{A}}^{[i]} \oplus 0_{\Pi \mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}},\quad {\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}(s)^{[0]}=\left[\begin{array}{cc} {\mathbb{A}}^{[0]} & s\cdot i_\lambda \\ s \cdot p^\lambda & 0 \end{array}\right]
\end{eqnarray}
where $i_\lambda$ and $p^\lambda$ are the maps~\eqref{eq:fiberwiseincludeproject}.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-76 -->
<!-- prop-29: body_md -->
\label{prop:appenindexbundle}
Given a ${\rm Cl}_n$-linear superconnection admitting cutoffs, a choice of locally finite open cover $\{U_\lambda\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ associated with a discrete subset $\Lambda\subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ determines a map 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:KOindexspec}
{\rm Ind}_\Lambda({\mathbb{A}})\colon M\to {\rm KO}^n,
\end{eqnarray}
to the $n$th space in the ${\rm KO}$-spectrum that is unique up to contractible choice. Given choices $\Lambda\subset \Lambda' \subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ related by a refinement of open covers, there is a unique homotopy between the associated maps~\eqref{eq:KOindexspec}.
<!-- end prop-29 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
The ${\rm Cl}_n$-modules $\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}\to U_\lambda$ determine class $[\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}]\in {\rm KO}^n(U_\lambda)$ for each $\lambda\in {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$. On overlaps $U_\lambda\bigcap U_{\mu}$ for $\lambda<\mu$ there are canonical inclusions
\begin{eqnarray}
g_{\lambda\mu}\colon \mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}\hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}^{<\mu}\label{eq:compatibilitydata}
\end{eqnarray}
and the orthogonal complement to the image of $g_{\lambda\mu}$ has a ${\rm Cl}_{n}\otimes {\rm Cl}_{-1}$-action extending the ${\rm Cl}_n$-action, determined by the invertible odd endomorphisms
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:compatibilitydata2}
e^{\lambda\mu}|_{\mathcal{H}_b^{\nu}}= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu}} {\mathbb{A}}^{[0]}|_{\mathcal{H}_b^{\nu}},\quad \mathcal{H}_b^{\nu}\subset (\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda})^\perp\subset \mathcal{H}^{<\mu}
\end{eqnarray}
that define the action of the generator $e\in {\rm Cl}_{-1}$. The inclusions $g_{\lambda\mu}$ and odd endomorphisms $e^{\lambda\mu}$ satisfy a compatibility property on triple intersections. By Corollary~\ref{eq:cormaptoKO}, we obtain a map to the $n$th space in the ${\rm KO}$-spectrum~\eqref{eq:KOindexspec}.
A refinement of open covers associated with $\Lambda\subset \Lambda'\subset {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$, determines a continuous functor between the associated \v{C}ech categories that after realization is a homotopy equivalence. This leads to a pair of functors~\eqref{eq:cormaptoKO} and restriction of the operators~\eqref{eq:compatibilitydata2} furnish a natural isomorphism between these functors. By \cite[Proposition~2.1]{Segalclassifying}, the resulting maps ${\rm Ind}_\Lambda({\mathbb{A}}),{\rm Ind}_{\Lambda'}({\mathbb{A}})\colon M\to {\rm KO}^{-n}$ are homotopic.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lem-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:anotherdamnhomotopy}
Let ${\mathbb{A}}$ be a self-adjoint Clifford linear superconnection that admits smooth index bundles. The differential forms~\eqref{eq:improperintegral} witness a coboundary in the \v{C}ech--de~Rham complex between~\eqref{eq:appencdR} and the (globally defined) cocycle ${\rm Ch}({\mathbb{A}})$. Hence, 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:superconnindex}
\widehat{{\rm Ind}}_\Lambda({\mathbb{A}})=[\{\mathcal{H}^{<\lambda}\to U_\lambda,\nabla^{<\lambda},\eta_\lambda,g_{\lambda\mu},e^{\lambda\mu}\}]\in \widehat{\rm KO}{}^n(M)
\end{eqnarray}
exacts a differential cocycle from the superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$.
<!-- end lem-35 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
The \v{C}ech--de~Rham coboundary follows from~\eqref{eq:satisfies}. The differential cocycle~\eqref{eq:superconnindex} uses the description of differential ${\rm KO}$-theory from~\cite[\S7]{DBEBis}.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- defn-77: body_md -->
A \emph{spin structure} for a rank $n$ real, oriented, metrized vector bundle $V\to M$ is a ${\rm Spin}(n)$-principal bundle $P_V\to M$ equipped with a double cover $P_V\to {\rm Fr}(V)$ of the oriented frame bundle of $V$ that is equivariant relative to ${\rm Spin}(n)\to {\rm SO}(n)$.
<!-- end defn-77 -->
<!-- defn-78: body_md -->
For $\pi\colon X\to M$ a bundle of Riemannian manifolds for which $T(X/M)$ has a spin structure, the \emph{spinor bundle} is 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:spinorsdefn}\label{eq:familiespsinor}
{\mathbb{S}}_{X/M}=P_{T(X/M)} \times_{{\rm Spin}(n)} {\rm Cl}_{n}.
\end{eqnarray}
The sections of ${\mathbb{S}}_{X/M}$ support an $M$-family of Dirac operators $\slashed{D}$ that graded commute with the left ${\rm Cl}_{-n}={\rm Cl}_n^{\sf{op}}$ action.
<!-- end defn-78 -->
<!-- prop-30: body_md -->
\label{prop:Bismutcutoffs}
Any finite-rank self-adjoint Clifford linear superconnnection admits cutoffs. Self-adjoint Clifford linear superconnections adapted to a family of Clifford linear Dirac operators admit cutoffs.
<!-- end prop-30 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
The finite rank case is~\cite[Theorem~9.7]{BGV}. For superconnections adapted to Dirac operators (without Clifford actions), this follows from~\cite[Proposition~9.10 and Theorem~9.26]{BGV}, see also \cite[\S7.2]{FreedLott}. The straightforward extension of these results to Clifford linear Dirac operators is~\cite[\S8.2-8.3]{DBEBis}.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
